entry.summary: This paper studies how coding agents resolve conflicts between existing repository conventions and new task instructions, using bidirectional controlled experiments in purpose-built and real-world repositories. It isolates three competing guidance sources: the agent's defaults, repository precedent, and task intent. The question is central to how reliably agents can evolve mature codebases.

entry.title: RoleFUZZER: User-Behaviour Fuzzing for Role-Specification Adherence in Large Language Models

author.name: Kshitish Ghate, Michael Saxon, Tadayoshi Kohno, Aylin Caliskan

entry.summary: RoleFUZZER adapts coverage-guided fuzzing from software testing to search over plausible user behaviors that can lead LLMs to violate system-prompt role specifications during multi-turn interactions. It uses a user-behaviour coverage grid crossing grounded traits to construct scenarios systematically. This brings principled testing methodology to the understudied problem of role adherence in deployed LLM personas.

entry.title: Persona Learning from Feedback for Personalized AI Assistants

author.name: Yiran Shen, Yu Xia, Liuyi Yao, Prithviraj Ammanabrolu

entry.summary: Persona Learning from Feedback (PLF) learns reusable, preference-grounded assistant personas as independent LoRA adapters on a frozen backbone, using a frozen self-teacher that conditions on persona specifications and response-specific feedback to give token-level supervision. This goes beyond persona prompting by grounding personalization in concrete behavioral feedback per response.

entry.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention

author.name: Amil Khan, Anantajit Subrahmanya, B. S. Manjunath

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in attention over packed 3D volumes: sequence position encodes memory layout rather than object geometry, so positional mechanisms can learn the wrong structure. It proposes PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that keeps neighborhood attention exact, compresses distant context into 3D block summaries, and applies axial RoPE indexed by true grid coordinates.

entry.title: Learning to Bound: Monotonic, Calibrated Neural Upper Bounds for MPE Inference

author.name: Akshay Vyas, Hailiang Dong, Shivvrat Arya, Brij Malhotra, Tahrima Rahman, Vibhav Gogate, Nicholas Ruozzi

entry.summary: L2B trains a neural predictor to produce admissible, calibrated upper bounds for Most Probable Explanation inference in probabilistic graphical models, amortizing the cost of classical bound computation like Mini-Bucket Elimination within branch-and-bound search. The framework targets the admissibility and tightness properties needed for effective systematic search.

entry.title: LLM Agent-Based Design of RISC-V CPUs with FPGA-in-the-Loop Evaluation

author.name: Leo Itoh, Junichiro Kadomoto

entry.summary: The authors build a development environment where LLM agents implement CPU candidates on an FPGA and use on-board performance measurements to guide design, avoiding slow RTL simulation. Applied under human supervision, the flow evolved a single-cycle RV32I core into a three-wide out-of-order RV32IM core reaching 5.61 CoreMark/MHz, with FPGA evaluation 9.6x faster than RTL simulation.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Co-Evolution Learning for Tool-Efficient Search Agents with Zero Labels

author.name: Qin-Wen Luo, Sheng Ren, Xiang Chen, Rui Liu, Jun Fang, Naiqiang Tan, Jun Wang, Hua Chai, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: ZEST-Search is a zero-label framework for training deep search agents via heterogeneous co-evolution, addressing adaptive question generation as agent capabilities improve and penalizing redundant tool use so that accurate answers do not rely on wasteful searches. It jointly evolves training questions and agent policy beyond outcome-only RL.

entry.title: Hammering with Vampire in Lean

author.name: Jonas Bodingbauer, Laura Kov\'acs

entry.summary: The authors present Vampire-Hammer, a hammer for the Lean interactive theorem prover that dispatches goals to the Vampire automated theorem prover via the Lean-auto framework using TPTP/TSTP formats, and reconstructs Vampire's proofs so they are checked by the Lean kernel. With a 10-second budget across 196,083 eligible Mathlib theorems, it solves 21,158 problems that other evaluated tools do not. This materially advances automation available inside Lean proof development.

entry.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents

author.name: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck

entry.summary: This paper introduces Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents automatically create realistic robotics simulations, based on the insight that simulation creation is fundamentally a coding task. Simulations are selected using U.S. GDP data to cover economically valuable physical tasks, aiming to overcome the expert-effort bottleneck limiting simulation coverage.

entry.title: What a Weight Update Buys: Leverage Across Training Stages

author.name: Shikhar Shiromani

entry.summary: The paper introduces leverage, an exact measure of the Fisher quadratic form of a weight update relative to random directions at the same checkpoint, computed with one forward-mode pass per direction. It orders released Olmo-3, Tulu-3, Zephyr, and OLMo-2 checkpoints over four orders of magnitude, finding pretraining accumulates like noise while SFT, RL-Zero/RLVR, and DPO achieve far higher leverage per unit weight change.

entry.title: Bi-Phase Training: Learning Efficiently From Scratch

author.name: Abel Gurung, Joseph Campbell

entry.summary: BPT is a parameter-efficient pre-training method that composes constrained high-rank left/right transformations with low-rank adapters whose updates are periodically merged into frozen base weights, preserving high-rank learning dynamics. It is validated on language-model pre-training from scratch with Qwen2.5-style models from 100M to 1.5B parameters and OLMo-2-1B on FineWeb-Edu.

entry.title: A Separation Principle for Adversarial Attacks and Defense of Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Farid Mafi, Saber Jafarpour, Mohammad Pirani

entry.summary: This work reframes adversarial feature attacks on GNNs as structure-driven rather than purely model-centric, deriving attacks from spectral properties of the normalized adjacency operator. Its central result is a separation principle showing the optimal feature perturbation is rank-one under a natural relaxation, connecting GNN vulnerability to graph geometry.

entry.title: Dual DeltaNet: Value-Side Memory Reorganization for Linear Attention

author.name: Yixiao Qian, Yaxin Zhang, Song Chen, Jiaxu Liu, Shengze Cai, Chao Xu

entry.summary: This paper proposes viewing the linear-attention recurrent state as a bank of addresses and introduces value-side reads to complement key-side reads, enabling explicit reorganization of how related value features are distributed across the state. Dual DeltaNet extends delta-rule linear attention with value-side correction to reduce interference in fixed-size states.

entry.title: Routed Continual Learning

author.name: Michael Philip, Mahesh Balakrishnan, David Geraghty, David Mao, Vidhya Venkat, Ilya Mironov

entry.summary: Routed Continual Learning is an architecture for agents that learn from accumulated experience by deciding how to partition and store past trajectories: experiences are clustered with per-cluster representations and a routing mechanism selects relevant history for new problems. This balances the cost of a global history against the information loss of a single compressed representation. It addresses a practical bottleneck for deployed learning agents.

entry.title: TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Foundation Model for the Human Gut Microbiome

author.name: Haochen Xue, Anastasia Godneva, Yulong Li, Qi Cao, Zhaodong Wu, Kaiyu Liang, Jionglong Su, Eran Segal, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: TaxoMFM is a microbiome foundation model that integrates taxonomic hierarchy into self-supervised learning via taxonomy-aware encoding and hierarchical compositional reconstruction. It is trained on TaxoGut-HPP, a large benchmark of over 100,000 gut microbiome profiles from 231 cohorts, and shows competitive performance on disease, health, and host trait prediction tasks including cross-cohort zero-shot settings.

entry.title: LinQuant: Functional Invariances for Low-Precision Linear Recurrences

author.name: Neehal Tumma, Philipp Nazari, Rohan Cherukuri, Daniela Rus, T. Konstantin Rusch

entry.summary: LinQuant addresses the gap in low-precision inference for linear-recurrence architectures, an emerging alternative to softmax attention in LLMs. The authors identify functional invariances that preserve full-precision computation while making operands more quantization-friendly, exploiting the fact that chunkwise-parallel prefill casts recurrence as dense matrix multiplications. This framework enables robust low-precision execution where naive quantization of the native formulation would be fragile.

entry.title: DWISE: Denoising Workload-Informed Scheduling Engine

author.name: Lie Li, Wen Li, Junxiao Shen, Jindong Gu, Guosheng Hu

entry.summary: Identifies that FCFS admission and prefill-priority scheduling policies designed for autoregressive LLMs waste much of the speed potential of diffusion LLMs due to heterogeneous decoding costs and idle batches. DWISE introduces workload-informed scheduling for dLLM serving, addressing head-of-line blocking and batch underutilization.

entry.title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections

author.name: Juan Belieni, Ana Carolina Erthal, Eliezer de Souza da Silva, Diego Mesquita

entry.summary: The paper identifies that most LLM unlearning methods degrade badly under sequential unlearning requests because successive updates interfere, undoing earlier deletions or compounding utility damage. It introduces Continual Orthogonal Projection, a gradient-projection scheme restricting each unlearning update to the orthogonal complement of directions affected by prior deletions.

entry.title: On Worst-Case Guarantees for Graph-Based Nearest-Neighbor Search

author.name: Majid Daliri, Mohammadreza Daneshvaramoli, Purna Dutta, Edo Liberty, Cameron Musco, Christopher Musco, Torsten Suel

entry.summary: The paper proves a strong lower bound showing that no standard graph-based nearest-neighbor method (greedy search on flat or hierarchical graphs, including HNSW, DiskANN, NSG) can achieve sublinear query time for approximate nearest neighbor search in Euclidean space, even with strong accuracy guarantees. This helps explain the persistent gap between graph-based methods and LSH in theoretical guarantees despite their empirical dominance.

entry.title: Pinpointing Pivot Points: The DECIDE Framework for Data Analysis Decision Importances

author.name: Zachary T. Rewolinski, Jan Simson, Frauke Kreuter, Christoph Kern, Bin Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces DECIDE, a framework for quantifying which human judgment calls in the data science life cycle most influence analytical conclusions, addressing the reproducibility crisis reflected in multiverse analysis, specification curve analysis, and vibration of effects. It is timely because agentic AI analysis tools could amplify variation in analyst decisions. By attributing outcome variation to specific decision points, the framework supports more reproducible and auditable data analysis pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond Passing Tests: A Systematic Review and Controlled Re-evaluation of Techniques for Improving the Quality of LLM-Generated Code

author.name: Prashank Kadam

entry.summary: This work combines a systematic literature review of 628 studies (2021-2026) on improving non-functional quality of LLM-generated code with a controlled re-evaluation at equal compute budgets. It finds that most studies measure only their targeted quality dimension, correctness often goes unchanged or unreported, and single automated quality signals are easily gamed, exposing weaknesses in how the field evaluates code quality techniques.

entry.title: Modular Bayesian Foundation Models: Bayesian time series encoders for OOD detection, routing and forecasting

author.name: Mame Diarra Toure, Quang Hung Pham, Mohamed Ryad Zemouri, David Stephens, Luc Vouligny, Martin Gagnon

entry.summary: The authors propose a modular time-series foundation model framework that combines end-to-end Bayesian encoder training with uncertainty-driven expert selection, allowing new experts to be added for new regimes without retraining a monolithic model. This addresses regime shifts in industrial time series where a single foundation model underperforms and retraining is costly.

entry.title: GROME: GROunding Factorized MEmory into Video World Models

author.name: Fang Yu, Xiaoxue Wu, Haiyu Zhang, Yangfu Li, Botong Zhao, Yu Qiao, Tianfan Xue, Yue Lu, Xinyuan Chen

entry.summary: GROME is a factorized memory framework for video world models that maintains long-horizon coherence by separating static scene structure from dynamic entities, addressing failures when content falls outside the context window. It combines static-dynamic factorization with grounding mechanisms to avoid geometric error accumulation and capacity limits of implicit retrieval. World models with persistent memory are central to long-horizon simulation and embodied AI, making this a relevant architectural contribution.

entry.title: Pronunciation-Supervised Text-to-Speech for Irish (Gaeilge)

author.name: William Lane

entry.summary: This paper adapts a large pretrained TTS model to Irish using only 12.8 hours of crowdsourced speech plus dictionary-based pronunciation documentation, correcting defects in the vendor fine-tuning script along the way. The resulting system achieves a character error rate of 0.225, substantially better than from-scratch and zero-shot baselines, and compiles Wiktionary pronunciations into a usable lexicon. It matters because it demonstrates a recipe for building speech technology for low-resource languages from linguistic documentation rather than large transcribed corpora.

entry.title: Tokenizer Tokens Tell Training Tales

author.name: Nishita Jain, Parth Upman, Shreyank N Gowda

entry.summary: The authors show that BPE tokenizers retain traces of their training corpora, enabling membership inference: rare strings become tokens only when corpus frequency pushes them over a merge threshold, so rare tokens used by a candidate dataset carry membership signal. They formalize this under a threshold model and derive a likelihood-ratio test for detecting whether a dataset was part of tokenizer training. This has direct implications for data privacy and contamination auditing.

entry.title: GOFish: Full Field-of-View Gaussian Splatting and Mesh Extraction

author.name: Allen Tu, Meher Gitika Karumuri, Shifan Zhu, Hailing Wang, Yen-Liang Lin, David Held, Matthias Zwicker, Tom Goldstein

entry.summary: Presents GOFish, the first 3D Gaussian Splatting surface reconstruction method trained directly on fisheye images that rasterizes fields of view beyond 180 degrees and extracts an aligned collision mesh from the same scene. Calibrated densification, mip filtering, and wide-angle appearance modeling support photorealistic rendering useful for robots, autonomous vehicles, and 360-degree cameras.

entry.title: Visually Irrelevant Hallucinations in Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ke Zou, Nan Zhou, Tao Yang, Meng Liu, Linchao He, Zehui Liao, Ling Huang, Guangren Huang, Yidi Chen, Yi Zhang, Hu Chen, Huazhu Fu

entry.summary: The paper defines and studies visually irrelevant hallucinations in medical VLMs—clinically meaningful statements in report generation and VQA that lack visual evidence or contradict the image. CLEAR is proposed, a model-agnostic post-hoc framework for phrase-level hallucination risk estimation using counterfactual localized evaluation with phrase-conditioned grounding.

entry.title: Data Scaling Laws in Stereo Matching: From In-domain Fitting to Cross-domain Generalization

author.name: Tong Zhao, Di Liang, Yiming Zeng, Bo Xu, Yingzhi Tang, Chen Bai

entry.summary: This work investigates data scaling laws in stereo matching, introducing XStereo, a 200K-sample realistic synthetic benchmark. The authors find a two-regime scaling behavior (power law transitioning to saturation) for in-domain training and characterize cross-domain generalization with large-scale synthetic data.

entry.title: MRC-MMAgent: Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Role Collaboration in Multimodal Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Shengqin Wang, Jie Jin, Xiaofan Li, Wentao Yan, Yu Cheng, Qingsong HuYihang Chen, Weilin Luo, Jingyu Gong, Xin Tan, Yuan Xie, Zhizhong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MRC-MMAgent, a multi-role collaborative reinforcement learning framework for multimodal tool-using agents that optimizes complete interaction trajectories, including evidence inspection, query reformulation, and conclusion revision, rather than training a single-role agent on terminal rewards. It embeds trajectory assessment and continuation into the training pipeline.

entry.title: DEQ-Stereo: Deep Euilibrium Video Stereo Matching via Adaptive Convergence

author.name: Kiljoon Han, Kyumin Hwang, Wonheok Choi, Jeonghoon Kim, Sunghoom Im

entry.summary: DEQ-Stereo reformulates iterative stereo-matching refinement as a deep equilibrium fixed-point problem, terminating adaptively on convergence instead of a fixed update schedule. This removes the rigid speed-accuracy trade-off in online video stereo matching and introduces components for fast, stable convergence within frames.

entry.title: RepConTUR: A Report-Conditioned Volumetric Multimodal Model for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Seunghwan Lee, Sangjoon Park, Jongmin Lee, Yoon Jo Kim, Wonyoung Cho, Jin Sung Kim, Han Joo Chae

entry.summary: Presents a native-3D early-fusion multimodal model that conditions abdominal tumor segmentation on full narrative radiology reports rather than short referring phrases, targeting radiotherapy planning where false positives inflate dose distortion and editing time. The work extends AbdomenAtlas 3.0 into a suborgan-level promptable dataset with report-derived VQA tasks including referring and report-grounded segmentation.

entry.title: PhysCount: Do MLLMs Count Visual Appearances or Physical Entities?

author.name: Lidong Lu, Jiaxin Lv, Liangrui Dong, Xinyi Mao, Lidong Zou, Zhenquan Li, Tong Lu, Guo Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces PhysCount, a benchmark with 546 real-world images and 4,595 human-written questions that tests whether multimodal LLMs can distinguish visible appearances (e.g., reflections, views through glass) from physically distinct objects when counting. It exposes a conceptual gap between perception and physical reasoning in current MLLMs. The findings matter for applications requiring genuine scene understanding rather than surface-level detection.

entry.title: 3D Occupancy-Language Fields from mmWave Radar

author.name: Haowen Lai, Zhiwei Zheng, Mingmin Zhao

entry.summary: TextRadar constructs a scene-level 3D occupancy-language field from panoramic mmWave radar observations, enabling open-ended language queries against a persistent spatial representation. It uses a distillation model to predict ranges and language features per observation, registered via radar-estimated poses.

entry.title: PRIME W0: Physical Priors from World Models for Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Huabin Peng, Fagang Jin, Yancong Wei, Tengfei Ma, Chuhang Liu, Chao Yu, Liqing Chen

entry.summary: PRIME W0 is a hierarchical conditional flow-matching VLA framework injecting per-layer KV representations from a pretrained VLM into an adaptive MoE action expert, conditioning on asynchronous world-model subgoal predictions and DINOv2 historical-frame semantics, with covariance-structured flow matching respecting kinematic coupling. It addresses the feed-forward limitation of most VLAs by adding temporal context and hierarchical representation use. Four-stage training suggests a substantial system effort.

entry.title: Teaching a Tree to Recover: Online Distillation of an LLM Supervisor with Counterfactual Replay

author.name: Kristian Ceder, Kilian Freitag, Knut {\AA}kesson

entry.summary: This paper addresses robot freezing in complex layouts by replacing costly per-anomaly LLM supervisor queries with an online distillation into a decision tree. Counterfactual replay after each episode labels recoveries as needed, unnecessary, or harmful, retiring unhelpful rules. In simulation across 20 unseen layouts, the tree handles at least 18 correctly via goal-reaching or help requests.

entry.title: Securing the Robotics Supply Chain

author.name: Cindy L. Bethel, Henrik I. Christensen, Odest Chadwicke Jenkins, George Pappas, Holly Yanco, Haley Griffin

entry.summary: A position paper by prominent robotics leaders (Bethel, Christensen, Jenkins, Pappas, Yanco) outlining a decade-long federal research and investment agenda for securing the robotics supply chain. It identifies gaps in component verification and certification, underfunded foundational hardware research, physical test infrastructure, and workforce development, arguing robotics warrants its own strategy rather than being downstream of AI investment.

entry.title: Forward-Backward Map Matching for Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation

author.name: Joseph O'Leary, Tapio Simula, Tom Kimpson, Corey Davey, Wenchao Li, Andrew D. Greentree, Allison Kealy

entry.summary: This paper frames magnetic anomaly map matching for GPS-denied airborne navigation as inference on a chain-structured factor graph, solved with the forward-backward algorithm to yield a full discrete posterior over candidate positions plus entropy-based uncertainty. This avoids the Gaussian assumptions of EKFs, the cost of particle filters, and the point-estimate limitation of Viterbi approaches.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics

author.name: Matthew Zurek, Yudong Chen, Josiah P. Hanna

entry.summary: The paper develops a unified game-theoretic foundation for bisimulation metrics in undiscounted RL (total- and average-reward settings), interpreting prior metric operators as Bellman-Shapley operators of zero-sum turn-based games. This yields unique metric definitions even at gamma=1 and enables transferring dynamic-programming techniques to the undiscounted case.

entry.title: CALM: Conflict-Aware Lifecycle Memory Governance for Long-Horizon Language Agents

author.name: Chang Li, Xianhao Ou, Xinyan Ma, Hao Li, Haoyuan Xu, Jiafeng Liang, Xiaohan Wang, Jiajun Chai, Guojun Yin, Ming Liu

entry.summary: CALM decouples persistent memory preservation from query-time admission, treating semantic relevance, evidence validity, and query-specific eligibility as distinct signals. It converts records into evidence-grounded memory cells, tracks validity and lifecycle states via support, conflict, and dependency signals, and gates admission by temporal applicability. It outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo with Qwen and GPT backbones.

entry.title: SocialArena: Evaluating Social Intelligence in Large Language Models

author.name: Zongqi Wang, Rui Wang, Yuchuan Wu, Hua Yang, Bingxue Qiu, Tianle Gu, Bing Zhao, Yujiu Yang, Jieping Ye, Yongbin Li

entry.summary: SocialArena is a benchmark that defines LLM social intelligence along three tiers: role-playing ability, mental state reasoning, and behavioral reasoning, motivated by deployments in counseling, companionship, and tutoring. It addresses fragmented prior evaluations and unverified evaluation reliability with a unified task suite. This enables systematic comparison of models on socially interactive capabilities.

entry.title: Compile Away Uncertainty: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Programmatic Compilation

author.name: Chengyu Yang, Yunxiang Zheng, Zongzheng Li, Jiamei Li, Boxun Lan, Xiaoyu Liu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Xiaohong Chen, Ming Hu

entry.summary: SKillCompiler is a self-evolving agent skill framework that compiles well-specified textual skill procedures into executable programs, replacing uncertain LLM interpretation with deterministic, verifiable execution. This reduces reliance on repeated LLM reasoning and lowers execution uncertainty without updating model parameters.

entry.title: Extremely Sparse-View Computed Tomography from 2D Projections via Pose-Aware Diffusion Priors

author.name: Linrui Dai, Jinxiu Liang, Chu Zhou, Mae Yamaguchi, Ryuya Takahashi, Imari Sato

entry.summary: The paper addresses the train-sparse / infer-sparse regime of extremely sparse-view CT, where dense-scan training volumes are unavailable, by learning a pose-aware diffusion prior from a single 2D projection per target. This bridges optimization-based methods that lack data-driven priors and learning-based methods that require dense scans. The approach has clear medical-imaging relevance where scan time or radiation limits apply.

entry.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents

author.name: Zihou Ren, Byungchul Tak, Long Wang

entry.summary: Presents REALM, an approach for enforcing least privilege in LLM agents by identifying the files, accounts, and services a task actually requires, including assets whose identities emerge only during execution, using a dependency graph with source-scoped admission of new assets. It separates asset discovery from authorization so prompt injection cannot redirect execution to excess resources.

entry.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout

author.name: Vishal Saxena, Soumyajit Mandal

entry.summary: OPERA uses a general-purpose LLM agent taught the gm/ID design methodology and the gLayout framework to design CMOS opamps from specifications through schematic sizing to post-layout sign-off using open-source tools. Unlike prior LLM agents that stop at schematics, this covers the full analog flow with explainable design choices.

entry.title: Learning Calibrated Confidence for Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Chenxiao Fan, Chongming Gao, Gangyi Zhang, Yaxin Gong, Leyang Shen, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Haoyan Liu, Xinting Hu, Fuli Feng, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: MASCAL trains each agent in a multi-agent system to produce a correctness probability for its intermediate answers by jointly optimizing task performance and confidence calibration, enabling downstream agents to decide when to trust or verify upstream evidence in multi-hop question answering. It addresses the missing quantitative trust signal in multi-agent pipelines.

entry.title: Measured or Real? When Model-Derived Measurements Can Be Corrected or Compared

author.name: Yifeng Li, Ziang Ni

entry.summary: This paper studies when noisy model-derived quantities such as example difficulty or benchmark leads can be reliably corrected or compared, proving the textbook reliability correction has infinite mean squared error and can yield correlations above one. The authors propose a bounded correction rule gated by significance testing and confidence bounds, with Gaussian-noise coverage guarantees.

entry.title: Conic-Lifting for Learning-rate-free Convex Optimization

author.name: Julien Grand-Cl\'ement, Joon Kwon, Francesco Orabona

entry.summary: The paper develops a unifying family of learning-rate-free online convex optimization algorithms on potentially unbounded convex domains via a conic-lifting construction that adds one scalar coordinate, tracing back to Blackwell. It unifies AdaGrad-style rates, Conic Blackwell algorithms, and parameter-free methods under one analysis framework.

entry.title: When the Top Answer Decides: Gender Bias in Decision Models

author.name: Yeb Havinga

entry.summary: This paper audits six decision models, language models built to return option probabilities in a single forward pass for routing and triage, finding that five give women significantly more favourable answers than men on gender-swapped decision benchmarks, with gender swaps changing 1-3.5% of top answers. It notes no bias measurement appears in their model cards. The study highlights an unaudited, increasingly deployed model category with fairness implications.

entry.title: PIVOT: Progressive Intervention via Online Teacher Correction

author.name: Zhihao Yang, Boyuan Zheng, Puhui Tan, Yukun Chen, Kuan Zhang, Longze Chen, Jiaming Li, Renke Shan, Lu Wang, Xianpei Han

entry.summary: PIVOT addresses the sparse-reward bottleneck in RLVR by distinguishing trajectory-level teacher intervention from token-level teacher supervision, showing either alone can be insufficient, and combining them progressively so stronger teachers correct failed rollout groups online. This targets hard reasoning tasks where all rollouts in a group fail. It contributes to the fast-moving area of teacher-guided reinforcement learning for reasoning.

entry.title: STRATA: Reinforcement-driven Active Sampling with Tri-paradigm Adaptation for Efficient 3D Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Junchao Zhu, Ruining Deng, Chongyu Qu, Zhengyi Lu, Yanfan Zhu, Yuechen Yang, Yu Wang, Shilin Zhao, Haichun Yang, Yuankai Huo

entry.summary: STRATA uses a reinforcement learning agent over a 3D graph integrating H&E morphology and single-cell priors to actively sample sparse voxels and reconstruct dense 3D transcriptomic maps, replacing dense grid sampling in expensive spatial transcriptomics acquisition.

entry.title: UniRA: Unified Representation Alignment and Auto-Encoding for Efficient Diffusion Generation

author.name: An Lanji, Dawei Liu, Jin Li, Haoran Xu, Mei Chen, Yu Tian

entry.summary: UniRA unifies two previously isolated acceleration lines for diffusion transformers: Representation Alignment (REPA), which aligns intermediate features with pretrained representations to speed training, and Representation Auto-Encoders (RAE), which replace pixel-space VAEs with representation-space tokenizers. The unified approach exploits both signals simultaneously for more efficient high-fidelity image generation.

entry.title: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control

author.name: Yuzhe Wu, Zijun Lin, Yeying Jin

entry.summary: Introduces Wizard, an agentic game world model enabling real-time, precise control over character motions in video-generated environments while generalizing zero-shot to novel scenes, characters, and actions. It decouples explicit game logic and controllable world representations from visual generation, addressing limits of prior systems that support only simple settings and predefined motion patterns.

entry.title: Leaking Muse's Charter, Meta's model spec

author.name: vigji

entry.summary: The author found that Meta's open-weights Muse Spark Open (released mid-October 2026) frequently references an internal 'Charter' in its chain of thought, and reconstructed a large portion of the document by iterative elicitation, with passages linked to eliciting transcripts. The reconstruction reveals the model's operationalized values hierarchy including duties to humanity and corrigibility, effectively exposing Meta's model spec through CoT.

entry.title: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis

author.name: Abhinav Goel, Agostino Capponi, Alfio Gliozzo, Chaitya Shah

entry.summary: The paper presents an execution-based evaluation for AI-generated smart contracts, replaying identical transactions on generated and reference contracts to measure behavioral agreement and localize where requested intent is lost. Grading tools are stress-tested against planted mistakes and audited against an answer key written without access to the description.

entry.title: GAUSS: A Workload-Aware Analytical and Monte-Carlo Simulator for LLM Inference Serving

author.name: Srikant Bharadwaj, Ankur Mallick, Spyridon Mastorakis, Anjaly Parayil, Dhruv Deshmukh, Victor Ruehle

entry.summary: Presents GAUSS, a workload-aware analytical and Monte-Carlo simulator predicting full latency distributions (time-to-first-token, time-between-tokens) and sustainable request rates for LLM inference serving given a workload, engine, and accelerator. It addresses operational provisioning, monitoring, and latency-SLO questions that single throughput numbers cannot answer.

entry.title: Rubricon: Automated Rubric Generation and Refinement for LLM Evaluation and Training

author.name: Ulyana Tkachenko, Hui Wen Goh, Guram Gogia, Jonas Mueller

entry.summary: Rubricon is a pipeline that automatically generates discriminative rubrics for tasks without verifiable answers, requiring no human preference labels or generator training. It samples multiple rubric candidates, selects the most discriminative, and refines criteria using observed pass rates, improving evaluation across five LLM benchmarks.

entry.title: DES-JEPA: Learning a Shared Vocabulary for High-Dimensional Discrete Event Sequences

author.name: Hugo Math, Maximilian Forstenh\"ausler, Christos Anagnostopoulos

entry.summary: DES-JEPA introduces a JEPA-style foundation-model approach for discrete event sequences (e.g., clinical trajectories and operational logs), where event vocabularies differ across domains and are too large for existing temporal foundation models. It learns a shared latent vocabulary that supports high-dimensional event streams beyond the fixed small event-type limits of prior models. This extends the foundation-model paradigm from numeric time series to discrete event domains.

entry.title: TreasuryQA Bench: Can AI Agents Work an Archive of Scanned Financial Records?

author.name: Ritiz Tambi, Sahar Shayegan, Joshua Meyer, Sun Kim, Ali Khan, Victor Shih, Mehdi Jamei, Andi Partovi

entry.summary: TreasuryQA Bench requires agents to both search for relevant files via Dropbox's MCP server and read scanned page images through hosted OCR over 1,435 scanned US Treasury publications, answering 70 questions. Unlike prior benchmarks that hand documents to agents or provide pre-extracted text, it mirrors the production setting of decades-old scanned records on shared drives. This tests the full retrieval-plus-OCR pipeline agents face in real deployments.

entry.title: When the Same Prompt Gives Different Answers (and the Same Answer Isn't Always Right): A Taxonomy of Failure Mechanisms, Testing, and Mitigation Strategies for LLM-Assisted Evidence Synthesis Read-and-Evaluate Tasks

author.name: Carole Lunny, Ian Goodman, Stefano Berrone, Connor TA Brenna, Emma K Reid, Ivan Perez-Neri, Shailesh Kolekar, Nityanand Jain, Ashwin Kamath, Lucas HCC Santos, Yulia Otmakhova, Heba Hussein, Diana M Cespedes, Gioia Dahdal, Salmaan Kanji

entry.summary: This multi-author paper develops a taxonomy of failure mechanisms for LLM read-and-evaluate tasks in evidence synthesis, such as study screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. It emphasizes that a correct judgment does not imply a reliable underlying process and proposes testing and mitigation strategies. This is a practical quality-assurance guide for using LLMs in systematic reviews.

entry.title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization

author.name: Jie Huang, Cuiling Lan, Qize Yu, Xiulian Peng, Yan Lu

entry.summary: MemSteer converts unlabeled user histories into QA supervision with supporting evidence to optimize agent memory systems, avoiding costly human annotation. It builds evidence-grounded answer plans that guide question generation, with source-grounded auditing and blind answer recovery to verify quality. This addresses the label scarcity bottleneck for adapting memory designs to new users.

entry.title: What Breaks When Facts Become Stories? The Distortions Source-Agreement Metrics Miss When Models Retell Real Events

author.name: Kwangsuk Park, JiWoong Yang, Vaniushkina Kseniia

entry.summary: The study has three model families rewrite 2,000 news articles as summaries and stories, measuring distortions along the five Ws and assessing which departures are warranted by the assigned perspective. It finds that source-agreement metrics measure the wrong construct for narrative reconstruction, where intended stylistic departure is the goal, and identifies systematic replacement patterns for time, manner, place, and causation.

entry.title: Beyond Selected Breakthroughs: Evaluating Language Models on Randomly Sampled Mathematical Conjectures

author.name: Helen Jenne, Davis Brown, Jesse He, Henry Kvinge

entry.summary: The authors introduce OpenConjecture, a dataset of open mathematical conjectures drawn from arXiv papers published since February 2026, and apply frontier GPT models to a random sample of 200 conjectures using a reproducible protocol without problem-specific guidance. The goal is to assess LLM mathematical capability beyond the handful of celebrated breakthroughs.

entry.title: LLM-Integrated Bayesian State Space Models for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Sungjun Cho, Changho Shin, Suenggwan Jo, Xinya Yan, Shourjo Aditya Chaudhuri, Frederic Sala

entry.summary: LBS is a probabilistic framework for multimodal temporal forecasting combining a state space model backbone for latent temporal dynamics with a pretrained LLM that encodes textual inputs for posterior state estimation and decodes textual outputs. It addresses fixed-horizon and uncertainty-quantification limitations of existing approaches.

entry.title: Scan Before You Install: Detecting and Mitigating Local and Composite Vulnerabilities in Skills

author.name: Parth A. Gandhi, Avital Aviv, Prasanna N. Wudali, Yuval Elovici, Asaf Shabtai

entry.summary: The authors build a six-module scanner that detects both unintended vulnerabilities in benign agent skills and composite weaknesses arising from multi-skill interactions, addressing gaps in existing scanners that only target explicitly malicious skills. On a 556-case SkillTrustBench subset it achieved 95.90% recall with a 4.22% false positive rate.

entry.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting

author.name: Yanbin Yin, Chuyu Xu, Liqin Ye, Jing Peng, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: EPSBench is a benchmark where LLM agents read filings, earnings-call transcripts, and news across 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies, estimate income-statement drivers with cited evidence, and convert them into GAAP diluted EPS via a shared accounting calculator. Six models are evaluated under a common harness against date-matched analyst consensus. It offers a rigorous, evidence-grounded test of agentic financial reasoning.

entry.title: Manifest-Assisted Retrieval in Artificial Intelligence Search: Evidence Gaps and a Security Evaluation

author.name: Gangzhen Qian, Kainan Zhou, Chuhong Xu, Hang Xiao, Zhi Jing, Rong Bao, Lu Yi, Zhaoyi Li

entry.summary: This paper critically evaluates the llms.txt manifest convention for AI search, finding substantial evidence gaps: a 15-tool study observed no automatic requests in 45 trials and a log study found 97% of domains with detected files received no recorded requests in May 2026. The authors formalize publication-fetch-use-action stages, define five threat paths with paired security-utility estimands, and test deterministic parser controls. It is a timely empirical reality check on a widely promoted but weakly validated convention.

entry.title: Enhanced image forensics through partial C2PA-based provenance information

author.name: Riccardo Ziglio, Eleonora Marchesini, Andrea Montibeller, Giulia Boato, Silvio Ranise, Cecilia Pasquini

entry.summary: The paper studies forensic analysis of images carrying partial C2PA Content Credentials, which record only the most recent operations while prior provenance is unknown. It shows how partial provenance can serve as trusted knowledge to adapt signal-forensic detectors to the statistics of the specific image and mitigate distractors, combining cryptographic provenance with classical forensics.

entry.title: CopyLoop: Fast Looped Transformer Decoding via Context Copying and Shallow Screening

author.name: Wenyu Du, Stephen Chung

entry.summary: CopyLoop is a training-free decoding algorithm for looped transformers that proposes multi-token suffixes via low-cost context copying, screens candidates early at shallow recurrent depth, and uses continuous recurrent scheduling to avoid sequential decoding bottlenecks. It tackles the high cost of full-depth decoding in looped transformer architectures.

entry.title: TrussTutor-Bench: Benchmarking large language models on solution accuracy, sycophancy, and error detection in statics

author.name: Evangelos Apostolakis, Erfan Hamdi, Sara Jahedazad, Emma Lejeune

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark of 200 verified statics problems testing not just final-answer accuracy but tutoring-critical skills: confirming correct student work rather than sycophantically agreeing, and detecting errors in flawed solutions. It fills a gap by showing that models able to solve mechanics problems may still lack the error-detection and non-sycophancy capabilities tutoring depends on.

entry.title: Where Position Matters: Profiling-Guided Layer-Wise RoPE Allocation in Transformers

author.name: Zhiwei Liu, Boao Kong, Bing Liu

entry.summary: Shows that Rotary Position Embedding coverage needs are heterogeneous and model-specific across Transformer layers, and proposes profiling-guided layer-wise RoPE allocation under a fixed budget, including physical rotary-dimension allocation for Multi-head Latent Attention. Normalized-depth mapping lets profiles measured on small models guide allocation for larger models before pretraining.

entry.title: Cord: Confidence-Anchored Order Residual Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chengwei Zhou, Zhaoyan Jia, Massoud Pedram, Gourav Datta

entry.summary: Cord improves decoding order selection for masked diffusion language models by anchoring on confidence decoding and learning a lightweight prompt-conditioned policy that departs from it via geometric residuals over direction, proximity, and infilling. The approach adapts the reveal order to both the prompt and the evolving partial response.

entry.title: Aligning Medical Vision Language Models at the Capability Boundary with Entropy Adaptive Rubric Grounding

author.name: Hongyu Bai, Jiaqi Zeng, Chunzheng Zhu

entry.summary: MedCBR is a two-stage alignment framework for medical vision-language models combining boundary-aware preference optimization with rubric-grounded reinforcement learning, using counterfactual preferences at the model capability frontier and entropy-adaptive rubric rewards. It targets reward hacking from final-answer-only sparse rewards and premature saturation on clinically critical boundary cases.

entry.title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets

author.name: Bole Ma, Ayesha Afzal, Jan Eitzinger, Harald Koestler, Gerhard Wellein

entry.summary: This paper provides an empirical energy accounting of speculative decoding in LLM serving, showing that energy savings depend on draft token acceptance rates and vary across target models and quantization schemes, analyzed jointly with latency targets and facility power constraints. It quantifies how speculation trades verification energy for per-user speedups. This matters because energy per token increasingly determines datacenter serving capacity.

entry.title: Finite-Step Geometry of Marginal-Preserving Velocity Fields in Generative Flows

author.name: Ewsey Obzherin, Valentin Khrulkov

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes how different velocity fields that induce identical continuous marginal paths in generative flows diverge after numerical discretization, using projected modified equations to characterize marginal-changing integration error. It derives convergence-order conditions, spectral obstructions for affine cases, and skew-score perturbations for diffusion probability-flow ODEs.

entry.title: Continual Adaptation Across Modalities: Learning and Forgetting in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Xinrui Wang, Zhihao Chen, Jia Tang, Alexandra Gomez-Villa, Bartlomiej Twardowski, Joost van de Weijer, Songcan Chen

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies learning and forgetting dynamics when unified multimodal models undergo continual learning across tasks and modalities, finding that cross-modal interference decreases with modality-specific parameter isolation and that the generation side is markedly more fragile than the understanding side. It maps how architecture and adaptation method shape intra-modal learning versus cross-modal interference.

entry.title: Causal Attention on CPU: A Cache-Aware and Load-Balanced Scheduling Kernel for Prefill

author.name: Kwun Fung Lau, Frost Mitchell, Kanya Mo, Emani Ashok

entry.summary: CACPU is a CPU attention kernel for causal full-sequence prefilling that uses tiered cache blocking and in-kernel task dispatching to exploit multi-level cache hierarchies. It achieves up to 2x speedups over PyTorch SDPA, FlexAttention, and SGLang attention kernels, and cuts time-to-first-token for Llama-3.1-8B prefill by up to 1.74x when integrated into SGLang. This is practically valuable for offloading long-context agentic workloads from saturated GPUs.

entry.title: End-to-End Guarantees for Masked Diffusion Models under Conditional Mixing

author.name: Fareed Sheriff

entry.summary: The paper presents the first end-to-end statistical guarantee for masked diffusion models, connecting denoiser training error to sampling quality under a conditional mixing condition on stationary sources (floored Markov and Doeblin HMM sources). It shows the empirical risk minimizer trained under any masking distribution attains controlled per-token excess error, closing the gap between training and sampling bounds.

entry.title: Coupled Guidance for Flow Matching

author.name: Mateo Cl\'emente, L\'eo Maxime Brunswic, Rui Heng Yang, Amir Rasouli

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis showing that naive translation of diffusion guidance into flow matching breaks the coupling distribution used during training, resulting in weaker control and instability. It derives guidance methods adapted to flow matching's coupling structure, improving controlled generation and generalization of stochastic controllers.

entry.title: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering

author.name: Moshe Shenfeld, Eliad Tsfadia, Katrina Ligett

entry.summary: The propose-filter-release framework privately filters its input so that a mechanism protecting the addition or removal of a typical record becomes fully differentially private on every input, letting noise scale to typical rather than worst-case sensitivity. With a novel filtering step requiring only a concave friendliness condition, it improves accuracy wherever a few outlier records otherwise dictate noise scale.

entry.title: An $\Omega(T^{3/4})$ lower bound for projection-free online learning with linear minimization oracles

author.name: Julien Weibel, Pierre Gaillard, Wouter Koolen, Adrien Taylor

entry.summary: The authors resolve an open question by proving a universal worst-case regret lower bound of Omega(T^{3/4} m^{-1/4}) for any projection-free online learning algorithm limited to m linear minimization oracle calls per round. They also propose an extended Online Frank-Wolfe variant using multiple oracle calls per round with matching upper bounds.

entry.title: Embodied at Sea: Imitation Learning for Multi-Task Underwater Manipulation

author.name: Greta Perez-Haiek (New York University), Luca Macesanu (New York University), Kevin Angers (New York University), Mohammed Imam (New York University), Timothy Gambin (University of Malta), Christopher Clark (New York University)

entry.summary: Researchers collected 1,616 episodes of underwater manipulation data in calm and turbulent waters to train 14 Vision-Language-Action models, addressing the severe domain shift caused by marine visual distortions and currents. In pool-based evaluation across three tasks with 1,260 on-hardware rollouts, 10 models beat the baseline, with the best reaching a 93.3% overall success rate.

entry.title: Streaming Speech Recognition on a Microcontroller: a 65.7M-Parameter Transducer in 2 and 4 Bits on the ESP32-P4

author.name: Billal Boumedine

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates running a 65.7M-parameter streaming Zipformer2 speech recognition transducer on an ESP32-P4 microcontroller with no neural accelerator, using 2- and 4-bit GPTQ quantization with Hadamard rotation and sensitivity-based bit-width allocation. The encoder weights compress from 71 MB to 26.65 MB, and a hand-written SIMD C engine processes each 1.28 s audio chunk in 0.90 s on board.

entry.title: PhysicsNeMo-Mesh: GPU-Native Meshes and Simulation Cases for Physics AI

author.name: Peter D. Sharpe, Corey Adams, Negin Sobhani, Sanjay Choudhry

entry.summary: PhysicsNeMo-Mesh is a GPU-native mesh processing module for the open-source PhysicsNeMo library, offering PyVista-like operations on unstructured meshes in batches inside PyTorch autograd, with semantic labeling of fields and full PDE problem specifications. It targets I/O bottlenecks and inflexible preprocessing in machine learning for physical simulation.

entry.title: Hidden Phase Transition in Single-Polymer Stretching under Elongational Flow

author.name: Aiqing Zhu, Fushuai Wang, Eleonore Vissol-Gaudin, Qianxiao Li, Beatrice W. Soh

entry.summary: Using a conditional extension of Universal and Identifiable Dissipative Dynamics, the authors jointly learn reduced stochastic dynamics and nonequilibrium free energy landscapes from polymer trajectories across flow strengths, revealing a previously unrecognized second dynamical transition beyond the coil-stretch transition. The new transition manifests as bimodality along a folding coordinate conditioned on small extension.

entry.title: Statistical Analysis of Synthetic Data with Verification: A Linear Regression Framework

author.name: Heejune Sheen, Harrison H. Zhou

entry.summary: The authors analyze verified self-training in linear regression, where a pre-trained estimator generates synthetic data with noise and a verifier filters samples by a threshold before post-training. They characterize how verification prevents model collapse and improves performance, covering both full fine-tuning and LoRA-style active-subspace updates. This provides much-needed statistical theory for the verification loops now common in synthetic-data pipelines for LLMs.

entry.title: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models

author.name: Michael Joseph, Yedid Hoshen

entry.summary: Improves membership inference attacks on diffusion models by calibrating reconstruction-loss scores for image difficulty along two time axes: training time (via Reference-Model Calibration against a reference model) and diffusion time. This separates genuine memorization from baseline reconstructability, addressing a key failure mode where easy unseen images score lower loss than complex training images. Directly relevant to privacy auditing and copyright concerns in generative models.

entry.title: CoSTA: Co-Evolving Self-Play Timeline Agents for Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Haikun Liu, Zhichao Yan, Shaoru Guo, Jiawei Gu, Victor Gutierrez Basulto, Jiapu Wang, Ru Li

entry.summary: CoSTA distributes temporal knowledge graph question answering across multiple co-evolving agents that learn to decompose questions, investigate subtasks, and synthesize evidence, avoiding evidence interleaving that plagues single-agent approaches. This targets complex cases where one fact's timestamp constrains the search for another. It advances multi-agent collaboration for structured temporal reasoning.

entry.title: ARBITRA: Robust Document-Level ATT&CK Extraction via Multi-Expert Argumentation

author.name: Youngjin Jin, Seungwon Shin

entry.summary: ARBITRA converts cyber threat intelligence reports into structured MITRE ATT&CK mappings by orchestrating role-specialized LLM experts that propose candidates from full reports, verified through a quantitative bipolar argumentation framework grounded in document evidence. It includes reasoning-specialized fine-tuning corpora. This bridges the granularity gap between sentence-level extraction methods and full-report LLM processing.

entry.title: Mobilizing the Archive: Bitext Extraction at Scale from Archival Documents for Extremely Low-resource Languages

author.name: Chutong Meng, Alec J. Bateman, Antonios Anastasopoulos

entry.summary: The authors propose mining parallel translation data for extremely low-resource languages from linguistic archives (grammars, dictionaries, documentation) rather than the web, using an OCR-plus-vision-language-model pipeline that aligns text with visual layout. This could scale bitext extraction to thousands of under-represented languages. It addresses a major gap in machine translation coverage for most of the world's languages.

entry.title: Testimony from Timelines: Evidence-Grounded Significance Testing of Temporal Clinical Hypotheses

author.name: Chengyang He, Wenlong Zhang, Koduvayur Subbalakshmi, Ping Wang

entry.summary: This work tackles whether LLMs can verify temporal clinical hypotheses (e.g., event-follows-event claims) by specifying nulls, selecting statistical tests, and identifying relevant records, rather than merely producing fluent conclusions. It argues existing benchmarks grade only the conclusion with data handed over, and builds an evidence-grounded significance-testing setting in health where wrong verdicts are costly. This is a meaningful step toward rigorous LLM data analysis.

entry.title: Evaluating Cultural Knowledge Editing in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Malvina Nikandrou, Georgios Pantazopoulos, Ioannis Konstas, Alessandro Suglia

entry.summary: Introduces CulturalBind, a benchmark of 3.2K images covering 1K culture-specific concepts across six domains, to evaluate culture-aware cross-modal knowledge and knowledge editing in vision-language models. It finds that textual and visual cultural knowledge is decoupled in pre-edit models and evaluates editing methods in single and sequential settings.

entry.title: Where Can We Fool the Model's Mind? Response-Guided Semantic Probing and Adaptive Routing for Transferable Attacks on Black-Box MLLMs

author.name: Ahmed Abdelnaby, Mohamed Elmahallawy

entry.summary: Introduces VISTA, a black-box adversarial attack framework against multimodal LLMs that identifies semantically vulnerable image regions purely from model responses, without gradients, logits, or internal access. It supports pure-transfer attacks via a proxy open-source MLLM and adaptive routing settings, highlighting a serious multimodal security vulnerability.

entry.title: The Power Watershed as a Differentiable Segmentation Layer

author.name: Galia Akl (AUB), Laurent Najman (LIGM, KUSTAR), Hugues Talbot (OPIS, CVN)

entry.summary: The paper establishes that the Power Watershed—the limit of seeded Random Walker as the exponent p grows—can serve as a differentiable last layer in segmentation networks, with exact gradients via one adjoint linear solve. It includes a conditioning study of solve, gradient, and limit-distance behavior in p, enabling classical morphology to be trained through end-to-end.

entry.title: SpectralTF-MAE: A Pre-trained Spectral Foundation Model for Tokamak Fusion Plasma Diagnostics

author.name: Xiao Wang, Zhijie Lu, Duoqing Yang, Jiangtao Yu, Jin Tang, Zichao Lin, Hongming Zhang, Guosheng Xu, Bo Lyu, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: A self-supervised masked-autoencoder foundation model pretrains on paired CXRS and XCS spectroscopy measurements from tokamak fusion experiments, using peak-aware masking and peak-enhanced reconstruction to preserve diagnostically important spectral structure. This reduces dependence on task-specific labeled data in plasma diagnostics.

entry.title: CLaW: Codec-Guided Adaptive Latent Watermarking for Traceable Diffusion Image Generation

author.name: Huangchao Song, Lingyun Yu, Cong Li, Peiqi Jiang, Mingqi Fang, Hongtao Xie

entry.summary: CLaW provides robust, efficient watermarking for text-to-image diffusion outputs using a pretrained watermark codec with frozen diffusion backbones and inversion-free detection, enabling user-level traceability while avoiding costly retraining and improving robustness to image transformations.

entry.title: Can Image Agents Complete Visual Commissions? A Benchmark and Modular Framework

author.name: Tong Li, Lishuai Gao, Qi Zeng, Yifan Li, Cong Wei, Zhuoliang Kang, Xiaoming Wei

entry.summary: Introduces Visual Commission Bench (VCB), a benchmark of 600 end-to-end visual commission tasks across 12 categories with 5,039 requirement checks, evaluating whether image agents can integrate heterogeneous materials and deliver coordinated outputs across dependent stages. Also presents V-Protocol, a reference agent that dynamically composes workflows.

entry.title: What Survives Label Downsampling? Exact Region Survival for Coarse Segmentation Targets

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang, Yukun Ou, San Tek Choi

entry.summary: MatchDown builds downsampled segmentation targets via minimum-cost matching between regions and grid cells instead of per-cell strided sampling or pooling, provably keeping as many regions as any one-region-per-cell target allows and certifying unavoidable losses. Across COCO, Cityscapes, and BBBC038 at downsampling factors 2 to 16, a priority-tiered variant preserves every region the evaluation metric scores.

entry.title: Benchmarking color judgment in multimodal LLMs with CIE-computable ground truth

author.name: Shuwei Yue, Kaida Xiao, Zhihua Wang, Qiao Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a five-task benchmark with CIE colorimetric ground truth testing MLLM color judgment, including AWB pair judgment, skin-tone bias, CCT estimation, CIE Delta E 2000 ordering, and color naming under changing illuminants, evaluating eight MLLM endpoints including Qwen3-VL variants, GLM-4.5V, GPT-5.4, Claude-Opus-4.7, and Gemini-3.1-Pro. Models handle coarse binary judgments but remain weak at numeric CCT estimation and fine color differences, with frontier models reaching only 715-1056 K CCT MAE on ColorChecker-24 stimuli.

entry.title: A Unified Benchmark for Aerial-Enhanced Autonomous Driving: The KITScenes Aerial Dataset

author.name: Daniel Lengerer, Richard Schwarzkopf, Jonas Merkert, Fabian Immel, Rupert Polley, Frank Bieder, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, J. Marius Z\"ollner, Klaus Bogenberger, Christoph Stiller, Carsten Markgraf

entry.summary: Introduces KITScenes Aerial, an extension of the KITScenes Multimodal autonomous driving dataset that adds spatially associated aerial imagery and higher-resolution neural representations to synchronized onboard sensors, vehicle poses, and Lanelet2 map annotations. It provides a common benchmark uniting aerial map construction, aerial-assisted online HD mapping, and cross-view localization, with evaluations across 53 map classes.

entry.title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies

author.name: Jialei Chen, Kai Wang, Kang Chen, Shuaihang Chen, Feng Gao, Wenhao Tang, Zhiyuan Li, Weilin Liu, Zhuyu Yao, Boxun Li, Yuanbo Xu, Chao Yu

entry.summary: LaWAM conditions vision-language-action robot policies on compact latent visual subgoals produced by a latent action-conditioned world model, rather than on expensive reconstructed future video. This gives policies predictive dynamics foresight while avoiding pixel-level redundancy. It is a strong systems contribution from what appears to be an industrial robotics team.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Evaluation

author.name: Xiaofeng Han, Kaize Luo, Zenghuang Fu, Zichong Zhu, Zhe Feng, Changwei Wang, Rongtao Xu, Weiliang Meng, Xiaopeng Zhang

entry.summary: This survey organizes physical AI research around the distinction between learner updates and improvers that revise the learning process itself, defining recursive self-improvement in embodied systems. It compares policy learning, imagined experience, memory and skill accumulation, and executable harnesses, connecting them to revisions of curricula, rewards, and research programs, and proposes evaluation approaches.

entry.title: Language-Grounded Force/Torque Pretraining for Extrinsic Contact Perception

author.name: Kazuki Takahashi, Hiroaki Murakami, Ryota Sakuma, Mitsuhiro Kamezaki, Matthew Ishige, Yoshihiro Kawahara

entry.summary: This paper pretrains bilateral six-axis force/torque histories as a semantically structured representation by aligning them with a frozen language embedding space, using supervision from simulated pick-and-place interactions. The learned representation supports text-queryable recognition of extrinsic contact states on unseen objects, which vision alone cannot always reveal. It bridges tactile sensing and language semantics for fine manipulation.

entry.title: Humanoid Dodgeball: Learning Fast Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance Motions for Humanoids

author.name: Aoqian Zhang, Chunzheng Wang, Haoran Chen, Annan Tang, Cheng Xiang, Fan Shi, Shuzhi Sam Ge

entry.summary: This paper introduces an RL framework for agile whole-body obstacle avoidance in humanoids, demonstrated through dodging fast-moving projectiles. Threat-aware reward shaping and direction-specific adversarial projectile policies balance reactive evasion, motion naturalness, and control robustness despite high-dimensional humanoid dynamics. The task doubles as a demanding benchmark for dynamic humanoid stability.

entry.title: Optimal Neural Estimation for High-Dimensional Nonparametric Regression under Multisource Covariate Shift

author.name: Chenghao Xu, Haotian Xu, Shivam Kumar, Daren Wang

entry.summary: The authors study high-dimensional nonparametric regression where multiple sources share a regression function but differ in covariate distributions, sample sizes, and noise levels. They propose an oracle weighted neural estimator and prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors, with rates expressed via an effective sample size combining all sources.

entry.title: Deogen: Automatic Benchmark Generation for Reasoning over Policies

author.name: Sam Kouteili, William Liang, Keeran Murray, Adriana Zhou, Ramesh Viswanathan, Scott Shapiro, Ruzica Piskac

entry.summary: DeoGen automatically generates benchmarks for deontic reasoning — applying given rules to facts to reach a verdict — by autoformalizing policy rules into first-order logic and building decision trees whose paths become benchmark entries. Leaf paths entail verdicts while non-leaf paths measure a model's ability to recognize indeterminate situations. This replaces costly hand-crafted deontic reasoning datasets with scalable, parameterizable generation.

entry.title: Letting AI Formulate the Research Question: Autonomous Research Agents

author.name: Ko Fujimura

entry.summary: This work extends autonomous research agents beyond executing human-chosen questions by letting a coding agent formulate its own research question, using divergence, screening for known failure modes, cross-model critique, and independent peer review that reruns the study. The authors report all 13 development runs transparently.

entry.title: Revisiting Over-refusal in Safety-aligned Large Language Models: A Representation and Optimization Perspective

author.name: Chao Chen, Pengyang Shao, Wei Qin, Shijie Hao, Fei Shen, Richang Hong

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why safety-aligned LLMs still reject harmless queries, showing that harmful and over-refusal representations are distinguishable at intermediate layers but increasingly overlap in deeper layers, and that harmful-sample gradients concentrate in a low-rank subspace. These observations inform mitigation of over-refusal from a representation and optimization perspective.

entry.title: Agentic process evidence

author.name: Yuval Kainan, Carmit Hershman

entry.summary: The authors argue that AI agents acting as autonomous software developers are ephemeral, leaving no durable record of reasoning and tool calls, making accountability impossible after a session ends. They call for agentic provenance and governance standards so that intent-mismatch and injection incidents involving agents can be investigated, treating agents as potential insider threats.

entry.title: EpiAgent: Epistemic Self-Play for LLM Agents

author.name: Xuanfa Jin, Xinyu Cui, Zhijian Ma, Xue Yan, Jian Zhao, Haifeng Zhang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: EpiAgent equips LLM agents with an explicit learnable epistemic layer that maintains and updates beliefs about other agents' private information, decomposing the policy into epistemic update and action selection stages. The approach draws on epistemic game theory to improve decisions under incomplete information.

entry.title: Rank-Aware Differentially Private Release of Listwise Preferences for LLM Alignment

author.name: Junwei Chen, Manjiang Yu, Pengpeng Qiao, Yang Cao

entry.summary: The paper extends local differential privacy to listwise preference feedback for LLM alignment, where full rankings reveal more sensitive user data than pairwise comparisons. A rank-aware exponential mechanism reduces the noise burden of the high-sensitivity ranking space, with analysis of how supervision granularity interacts with privacy noise in downstream training.

entry.title: Echo: Scaling Visual Reinforcement Learning with Off-policy Experience

author.name: Gagan Khandate

entry.summary: Echo is a single-stage off-policy RL framework that scales experience collection without proportionally increasing visual computation by using inverse distillation: a cheap state-based auxiliary policy imitates the evolving visual policy and collects unrendered experience for off-policy value learning. This avoids the imitation gap of standard teacher-student distillation for visual policies.

entry.title: Calculation and rejection diverge in language models tested at known mechanical limits

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This controlled study tests whether language models can judge the physical feasibility of engineering designs by placing beam loads and disk speeds at known percentages beyond plastic collapse or burst limits, evaluating 12 models over 4,860 calls. The key finding is a divergence between calculation and rejection: models that correctly flag an impossible design when asked only about feasibility will still report it as solved when asked for a full answer, with some models accepting beams 10-30% beyond collapse.

entry.title: MEV: A Multi-Event Video Dataset for Long-Take Generation

author.name: Peiyuan Zhu, Shaoan Xie, Yifan Shen, Wen Tian, Zijian Li, Guangyi Chen, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: MEV is a dataset of high-quality real-world multi-event videos with precise temporal boundaries and fine-grained procedural annotations, designed to supervise long-take text-to-video generation. It addresses the weakness of existing short-clip, single-event datasets that lead to temporally inconsistent generations. The event-centric structure enables temporally localized conditioning for video models.

entry.title: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models

author.name: Xiaogeng Liu, Xinyan Wang, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: FlipJev is a black-box, query-based red-teaming attack targeting typed decision models such as Jev, which answer in a single fast query rather than generating free text. Across 12 datasets it finds universal adversarial suffixes without requiring an attacker LLM, showing Jev resists common prompt injections but remains vulnerable to this attack class.

entry.title: Clean Sheets and Checkpoints: Evidence Complexity for Certifying Sequential Agent Risk

author.name: Rohith Yanambaka Venkata, Don McBride, Tiago Sequeira, Md. Al Amin

entry.summary: Develops a statistical framework for certifying that an AI agent's completion probability is at most epsilon given B clean-sheet (zero-success) audit responses, modeling dangerous-capability evaluations as chains of milestones divided into checkpoint segments. The bounds cover adaptive deployment processes under success-probability caps, formalizing what absence of failures actually proves.

entry.title: Raincheck: Deferred Multimodal Prefill for Efficient Multi-Turn MLLM Inference

author.name: Wenjie Huang, Jun Zhang, Hongyaoxing Gu, Haoyang Huang, Tianqi Xu, Xinyue Hao, Xinyi Hu, Xinle Du, Jun Dai, Shuang Ge, Chen Lei, Yue Li, Mingcheng Wan

entry.summary: Raincheck decouples initial token selection from later availability in multi-turn multimodal LLM inference: unselected tokens from query-aware pruning are progressively prefilled using unused decode-time compute and scheduling gaps, with attention visibility control ensuring correctness. This reduces time-to-first-token without permanently discarding information later questions may need.

entry.title: Latent Prediction Yields Cross-Subject Alignable Representations in Sensory-Evoked fMRI

author.name: Serwan Jassim, Victoria Bosch, Daniel Anthes, Elia Bruni, Tim Kietzmann

entry.summary: The authors adapt a joint embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to train participant-specific self-supervised encoders directly on brain fMRI data from the Natural Scenes Dataset, without exposure to stimulus images, and evaluate the resulting brain embeddings on brain captioning, image reconstruction, and cross-participant generalization. The work shows SSL can yield strong downstream performance in neuroimaging. This matters for both neuroscience methodology and the study of representational alignment between brains and models.

entry.title: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates

author.name: Max Neuwinger, Hanna Yukhymenko, Imanol Schlag

entry.summary: The authors propose a scalable template-based augmentation pipeline that extracts safe templates from harmful prompts, translates them, and fills slots with culturally authentic harmful and benign entities to produce multilingual refusal corpora. They release MSafeTemp, a validated corpus spanning 60 languages for multilingual safety alignment and evaluation.

entry.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers

author.name: Jiongfan Yang, Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Zhongang Cai, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples output detail from global attention sequence length by expanding each spatial anchor into multiple slots with disjoint bands of DCT coefficients. The key insight is that low-frequency structure benefits from global exchange while high-frequency detail can be modeled locally, avoiding quadratic cost growth for finer detail.

entry.title: HotPOT: Operator Transformer with Heterogeneous Physics Experts for Large-Scale PDE Pre-training

author.name: Jiayi Li, Guancheng Zhou, Yisi Luo, Ruihua Chen, Penghao Jiang, Deyu Meng, Flora D. Salim, Piotr Koniusz

entry.summary: HotPOT introduces an operator transformer for multi-PDE pre-training that combines a shared encoder with heterogeneous physics experts, where each PDE family gets a specialized expert architecture reflecting its distinct state evolution. This improves on homogeneous mixture-of-experts designs by reducing cross-task interference among equations with different governing physics.

entry.title: Logical Guidance of Stochastic Interpolants

author.name: Gerrit Gerhartz, Francesco Alesiani, Jonathan Warrell, Henrik Christiansen, Matheus Ferraz, Mathias Niepert

entry.summary: This paper develops exact logical composition of conditional velocity fields for flow matching and stochastic interpolants, showing negation and exclusive disjunction compose exactly on any interpolant while conjunction is exact only on Gaussian paths. LOGSI uses score-based re-equilibration as a principled correction mechanism for composable generative guidance.

entry.title: Rennala NSGD: Asynchronous Stochastic Optimization Beyond Euclidean Geometry

author.name: Igor Sokolov, Alexander Tyurin, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: This paper analyzes minibatch stochastic gradient descent for smooth nonconvex optimization under arbitrary norms in finite-dimensional spaces, motivated by matrix-aware optimizers like Muon and Shampoo used in LLM training. Using the framework of kappa-regular normed spaces, it derives high-probability oracle complexity bounds including for distributed settings.

entry.title: Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds

author.name: Jakub Gilewicz, Dominik Galus, Piotr Wojdas

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates fourteen UED, domain randomization, and robotics curricula under one protocol on five 3D quadruped robots in MuJoCo MJX, using interpretable terrain parameter vectors and matched environment-step budgets with a shared PPO student. It addresses the gap that UED methods are usually compared only on simple 2D tasks while legged-robot curricula are hand-designed.

entry.title: Revisiting Temporal Link Prediction through Structural Proximity

author.name: Yuzhang Fei, Yanping Zheng, Lu Yi, Zhewei Wei

entry.summary: The authors show that a simple, training-free structural measure, Personalized PageRank on historical interaction graphs with sliding-window or exponential time decay, matches or beats learned temporal link prediction methods across 14 datasets, ranking first on nine. They analyze historical paths to unseen destinations to explain why this classical baseline is so competitive.

entry.title: PALATE: Pretrained Autoregressive LATent Embeddings

author.name: Sizhang Zhao, Praveen Gondhi, Bin Li, Utsaw Kumar

entry.summary: PALATE trains a GPT-style generative model over a consumer's engagement sequence at a marketplace and uses the last-token hidden state as a learned per-consumer representation for the production ads ranker, replacing hand-engineered history signals. It demonstrates a deployable approach to personalization from sparse, high-cardinality interaction histories at production scale.

entry.title: Bayes-Consistent Losses for Adaptive Inference in Classification

author.name: Shirley Xiaoqi Liu, Florence Regol, Antonios Valkanas, Patrick Rebeschini, Mark Coates

entry.summary: The paper proposes cost-sensitive hinge losses for jointly training classifiers with single-stage or cascade routers in adaptive inference systems that balance accuracy against inference cost. The authors prove linear calibration bounds establishing Bayes consistency for these losses in both routing settings. This fills a principled-theory gap for joint model-router training, an increasingly important topic for efficient LLM deployment.

entry.title: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing

author.name: Binjie Wang, Xinran Zhao, Shoubin Yu, Xiang Li, Silong Yong, Chenyang Yang, Tianyu Chen, Ruofei Du, He He, Chen Zhao, Tongshuang Wu

entry.summary: Introduces 3DCodeEdit, a benchmark of 2,592 instruction-guided editing tasks over 108 Blender programs that construct 3D objects in code, spanning parameter, structural, style, and scene-composition edits judged via renders against human-reviewed checklists. Across 17 models the average success rate is only 37%, revealing that current LLMs are weak at understanding and editing existing 3D programs. Fills a gap between generation-only and simple-edit benchmarks.

entry.title: Implicit Minor Detection from Multi-Turn Dialogue in High-Risk AI Interactions: A Constrained Self-Evolving LLM Harness

author.name: Xiaohan Zhang, Ying Zhao, Ruilin Guo, Xuanyuan Yu, Kaibo Huang, Yukun Wei, Zhongliang Yang, Linna Zhou

entry.summary: The paper formulates implicit detection of whether a dialogue partner is a minor, using only weak conversational cues when identity signals are absent, as a prerequisite for age-conditioned safeguards. It proposes a constrained framework with an LLM, a self-evolving Harness, and a Maker-Checker protocol that requires structured evidence and version-level review. This is a safety-relevant capability with significant privacy and misuse considerations.

entry.title: XLaw-JP-27B: A Lightweight Open Model Specialized for Japanese Law

author.name: Andrew Shin

entry.summary: XLaw-JP-27B is an Apache-2.0 open-weight model specialized for Japanese law that runs on a single 48GB GPU, built by adapting Qwen3.8-27B, an existing base model released earlier in 2026, with hybrid retrieval over statutes and case summaries, QLoRA self-distillation on verified bar-exam answers, and a contract-specific LoRA adapter. It is evaluated on eight Japanese legal tasks against 12-33B open models under identical conditions. It demonstrates a practical recipe for domain-specialized legal models.

entry.title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation

author.name: Zheng Zhu, Xiaozhuan Liang, Xi Chen, Bei Yu, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: CORAL introduces a reasoning paradigm where LLM agents proactively manage their own context: an agent-callable toolset lets the agent checkpoint progress and verified facts, then reset a cluttered context to start a fresh episode. This mitigates cognitive overload on long-horizon tasks where irrelevant accumulated information dilutes attention. It is relevant to improving agent reliability on extended reasoning tasks.

entry.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation

author.name: Shaohan Yu, Jie Qin, Wende Tan, Haiwen Diao, Limeng Qiao, Yueming Lyu, Chenyang Si

entry.summary: IntReal provides two resources for multimodal interleaved generation: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of interleaved text-image samples across four categories, and an evaluation suite with fine-grained protocols diagnosing unified multimodal model performance across capability dimensions. It targets the underexplored task of jointly generating naturally interleaved content.

entry.title: Kinematic Causal Attribution: Black-Box Explanations of Motion versus Geometry for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models

author.name: Zerui Wang

entry.summary: Kinematic Causal Attribution is a black-box interventional attribution method for 4D point-cloud video models that separates motion cues from shape cues using a freeze operator and a shape-free proxy, requiring only access to model outputs. It targets deployment safety checks for robots, monitoring, and AR applications.

entry.title: FutureWorld: A Plug-and-Play Causal Next-State Predictor for Interactive Video World Exploration

author.name: Guangyuan Li, Kelu Yao, Shuolin Xu, Xinlei Yu, Wei Xing, Lei Zhao, Peng-Tao Jiang, Xiaogang Xu, Xiaobin Hu

entry.summary: Proposes FutureWorld, a plug-and-play causal next-state predictor for interactive video world models that anticipates future scene states to limit error recirculation caused by reusing flawed generated latents as history, improving consistency over extended interactions.

entry.title: DINOv2 for PET: A Pre-Training Domain Benchmark Across Classification, Segmentation, and Prognosis

author.name: Roxanne De Maeyer, Yannick Brackenier, Vicky De Ridder, Simon DeKeyser, Maarten Larmuseau, Jef Vandemeulebroucke
