author.name: Christoph B Rist, Larissa T Triess, Markus Enzweiler, Dariu M Gavrila

entry.summary: Introduces a source-only training scheme for LIDAR semantic segmentation that generalizes to unseen sensors by adding an occupancy-prediction auxiliary objective, aggregating source-domain scans into a simple world model used as supervision. The method does not alter input scans, preserving compatibility with new sensor setups.

entry.title: Operator-Aware Posterior Sampling for Multivariate Weather Downscaling

author.name: Carlo Saccardi, Rudolf Saathof, Geethu Joseph, Justin Dauwels

entry.summary: The paper formulates statistical weather downscaling as a Bayesian inverse problem, using a diffusion prior over high-resolution meteorological fields and incorporating coarse inputs at inference time via a likelihood, which decouples the prior from any specific coarse data source. It tackles two key obstacles: the absence of a fixed coarsening operator when coarse and target fields come from different reanalysis systems, and guidance gradients that vary by orders of magnitude across variables, proposing operator-aware posterior sampling to handle both.

entry.title: FlexTry-On: A Time-Efficient Framework for Multi-Scenario Virtual Try-on

author.name: Phuong Dam, Quyen Nguyen Duc, Son Hoang Minh, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: FlexTry-On is a unified diffusion-based framework for virtual try-on that handles cloth-to-person, person-to-person, cross-domain, and in-the-wild scenarios with a single conditioning formulation. It uses text-aware condition extraction and a dual-conditioning diffusion transformer to jointly model garment appearance and person identity, replacing scenario-specific pipelines.

entry.title: TokenRepel: Generating Diverse Image Sets Without Compromising Quality

author.name: Qingtao Yu, Zhen Wang, Ning Lai, Boyang Hu, Hongdong Li, Dylan Campbell

entry.summary: TokenRepel is an inference-time method that increases the diversity of image sets generated from the same prompt by repelling feature tokens across samples via negative Riemannian gradient steps on a von Mises-Fisher mixture, paired with a density-preservation mechanism that projects changes onto a half-space aligned with the model score to protect per-image quality.

entry.title: Neural Blind Deconvolution for Image Scanning Microscopy

author.name: Eliot Guez, Nathan Buskulic, Lisa Cuneo, Luca Calatroni, Giuseppe Vicidomini

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free blind Deep Image Prior framework for image scanning microscopy that jointly estimates the specimen and detector-dependent point spread functions, exploiting differences between scanned images to encode aberration information. PSFs are parametrized through detector geometry with shared excitation/emission components and a Gaussian pre-initialization for stability.

entry.title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Rongxing Ding, Hongyu Qu, Kehong Wu, Xudong Wang, Fan Zhang, Xinguang Xiang, Xiangbo Shu

entry.summary: Proposes HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework for vision-language-action models that jointly predicts short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives and uses action-guided world retrieval to filter predicted futures by their relevance to current action requirements. It addresses the problem that prior methods model near- and long-horizon prediction separately and incorporate futures into policies without relevance weighting.

entry.title: RADIOlogy: A Single-Pass Approach to Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Joaqu\'in Figueira, Giacomo D'Amicantonio, Egor Bondarau

entry.summary: RADIOlogy leverages an emerging property of multi-head attention pooling in vision-language models to achieve training-free zero-shot anomaly detection in a single pass, avoiding prompt learning and expensive sliding-window scans. This is particularly relevant for specialized domains like medical imaging where segmentation masks are unavailable. It offers a practical efficiency win over CLIP-based anomaly detection pipelines.

entry.title: CAPTURER: A Dexterous Aerial Manipulator for Dynamic and Precise Grasping across Diverse Environments

author.name: Meng Wang, Jindou Jia, Sicheng Zhou, Zeshuai Chen, Kexin Guo, Xiang Yu, Lei Guo

entry.summary: CAPTURER is an aerial manipulator achieving centimeter-level grasping of dynamic targets across varied environments, with onboard perception, drift correction, and compensation for dynamic coupling and disturbances. Most prior aerial grasping work handles static targets in fixed scenarios, so this advances the state of integrated aerial manipulation systems. It demonstrates coordination between flight control and an onboard manipulator under real-world disturbances.

entry.title: socx: GPU-Accelerated Chance-Constrained Stochastic Optimal Control using JAX

author.name: Tanmay Dokania, Yashwanth Kumar Nakka

entry.summary: socx is a JAX-based GPU solver for chance-constrained linear stochastic optimal control that decomposes lifted convex reformulations into parallel LQ-tracking subproblems and Euclidean projections. It reports up to 98x speedup over MOSEK and 2224x over SCS, and scales to horizons where commercial solvers exhaust memory.

entry.title: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure

author.name: Exauc\'e Luweh Adjim Ngarti (AIRSEA), \'Elise Arnaud (AIRSEA), L\'eo Nicoletti (Mines Saint-\'Etienne MSE, LIMOS, FAYOL-ENSMSE, FAYOL-ENSMSE), Victor Trappler (Mines Saint-\'Etienne MSE, LIMOS, FAYOL-ENSMSE, FAYOL-ENSMSE), Arthur Vidard (AIRSEA)

entry.summary: This paper constructs a family of localized Bayesian posteriors for physical model calibration by weighting observation likelihoods according to proximity to a target context, using Gaussian localization with covariance inflation to handle context uncertainty. A conditional normalizing flow performs amortized variational inference, demonstrated on an ocean turbulence closure problem.

entry.title: SCOPE: Selective Critical-Step On-Policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qirui Liu, Wei Cao, Yu Mi, Yichen Sun, Xuekun Zhang, Lei Liu, Yue Shen, Zhixuan Chu

entry.summary: SCOPE improves outcome-based RL for long-horizon LLM agents by having the policy analyze its own trajectories, generate step-specific hindsight skills, and distill guidance only at selected error steps. A bounded signed teacher-student coefficient and success-relative length reward stabilize auxiliary updates and prevent off-target distillation.

entry.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Questions: Evaluating LLMs on Underspecified Financial Queries

author.name: Radha Yadav, Prasanna Devadiga, Peeyush Mishra, Apoorv Singh

entry.summary: The paper studies frame collapse, where financial assistants answer an underspecified question with a real number that answers a different question, in the Indian mutual fund domain where correct answers are computable for every reading. Across controlled studies on ambiguous figures, unlabeled alternatives, and missing user facts, models frequently used ambiguous values under the user's label and were sensitive to layout. The work exposes an underexamined failure mode for financial LLM applications.

entry.title: Certified Access: Test-Time Compute on Conservative Physics-Structured AI Memory

author.name: Pratik Jawahar, Riccardo Maggioni, Jonas Petersen, Matteo Cozzi, Gian-Alessandro Lombardi, Marek Gajewski, Camilla Mazzoleni, Federico Martelli

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical and empirical framework for test-time compute mechanisms such as retries and confidence-based escalation on a Hamiltonian latent dynamics memory model. Because the memory advances latent states via damped symplectic integration, every compute-expanding mechanism admits exact phase-volume Jacobians, bounded energy changes, and transport laws. This gives structural guarantees about what extra test-time computation buys and costs.

entry.title: Finding Is Not Returning, Returning Is Not Reconstructing: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Agent Social Re-entry

author.name: Sheng Wan, Cong Ma, Sichen Dong, Qian'Ang Mao, Chenhan Zhang, Daning Hu, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces agent social re-entry as a multi-dimensional evaluation problem for LLM agents in persistent social environments, distinguishing finding a past interaction, deciding to return to it, and reconstructing context for coherent continuation. It shows that remembering an interaction does not imply the ability to re-engage with it autonomously.

entry.title: KARMA: Training-Free Knowledge-Atomic Harness Evolution for Industrial Advertising Agents

author.name: Xinhua Miao, Yuanzhen Rong, Weiru Zhang, Xiaoyi Zeng

entry.summary: KARMA is a training-free framework that evolves six typed knowledge modules of industrial advertising agents while keeping model weights and executable code frozen, using a deterministic trace verifier, critic-guided atomic knowledge edits, and a regression-gated validation mechanism. It enables agents to adapt decision knowledge to changing products, traffic, and policies.

entry.title: Where the Error Lives: Spectral Representations of Learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians

author.name: Fang Sun, Hekai Cheng, Ruoyan Li, Yuanzhou Chen, Wei Wang, Jason Cong, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why small entry-wise errors in machine-learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians do not guarantee accurate eigenvalues and eigenvectors, examining spectral error representations for learned DFT models. It develops spectral diagnostics that go beyond prior wavefunction-alignment approaches for evaluating equivariant Hamiltonian prediction networks.

entry.title: SparseTokenGS: Gaussian-based Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction via Reusable Token Pool

author.name: Zihan Deng, Zhenzhen Gong, Yujie Liu, Jiaxin Gong, Dingkun Liu, Kexian Xie, Yixing Huang, Peng Jin, Tianye Niu, Zhisheng Wang, Fenglin Liu, Hongming Shan, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: SparseTokenGS improves feed-forward Gaussian sparse-view CBCT reconstruction by introducing a reusable token pool so information from the whole scan remains retrievable during coordinate decoding, addressing the scan-inconsistency of methods whose fields are fixed at construction. The work targets low-dose dental and image-guided interventional imaging. It is a solid architectural advance on a known limitation.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Reliability--Safety Bounds and Finite-Alignment Dynamics in AI Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Miao-Miao Yi, Zhen-Yu Cai, Y -M. Du, C. P. Sun

entry.summary: The authors prove a universal, model-independent information-theoretic trade-off inequality between reliability and safety, with a boundary set by a single parameter quantifying a hidden layer's ability to distinguish benign from hazardous inputs. Using a canonical Boltzmann-machine model of AI response behavior, they derive exact reliability-safety relations and characterize how this trade-off evolves through knowledge distillation.

entry.title: Evaluating Visual Realism of AI-Generated Videos with Eye Tracking

author.name: Danqing Shi, Lan Jiang, Jake Lyons, Miri Zilka

entry.summary: This study uses eye tracking as a complementary signal to explicit human judgments for evaluating AI-generated video realism, running two Visual Turing Test experiments with 90 participants across 438 videos from the latest generative models. The results show gaze patterns carry informative signals that align with explicit human feedback while revealing perceptual processes ratings cannot capture.

entry.title: When Does Closed-Loop Curriculum Adaptation Help GRPO? An Analysis on Countdown

author.name: Yuv Raj Pant, Moshiur Rahman Tonmoy, Kaiqun Fu

entry.summary: Introduces CLOSEDLOOPGAUSSIAN, an adaptive curriculum for reinforcement fine-tuning with GRPO that preserves an easy-to-hard Gaussian task structure while adapting to the model's current capability, avoiding uniformly failed or trivially easy rollouts. Evaluated on Countdown, it addresses the sample-inefficiency of fixed curricula in reasoning-model post-training.

entry.title: Generating Critic-Guided Synthetic Experience in Latent World Models

author.name: Jorge de Freitas, Christos Ziakas, Alessandra Russo

entry.summary: Proposes Critic-Guided Synthetic Experience (CGSE), which treats a learned world model as a local transition generator and uses a critic to refine candidate actions from an offline policy, generating synthetic experience that augments offline RL datasets. This aims to mitigate compounding rollout errors that limit policy learning in latent world models.

entry.title: SymKL: A Unified Representation-Space Measure of Signal Degradation

author.name: Dhananjaya Jayasundara, Sudarshan Rajagopalan, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: SymKL is a modality-agnostic full-reference degradation measure: an implicit neural representation is fitted to the pristine reference, its diagonal Fisher information captures local information geometry, and the symmetric KL divergence between sensitivity profiles evaluated at reference and degraded signals defines the score. It applies uniformly across signal types where classical measures are modality-specific.

entry.title: When to spend privacy: optimal allocation in private learning

author.name: Umberto Biccari, Yongcun Song

entry.summary: The paper formulates the Gaussian noise-variance schedule in DP-SGD as an open-loop control problem under zero-concentrated differential privacy, proving that every local minimizer exhausts the certified privacy budget. It introduces Privacy-Budget Adjoint Mirror Descent (PB-AMD), combining adjoint gradients with entropic updates that preserve positivity and budget constraints.

entry.title: Understanding axial attention in TSFMs through single location regression

author.name: Andrei-Tiberiu Pantea, Aymeric Dieuleveut

entry.summary: The authors extend the Single Location Regression framework to 2D structured data to give the first rigorous theoretical analysis of axial attention as used in Time Series Foundation Models, proving Bayes optimality of an analytically tractable axial-attention predictor under specific asymptotic regimes and analyzing training dynamics. This begins to explain why axial attention succeeds empirically in TSFMs. It matters because theoretical grounding for time series foundation model architectures is scarce.

entry.title: Deep learning for non-transvenous ICD screening: tailored neural network architectures, extended experiments, and explainability

author.name: Bartosz Morawski, Samuel J. Ward, Alex Touze, Lin-Thiri Toon, Paul R. Roberts, John Paisey, Alain B. Zemkoho

entry.summary: This paper presents a 24-hour ambulatory ECG screening framework for subcutaneous and extravascular implantable defibrillators, including the first T:R analysis in an EV-ICD cohort and the first full deep-learning evaluation of EV-ICD screening. Tailored architectures with explainability aim to reduce inappropriate shocks caused by oversensing, a mortality-associated complication.

entry.title: MASS: Multi-mask Selective Self-Distillation for Leakage-Resilient Reasoning

author.name: Xiuqi Liu, Oveys Delafrooz Noroozi, Upamanyu Madhow

entry.summary: MASS improves on-policy self-distillation by approximating the marginal over diverse reference realizations using multiple independently masked views of one verified solution, aggregating teacher predictions and selectively transferring reliable token-level corrections. It targets mathematical reasoning and is framed around leakage-resilient supervision where the teacher sees privileged information.

entry.title: NAGO: Noise-Aware Generative Operator via Flow Matching

author.name: Guanyu Chen, Shengze Xu, Pengwei Liu, Xingyu Ren, Pengkai Wang, Antonios Armaou, Tieyong Zeng, Dong Ni

entry.summary: NAGO is a noise-aware generative operator for sampling invariant measures of stochastic PDEs in function space, treating the flow-matching source measure as a design variable instead of a fixed Gaussian. It derives admissibility conditions and a spectral-matching rule for choosing the source, improving sampling across stochastic-field benchmarks.

entry.title: BASILISC: Bayesian Alignment of Siamese-Integrated Latents for Inferring Single-cell Correspondence

author.name: Sepideh Saran, Mahsa Ghanbari, Uwe Ohler

entry.summary: BASILISC is a probabilistic siamese network framework for matching single-cell representations across modalities that outputs uncertainty on the correspondence itself, addressing the missing confidence measures in existing cross-modal single-cell integration models trained on paired multimodal assays. This enables more trustworthy downstream biological interpretation. The work is from a credible computational biology group (MDC Berlin).

entry.title: Going deep, reaching further: What can Boltzmann machines efficiently represent?

author.name: Tobias Reinhart, Gemma De les Coves

entry.summary: The paper proves that depth and higher-order interactions enlarge the set of functions a model can represent efficiently, formalized as efficient reach. It shows deep Boltzmann machines have maximal efficient reach, RBMs are sub-maximal, and k-body RBM generalizations form an intermediate hierarchy, despite all being universal approximators.

entry.title: D-MOD: Diffusion mode estimation for accelerated MRI

author.name: Md Kawsar Ahmed, Mathews Jacob

entry.summary: Introduces a fast algorithm that returns the posterior mode rather than random posterior samples for diffusion-prior MRI reconstruction, using a minorize-maximize scheme on a smoothed log-posterior lower bound with provable objective increase. Each iteration denoises multiple noisy samples and fuses them with measured k-space via conjugate gradient, avoiding costly sample averaging.

entry.title: Numerical Integration on Bounded Domains via Learned Reflected Diffusions

author.name: Kirill Korolev, Artur Goldman, Timofei Gritsaev, Tigran Ramazyan, Nikita Morozov

entry.summary: The authors build learned diffusion samplers for high-dimensional integration over bounded convex domains using reflected dynamics that respect the domain constraint by construction. A reflected diffusion progressively transforms the target toward the uniform distribution on the domain, with a neural score model trained to reverse the process, providing an adaptive proposal where standard QMC and importance sampling struggle.

entry.title: What Does LOL Measure? Hidden Label Shifts in Low-Light Enhancement Benchmarks

author.name: Adityan Thirumani Srinivasan

entry.summary: This audit of the LOL-v1 and LOLv2-Real low-light enhancement benchmarks finds that test labels differ from training labels: LOL-v1 test labels have 1.48x higher saturation than the LOLv2 rendering used in training labels, and the LOLv2-Real test set has other structural idiosyncrasies. With 18 public checkpoints under one metric implementation reproducing published numbers to 0.09 dB, the paper questions what these standard benchmarks actually measure.

entry.title: BEVLight: Generalizable Traffic Signal Control from UAV Bird's-Eye Views

author.name: Maonan Wang, Yuxin Cai, Junming Liu, Zhengyan Huang, Yi Yu, Ding Wang, Yifeng Zhang, Yirong Chen

entry.summary: BEVLight is a visual traffic signal control framework that maps UAV bird's-eye-view observations directly to signal actions, grounding visual features onto lanes and composing them along intersection topology for generalization across intersections and visual domains. It moves beyond fixed roadside cameras that tie existing visual TSC to specific configurations.

entry.title: Latent Path Exploration via Potential-Guided Subtrajectory Balance

author.name: Xiaoling Zeng, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: SubLAT guides stochastic latent reasoning in language models by coupling a relative answer potential with a Subtrajectory Balance objective, borrowed from GFlowNet-style training. The potential scores sampled intermediate latent states against replacements with a terminal correctness signal, steering exploration toward useful reasoning paths without explicit chain-of-thought traces. This targets a frontier question in continuous latent reasoning and efficient test-time computation.

entry.title: ATI-OPD: Adaptive Teacher Intervention for Stable Long-Sequence On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jiannan Guan, Youxin Jiang, Yutai Hou, Qiguang Chen, Yirong Zeng, Haitao Wang, Dengyun Peng, Zheng Yan, Jinhao Liu, Tao Ye, Dandan Tu, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Proposes ATI-OPD to stabilize on-policy distillation for long responses: as the student's prefix departs from teacher reasoning, token-level feedback weakens and updates reinforce deviations. ATI-OPD adaptively revises the earliest high-disagreement tokens in the student's reasoning prefix to restore subsequent teacher guidance, going beyond length control, reweighting, or fixed cutoffs. From a strong NLP group (Che lab).

entry.title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation

author.name: Yifu Luo, Chuang Ma, Zeyu Chen, Enkelejda Kasneci, Qi Chen, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: The paper argues that in on-policy self-distillation for LLM post-training, teacher preference varies token by token within a response, so a single fixed teacher exposure strategy is insufficient. They validate this with a teacher-intervention pilot and propose selecting a preferred teacher per token via a multi-teacher adaptive scheme. This improves the efficiency and quality of self-distillation-based alignment.

entry.title: Intersectional Invariant Learning for Fair Deepfake Detection

author.name: Uzoamaka Ezeakunne, Taiwo Olabamipe, Deevesh Jain, Xiuwen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Intersectional Invariant Learning (IIL), a fairness-aware feature learning framework for deepfake detection that alternates between identifying the hardest demographic partitions and applying invariance constraints, addressing feature-level bias rather than only equalizing outputs. The approach targets large false-positive-rate disparities across demographic groups in detectors that otherwise score high overall accuracy.

entry.title: Knowledge-structured and evidence-aware semantic self-distillation for glomerular pathology foundation model

author.name: Qiming He, Jing Li, Zihan Wang, Tian Guan, Yifei Ma, Zimo Zhao, Yanxia Wang, Hongjing Chen, Yexing Zhang, Yizhi Wang, Xinrui Chen, Xitong Ling, Minxi Ouyang, Yujie Xie, Lianghui Zhu, Yiqing Liu, Qingxia Hou, Shuyan Zhao, Xiaoqin Wang, Lili Ma, Qiang Huang, Zhiyuan Shen, Junru Cheng, Siqi Zeng, Chao He, Yonghong He, Zhe Wang

entry.summary: GloSAGE is a semantic self-distillation framework for glomerular pathology foundation models that uses a pretrained visual teacher's lesion predictions to construct structured pathology descriptions, avoiding costly image-text pair collection. Reliability-guided anchor selection and evidence-guided negative-pair construction handle partially observed lesions while keeping the visual encoder frozen.

entry.title: GradSplat: Gradients Inside the Forward Pass for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jingong Chen, Linlian Jiang, Guangyuan Li, Xinxin Zuo, Yang Wang, Chulwoo Pack, Kyle Gao, Kwanghee Won

entry.summary: GradSplat closes the accuracy gap between feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting predictors and per-scene optimization by applying gradient refinement of photometric loss inside the forward pass, using log-anisotropy corrections and a learned recurrent update applied first to opacity/color and then to Gaussian shape.

entry.title: Edited Endpoints as Partial Goals for Image-to-Video Generation

author.name: Sihyun Kim, Sanghyun Jo, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: This paper identifies temporal artifacts from full-frame endpoint conditioning in image-to-video generation, measuring them with metrics like Hard-Cut and Background Motion Reversal across five video models, and proposes Partial, a selective conditioning scheme constraining only edit-relevant regions estimated from image-editor attention.

entry.title: Calibrating Attention-Based Token Pruning for Efficient Multi-Image Synthesis in UMMs

author.name: Zimeng Wu, Qijian Tian, Penghui Du, Changqian Yu, Jiaxin Chen, Yunhong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CATP, the first training-free context-compression method tailored to generation in unified multimodal models, calibrating discrepancies in attention-based token pruning (insufficient reference exploration, confused conditional guidance, pooling ambiguity) to improve the quality-efficiency trade-off for multi-image synthesis.

entry.title: Cross-Encoder Anchor Refinement for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Kaisong Ji, Ziyang Xu, Chang Bian, Yu Zhou, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: CEAR improves zero-shot anomaly detection by connecting a convolutional encoder pretrained for industrial products with ViT patch features at the anchor stage, building an image-specific memory queried via cross-attention with residual refinement before normal/anomalous prototypes are formed. This combines contextual representations with complementary local evidence to localize subtle defects in unseen categories.

entry.title: LoRe-MIM: Lost-or-Replaced Masked Image Modeling for Self-Supervised Representation Learning in Whole-Body PET/CT

author.name: Amartya Bhattacharya, Bashirul Azam Biswas, Biratal Raj Wagle, Michael S. Leapman, Matthew E. Maeder, James B. Yu, Indrani Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Curates a large heterogeneous multi-tracer, multi-institutional whole-body PET/CT cohort and proposes a lost-or-replaced masked image modeling pretext task for self-supervised learning of cross-modal representations. The approach targets annotation scarcity in clinical PET/CT applications such as disease detection and treatment response assessment.

entry.title: AVPS-360: A Spatial Audio-Visual Benchmark for Instance Segmentation and Tracking of Sound-Producing Persons

author.name: Yifu Sun, Parthasaarathy Sudarsanam, Tuomas Virtanen, Archontis Politis

entry.summary: Introduces AVPS-360, a spatial audio-visual benchmark pairing first-order Ambisonics audio with synchronized 360-degree video across 230 recordings (10.5 hours) and 31,678 manually verified annotations, bridging audio-visual instance segmentation and sound event localization and detection. It addresses the limitation of existing AVIS benchmarks that use monaural audio lacking inter-channel cues for separating concurrent sound sources.

entry.title: Decoding Geometry, Not Tokens: Efficient VLMs for Robot Affordance and Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Akila Ayanthi, Darshana Priyasad, Tharindu Fernando, Dimity Miller, Sridha Sridharan, Clinton Fookes, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: This paper shows that compact 0.5-2B parameter VLMs already encode rich spatial information in intermediate hidden states, and that autoregressive token decoding is the dominant bottleneck for trajectory prediction. The authors propose a lightweight geometric decoder that exposes latent spatial information directly for affordance and trajectory prediction. A practical recipe for efficient robotic VLM usage.

entry.title: Quantize by Doing: Task-Guided Mixed-Precision Quantization of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jiuyi Xu, Xiao Hu, Meida Chen, Song Wang, Yang Ye, Yangming Shi

entry.summary: QbD-VLA is a post-training mixed-precision quantization method for vision-language-action models that allocates weight and activation bit widths using task success from short closed-loop evaluations, explicitly accounting for interactions between quantized components. It targets maintaining task performance at reduced memory footprints where calibration-data-based sensitivity methods fall short.

entry.title: Kinematic-Tactile Aligned Dexterous Retargeting with Contact Wrench Space Alignment

author.name: Xinyuan He, Ziheng Xu, Yueyuan Chen, Yufan Ye, Yuanshuo Tan, Huiming Pan, Jianjun Meng, Shuo Jiang, Peter B. Shull

entry.summary: A hierarchical three-stage framework retargets human demonstrations to dexterous robot hands while preserving tactile information, using object-centric contact wrench space as the physical alignment representation alongside kinematics. Robot fingertip force targets are optimized from human wrench support profiles built from tactile forces and contact geometry. Most retargeting work preserves only kinematics, so this adds a physical-interaction dimension.

entry.title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features

author.name: Huanyan Zhu, Cheng Li

entry.summary: The authors construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator to simultaneously address kernel matrix inversion cost and kernel integral (quadrature) error, including for integrands outside the RKHS. This extends low-rank kernel approximations to control downstream Bayesian quadrature error.

entry.title: Beyond Low-Pass Dynamics: Frequency-Selective Spiking Reservoirs with Resonant Neurons

author.name: Aurora Micheli, Claudio Gallicchio, Nergis Tomen

entry.summary: Proposes HRF-Res, a liquid state machine replacing Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons with heterogeneous Harmonic Resonate-and-Fire neurons that exhibit intrinsic oscillatory, frequency-selective dynamics. This enables spiking reservoirs to distinguish information encoded at different temporal frequencies, improving on the low-pass limitations of LIF-based reservoirs.

entry.title: SciGame: Let Agents Play the Scientific Discovery Games in the Real and Counterfactual World

author.name: Yusheng Zhao, Bowei He, Xue Liu, Mingxiao Li

entry.summary: Introduces SciGame, a controlled benchmark converting scientific literature into structured cards that yield paired Original and dimensionally consistent Counterfactual environments for evaluating LLM scientific discovery. It includes a Historical collection of canonical laws and a Temporal collection from post-cutoff papers, separating pretrained priors from genuine inference.

entry.title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms

author.name: Sikai Cheng, Tinghan Ye, Arnaud Deza, Xiaonan Qi, Miao Li, Litong Liu, Changkun Guan

entry.summary: DecompGym is a benchmark of 81 instances across nine problem families evaluating how well coding agents implement Benders decomposition and column generation solvers, with criteria covering runtime, numerical feasibility, and optimality. It systematically characterizes where current agents fail in building these hard-to-implement optimization algorithms.

entry.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement

author.name: Yu Liu, Youxing Li, Yuedong Tan, Zhiwei Yang, Zihan Su, Hanqi Feng, Shaojie Zhang, Libin Liao, Zihao Wan, Chenxu Wu, Cong Cao, Fangfang Yuan, Yanbing Liu, Ziheng Chen, Pei Fu, Radu Timofte, Zongwei Wu, Nicu Sebe, Barnabas Poczos, Jian Luan

entry.summary: A-RSI studies recursive self-improvement by focusing on when to acquire fresh training experience rather than only what to generate. It monitors reward variation and accuracy in training logs to refresh the task pool when learning signal declines, and keeps supervision independently checkable rather than relying on self-consistency or majority voting. The approach targets zero-data multimodal self-improvement.

entry.title: ATLAS-Bench: An Agentic Tool-Use Benchmark for Local Area Search

author.name: Keyun Zhang, Dapeng Yin, Fanfu Wang, Shuang Lang, Zhenyu Zhu, Yulin Huang, Chong Yang, Pengjie Wang

entry.summary: ATLAS-Bench provides 1,200 queries across three regions, built from real search events with place attributes, reviews, and user profiles, for evaluating agentic local search. Each query separates mandatory requirements from preferences and factual from subjective judgments, with supporting evidence and checking criteria. This gives much finer-grained evaluation of whether search results truly satisfy user needs.

entry.title: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training

author.name: Qiaosheng Chen, Kaijia Huang, Fanqi Zhou, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: AgenticDS is a contract-based agent system for finding training datasets in million-scale repositories, enforcing hard constraints such as task, license, and training stage that plain text retrieval cannot verify, and checking that returned data will actually improve model training. It addresses weaknesses of both text retrieval and unconstrained tool-calling agents.

entry.title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams

author.name: Qinuo Cao, Xin He, Dianxuan Fu, Lizhi Zhang, Zhaoqing Xing, Jiapu Wang, Xin Wang, Na Zou, Yi Chang, Qinggang Zhang

entry.summary: EvoTeam evolves LLM multi-agent systems at the collaboration level, adjusting team organization and inter-agent interactions from collective execution experience across heterogeneous tasks. It addresses limitations of prior approaches that constrain team reorganization within a shared structure and reuse interaction rules across incompatible contexts.

entry.title: Bridging Semantics and Structure: A Theoretically Grounded Framework for Link Prediction on TAGs

author.name: Chen Shao, Ruirui Wang, Tobias Kafer, Danai Koutra

entry.summary: Bridge-LP is a simple, efficient, theoretically grounded framework for link prediction on text-attributed graphs that unifies GNN structural signals with LM semantic signals. It includes three theoretically justified design components, such as jumping connections of textual proximity, to resolve the question of optimal fusion of the two inductive biases.

entry.title: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction

author.name: Haowen Shi, Xuzhe Yan, Fahao Chen, Peng Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that prefill-based LLM decoding length prediction benchmarks conflate predictor quality with task hardness, with accuracy collapsing when the model, dataset, or sampling configuration changes. Treating decoding as a stopped stochastic process with ramping stopping probability, the authors derive bounds that every prefill-side predictor must obey.

entry.title: From Geometry to Behavior: How Instruction Exposure Unlocks Latent Rhetorical Directions in LLMs

author.name: Shengjie Xu

entry.summary: The paper extracts an Analogy Vector from the residual stream via difference-in-means, enabling steerable explanation style across seven instruction-tuned models (Gemma-2, Llama-3.1, Qwen-2.5 at 2B-32B scale). Its central finding across matched base-instruct pairs is that instruction exposure determines whether latent rhetorical capabilities are geometrically accessible and activatable.

entry.title: Merge and Branch: Efficient Tree-Structured Supervised Fine-Tuning of LLMs for Recommendation

author.name: Yunqin Zhu, Yao Xie

entry.summary: Merge and Branch improves supervised fine-tuning for generative recommendation by compressing item histories into few learned tokens and predicting multiple target semantic identifiers per encoded history, organized as a shallow wide tree. The authors develop tree FlashAttention to execute this layout efficiently, addressing the asymmetry between expensive history encoding and single-target supervision.

entry.title: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute

author.name: Jiansheng Wang, Jaskeerat Singh, Haochen Xu, Xinyi Li, Mingyuan Yan, Shaohui Liu, Yuzhuo Li, Yize Chen, Wenqi Cui

entry.summary: LLM-PowerTrace is an open dataset of time-resolved, per-GPU power traces sampled every 100ms during LLM fine-tuning and inference across NVIDIA platforms, paired with contextual metadata. Unlike aggregate energy benchmarks, it captures sub-second power dynamics such as peaks, ramps, and synchronized fluctuations. This supports data-center and grid-level modeling of AI as an electrical load.

entry.title: Aligning Misaligned Benchmarks for Single-View Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Yang-Che Tseng, Erqun Dong, Jeong-gi Kwak, Gopal Sharma, Shakiba Kheradmand, Stephan Garbin, Hossam Isack, Kwang Moo Yi

entry.summary: The authors show that evaluation of single-view novel view synthesis is confounded by how each method's reference frame is aligned to ground-truth poses, with test-time pose optimization landing in arbitrary local optima. They propose an alternative that avoids this ill-posed alignment, enabling fairer standardized comparison. This is an important methodological correction for a rapidly advancing area.

entry.title: When AI performs, what remains? An integrative review of generative AI and cognitive capital in individuals and organizations

author.name: Giuseppe Riva, Stefania La Rocca, Brenda K. Wiederhold, Andrea Gaggioli

entry.summary: This integrative narrative review examines the long-term effects of generative AI on knowledge, skills, and judgment retained in people and organizations, using the construct of cognitive capital. It distinguishes individual and organizational cognitive capital from human-AI joint performance, so that productivity gains can mask depletion of underlying human capabilities.

entry.title: Rethinking GFlowNet Training: Negative Reinforce Dynamics

author.name: Pedro Dall'Antonia, Daniel Csillag, Diego Mesquita

entry.summary: Analyzes GFlowNet training gradients and shows the semi-gradient update conventionally used avoids an anti-exploratory mechanism present in the full gradient, connecting the full gradient to min-min dynamics between the GFlowNet and a decoupled sampler. This theoretical insight clarifies the exploration-correctness coupling at the heart of generative flow network training.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for the Game of Balatro: A Fast Simulator and Two-Policy Training Approach

author.name: Ajay Vikram Periasami, Anjaneya Gupta, Ethan Cheng, Ivan Rosales

entry.summary: Builds an end-to-end RL pipeline for the roguelike deckbuilder Balatro, including a high-throughput Rust simulator diffed against the live game, a condensed masked action interface, and a multi-agent PPO setup splitting play into a tactical blind policy and a strategic shop policy. It tackles a game combining a 3,000-action space, long sparse-reward horizons, and pervasive stochasticity.

entry.title: FDSML: Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning with Parameter-Aware Triplet Loss

author.name: Hina Otake, Shinei Arakawa, Keitaro Tanaka, Yoshihiro Fukuhara, Hirokatsu Kataoka, Shigeo Morishima

entry.summary: FDSML extends formula-driven supervised learning by deriving relational supervision from image-generation parameters rather than discrete labels, combining a refined fractal dataset (FineFractalDB) with a Parameter-Aware Triplet Loss that defines positives and negatives by distance in Iterated Function System parameter space. This enables vision pre-training without real images while respecting continuous parameter structure.

entry.title: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure

author.name: Hicham Hammouchi, Gabriele Lenzini

entry.summary: InferD is a honeypot framework designed specifically for AI serving stacks, inference APIs, vector databases, and agent orchestration gateways that are increasingly exposed on the public internet. It reproduces observable AI-service behavior such as model inventories, token formats, and tool-call protocols while ensuring no real inference or tool execution occurs.

entry.title: HEMO: Harness Self-Evolution for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Jianghan Zhu, Cong Zhang, Ni Zhang, Yifan Yang, Yew Soon Ong, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: HEMO extends LLM-based automatic operator design for multi-objective combinatorial optimization by making the discovery harness itself a self-evolving optimization target. It maintains persistent harness state and updates one module at a time, revising experience retrieval, operator improvement, parent selection, and search orchestration logic.

entry.title: Upcycling Language Models for Multiple Specialized Domains

author.name: Mingzi Cao, Xi Wang, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: The authors propose Domain-Specific upcycling, a model-expansion method that adds experts and a router to dense Transformer layers to adapt one model to multiple specialized domains, avoiding the equal-weighting and always-active-adapter limitations of LoRA-combination approaches while offering higher capacity than low-rank methods. This targets multi-domain adaptation with minimal cross-domain interference. It matters because it offers an efficient alternative path to multi-domain LLM specialization beyond stacked or merged adapters.

entry.title: TaskFrame: Connecting Task-Level Planning with Frame-Level Control for Game Agents

author.name: Guangzhi Wang, Junfu Pu, Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Honghao Chen, Cheng Cheng, Lingen Li, Yinan Zhou, Jiarui Wu, Yinuo Jiang, Hongbo Jin, Xiaodong Cun, Ying Shan

entry.summary: TaskFrame is a hierarchical planner-controller framework for general game agents that couples a vision-language task planner (decomposing goals into atomic instructions optimized with supervised learning and dependency-aware GRPO) with a low-latency frame-level keyboard-and-mouse controller, using cached goal-token hidden-state embeddings for coordination. This separates high-level reasoning from low-latency control to suit their different computational profiles. It matters as a blueprint for interactive agents in fast visual environments.

entry.title: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing

author.name: Xiangyu Xu, Bangshuai Peng, Ziyi Liu, Mengjie Zhao, Chenhao Lu, Zhengyang Fan, Huazhe Xu, Kaizhe Hu

entry.summary: BURGER is a language-conditioned robotic drawing benchmark with a scalable prompt-driven pipeline generating continuous drawing trajectories in simulation and the real world, enabling study of how vision-language-action models generalize as training data scales. It includes 28,200 simulated demonstrations across 282 drawing tasks where instructions permit open-ended valid outputs.

entry.title: Muon Makes the First Mixture-of-Experts Layer Harder to Balance

author.name: Marcos Hernanz

entry.summary: This empirical study measures how the Muon optimizer affects expert-routing bias spans in MoE language models at 55M and 108M active parameters, finding that Muon roughly doubles the balance span of the first MoE layer across seeds. The effect originates from Muon training the rest of the network rather than the router itself, providing actionable insight for MoE training recipes.

entry.title: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Brener Ramos, William R. Wolf, Tarc\'isio C. D. Oliveira, Scott T. M. Dawson

entry.summary: The authors propose reduced-order GNN models that predict only sparse probe measurements and integrated quantities on coarse meshes, bypassing full-state reconstruction for parameterized 2D/3D flows. The approach matches or outperforms finer-mesh surrogates with lower training cost, aided by a dynamics-informed adaptive sampling strategy, even for 3D chaotic dynamics.

entry.title: Data Amount Heterogeneity Improves Performance in Federated Learning for Neuroimaging

author.name: Paul Kurian, Tamoghna Chattopadhyay, Abhijith Shaji, Greg Ver Steeg, Paul M. Thompson, Jose Luis Ambite

entry.summary: This paper finds, counterintuitively, that data amount heterogeneity across sites improves federated learning performance for neuroimaging tasks such as Alzheimer's classification from structural MRI, in a pipeline using homomorphic encryption. The result challenges the standard assumption that heterogeneity is purely detrimental in cross-silo FL.

entry.title: Exponential-Nemytskii Neural Operators: Learning Field Evolution Across Step Sizes

author.name: Jingye Li, Jinglai Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes a neural operator whose step-size dependence follows a first-order Duhamel approximation of semilinear dynamics, combining exact linear propagation with a local nonlinear term, enabling predictions at unobserved step sizes without dense supervision. The authors prove that agreement at two step sizes controls prediction differences across a range, plus identifiability conditions. A principled treatment of variable-step operator learning.

entry.title: Interpretable by Design Tabular Prediction via In-Context Local Linear Learning

author.name: Ran Eisenberg, Steven Berger, Ofir Lindenbaum

entry.summary: TICL3 is an interpretable-by-design predictor that uses tabular foundation models to guide a local linear prediction rule, providing faithful per-instance feature attributions rather than unreliable post-hoc explanations. It leverages in-context learning so predictions require no dataset-specific fine-tuning, with applications such as biomarker identification in biology.

entry.title: H$^2$R: Hierarchical Hint-Based Reward for Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: He Tu, Siye Li, Hongyi Wen

entry.summary: Introduces Hierarchical Hint-based Reward, which uses the intrinsic sub-question structure of math problems as logically grounded intermediate milestones during RLVR training, reducing the effective reasoning horizon. Also releases HiMath, a benchmark of hierarchically structured mathematical problems for evaluating such training.

entry.title: Causal-prior-constrained deep learning for rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones

author.name: Xinrui Li, Yijun Jin, Yifan Dong, Shoujuan Shu

entry.summary: Introduces CausalVisionRI, a deep learning system for 24-hour tropical cyclone rapid intensification warning in the western North Pacific that integrates infrared imagery, atmospheric and oceanic fields, and an observationally discovered causal graph with sign-verified effects. The causal prior, learned from 522 historical cyclones, makes the model's drivers auditable.

entry.title: Nonlinear Dynamical Systems as Scalable and Efficient Physical Neural Networks

author.name: Tyler King, Magnus Saebo, Jeremie Laydevant, Haoting Zhen, Maxwell G. Anderson, Tatsuhiro Onodera, Peter L. McMahon

entry.summary: The paper shows in simulation that applying modern ML training practices, including model compression, substantially closes the accuracy gap between physical neural networks based on nonlinear dynamical systems and conventional digital networks. This supports the viability of such physical systems as energy-efficient ML accelerators.

entry.title: Towards Reliable, Scalable, and Value-Aligned Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising

author.name: Yatong Xiao, Yibo Sheng, Lixiang Wang, Mingjie Sun, Yunhao Sha, Pengfei Zhang, Shengyu Wang, Peng Wang, Wenjin Wu, Peng Jiang

entry.summary: The paper describes improvements to GR4AD, an industrial generative recommendation framework deployed at Kuaishou, addressing three limitations: sensitivity of deterministic semantic-ID assignment, diminishing returns from backbone scaling under serving constraints, and poor credit assignment in sequence-level value optimization. The work advances value-aligned generative retrieval for large-scale advertising.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Doppler-Guided RF Odometry

author.name: Kunzhe Song, Jialuo Du, Jingkai Lin, Huacheng Zeng

entry.summary: RFWalk is a self-supervised, RF-only odometry framework for robot ego-motion estimation in conditions like darkness, smoke, and fog, modeling dense cross-frame correspondences as random walks on a space-time graph learned via temporal cycle consistency. A Doppler consistency loss leveraging measured radial velocity filters out cycle-consistent but physically implausible correspondences, removing the need for inertial sensors or pose supervision.

entry.title: Zero-Complement Extrapolation: Parameter Recovery and Classification in Severely Imbalanced Logistic Regression under Rank-Deficient Regimes

author.name: Chongsun Park

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Self-Calibrated Zero-Complement estimator for binary logistic regression when minority-class samples are fewer than the feature dimension, shifting from minority oversampling to majority-fringe extrapolation, with guarantees grounded in Stein's Lemma. It addresses separation, intercept bias, and SMOTE collapse in severely imbalanced, rank-deficient settings.

entry.title: Satisficing Regret Minimization in Bandits with Knapsacks

author.name: Qing Feng, Tianyi Ma, Ruihao Zhu

entry.summary: This theory paper studies a satisficing variant of bandits with knapsacks where the learner maximizes how often selected policies exceed a reward threshold under budget constraints, introducing an algorithm that handles uncompensatable threshold deficits and random early resource depletion. It establishes performance guarantees measured via cumulative satisficing regret.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Under Runtime Confounding: Policy Learning and Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Raphael Kim, Michele Santacatterina, Ramin Zabih, Keith Barnatchez

entry.summary: The paper studies runtime confounding in RL, where logged data are fully observable but deployment-time decisions lack certain variables, causing bias that propagates across time through sequential decision effects. It develops methods for policy learning and off-policy evaluation in this setting, relevant to healthcare, e-commerce, and robotics deployment. This addresses a real-world gap between training-data observability and deployment-time information constraints.

entry.title: Rimuru: Unified Memory Management for Modern LLM Serving via Elastic Expert Offloading

author.name: Zhiyuan Fang, Dingyang Li, Jianfeng Zhong, Bin Wang, Weixi Zhu, Cunshu Ni, Zicong Hong, Wuhui Chen, Zibin Zheng

entry.summary: Rimuru introduces unified memory management for LLM serving systems, jointly handling model weights (including MoE experts) and attention/KV states rather than provisioning them with fixed boundaries. It enables elastic expert offloading so idle memory can be reallocated between weights and states under varying workloads, improving concurrency and throughput in resource-constrained settings. Efficient serving infrastructure is a key enabler as modern LLM architectures introduce heterogeneous tensor layouts and lifetimes.

entry.title: Human-Residual Steering: Aligning Frozen LLM Judges with Human Judgment Distributions

author.name: Chen Lyu, Phong Do, Gabriele Pergola

entry.summary: Proposes Human-Residual Steering (HRS), the first method to align frozen LLM judges with the full distribution of human judgments via learned low-rank hidden-state interventions, rather than output calibration or fine-tuning. An oracle analysis shows single-layer low-rank corrections remove most judge-human distribution discrepancy, and HRS learns to predict these corrections. Useful for LLM-as-a-judge applications requiring annotator-level variation modeling.

entry.title: A Low-Rank Space Captures Linear Alignment Between LLM and Human Neural Activity During Naturalistic Language Listening

author.name: Zach Paris, Emily Finn

entry.summary: Using ridge reduced-rank regression across intracranial and fMRI listening datasets, the authors find that 1-3% of an LLM's embedding dimensions suffice to recover full linear encoding of human neural responses. Identifying this brain-predictive subspace clarifies which representational directions drive LLM-brain alignment. This advances the use of LLMs as models of human language processing.

entry.title: Convex Potential Learning for Optimal Transport Between Medical Images

author.name: Hongyu Kan, Ivan Medri, Natasha Ironside, Kristofor Pas, Richard Corp, Shinjini Kundu, Gustavo Kunde Rohde

entry.summary: Proposes estimating optimal transport maps between medical images by parameterizing the convex potential function, guaranteeing by construction a curl-free map consistent with Brenier's theorem. The method scales to large 3D medical images and achieves lower transport errors and higher-quality maps than existing regularized approaches on 2D and 3D datasets.

entry.title: StepControl: Long-Horizon Human Motion Generation from Foot-Contact Schedules

author.name: Hojun Jang, Jinseok Bae, Donggeun Lim, Taesun Kim, Seungbin Jeong, Younghwan Lee, Yong Seok Kim, Young Min Kim

entry.summary: Presents StepControl, an autoregressive diffusion model for controllable human motion generation conditioned on a binary left/right foot-contact schedule, without requiring target poses or semantic prompts. Contact events are injected via cross-attention with classifier-free guidance, plus a stochastic mixture noise schedule and warmup for stable long-horizon generation.

entry.title: ETA-Motion: Efficient Topology-Agnostic Motion Diffusion via Sparse Joint Learning

author.name: Seoyoung Hwang, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: ETA-Motion is a diffusion framework for generating character motion across arbitrary skeletons, replacing dense full-joint modeling with sparse joint learning on a compact subset of joints. This reduces computation and improves transfer of motion patterns across diverse skeletal topologies with inconsistent joint semantics.

entry.title: What do MLLMs know about 'Waldo'? Evaluating Visual Reasoning under Multi-Instance Multi-Object Challenges

author.name: Saumya Mundra, Ajoy Mondal, Vineeth N Balasubramanian, C. V. Jawahar

entry.summary: MIMO-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs in settings where object categories contain multiple visually similar instances, requiring referring expressions composed of multiple visual subtasks to uniquely identify targets. The benchmark exposes limits of MLLM visual reasoning under realistic ambiguity.

entry.title: COGS: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Attribute-Aware Object-Level 3D Gaussian Splatting Perception

author.name: Zheng Xiao, Yifan Liu, Weijian Deng, Jiashu Li, Ziqin Liu, Zhenjun Han, Jianbin Jiao

entry.summary: COGS provides a 15,675-object, 40-category 3DGS dataset with artifact filtering and appearance variation, plus a benchmark for object classification and Gaussian-attribute-usage diagnosis to clarify how 3D architectures exploit heterogeneous Gaussian attributes during perception.

entry.title: ACD-GS: Asymmetric Curvature-aware Densification for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Houqiang Zhong, Tianchi Zhu, Qiang Hu, Xiaoyun Zhang, Li Song, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes ACD-GS, which replaces heuristic first-order screen-space gradient densification in 3D Gaussian Splatting with second-order depth-response-based, curvature-aware criteria to distinguish true geometric discontinuities from textures and noise, yielding more compact and geometry-faithful reconstructions.

entry.title: M-PFT: Angular Margin for Calibrated Prompt-Tuning of Fine-Tuned Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shihab Aaqil Ahamed, Mohamed Ansaff, Nang Khin Myat Lay Phyu, Udaya Sampath K. Perera Miriya Thanthrige, Chamira U. S. Edussooriya, Ranga Rodrigo, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: M-PFT is an angular-margin prompt-tuning method that addresses base-to-novel dual miscalibration in prompt-tuned VLMs, where models are underconfident on base classes and overconfident on novel classes. It introduces geometric understanding of the hyperspherical embedding space with two complementary margin-based objectives to reshape decision boundaries and improve calibration.

entry.title: MLLM-GS: Multimodal Large Language Model Prior-Guided Fast Novel View Synthesis in Extreme Environments

author.name: Zhiliang Wu, Xinye Zheng, Kun Li, Fei Wang, Hao Guo, Yanyan Wei, Guanghui Yue, Beier Zhu, Wei Zhou, Xun Yang

entry.summary: MLLM-GS uses multimodal LLM priors to guide fast novel view synthesis in degraded extreme environments, avoiding degradation-specific models and mitigating pixel misalignment and color deviations that generative priors would otherwise propagate into 3D reconstruction. It also targets reduced computational and memory cost versus prior 3D reconstruction pipelines.

entry.title: NeurEO: dissecting Earth observation embeddings with computational neuroscience

author.name: Thijs L van der Plas, Jacob JW Bakermans, Ioannis N Athanasiadis

entry.summary: Applies interpretability methods from computational neuroscience to analyze AlphaEarth embeddings, treating embedding features as spontaneous neural activity and relating them to land cover and elevation correlates as stimulus-response activity. The work aims to assign semantic meaning to compressed Earth observation representations used for geospatial downstream tasks.

entry.title: SonoWorld4D: From One Video to a 4D Audio-Visual Scene via Diffusion Synchronization

author.name: Derong Jin, Xiyi Chen, Ming C. Lin, Ruohan Gao

entry.summary: SonoWorld4D defines a new task, Video-to-4D Audio-Visual Scene generation, converting a monocular video into an explorable 4D scene with a 360-degree background, explicit motion trajectories of sound-emitting objects, and a physically grounded multi-source sound field synthesized via dual-space audio diffusion synchronization. Sound has been largely ignored in dynamic scene generation, making this a notable expansion of the modality space.

entry.title: HERON: Real-Time Obstacle-Aware Reachability Maps for Mobile Manipulators

author.name: G. Dupoiron, F. Michaud, J. P. Roberge

entry.summary: HERON is a 3D U-Net trained on reachability maps generated with GPU-accelerated inverse kinematics that predicts obstacle-aware reachability at 2 cm resolution from a live depth camera in real time. Deployed on a Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT and INT8 quantization, it enables online base-repositioning decisions during mobile manipulation.

entry.title: Ask to Evolve: A Unified Harness for Lifelong Embodied Navigation with Hybrid Action Space and Persistent Memory

author.name: Kai Sheng, Liuyi Wang, Jinlong Li, Haojie Dai, Chengju Liu, Qijun Chen

entry.summary: EvoLife is a navigation harness giving embodied agents a hybrid action space (waypoint, discrete, pixel-based, object-directed navigation), active interaction for seeking clarification, and persistent memory so experiences inform future tasks. It unifies action, interaction, and memory for lifelong embodied navigation. The design aims at agents that know when to ask for help and accumulate experience over time.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Sampling-Based Reachability: Geometry and Flow Distortion

author.name: Jixian Liu, Ihab Tabbara, Hussein Sibai, Enrique Mallada

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the geometric error of sampling-based reachability analysis as a support estimation problem under flow distortion, using assumptions on initial-set volume density, sampling density, and one-sided Lipschitz constants. It provides fine-accuracy guarantees that allow initial sets with corners and expanding or contracting dynamics, filling a gap left by prior probability-mass or convex-hull bounds.

entry.title: DecisionUnlearn-Bench: Unlearning Probabilistic Decisions under Changing Schemas

author.name: Tiantong Wu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: DecisionUnlearn-Bench empirically compares full, unlearned, and retain-only probabilistic decision models across deletion granularities, label renderings, and candidate sets on BANKING77, spanning 20 model configurations. It finds displacement grows from example to association to class deletion, and that replacing semantic labels with opaque codes nearly eliminates the retrained oracle's recognition of deleted classes. The label-rendering result is a surprising and useful insight for unlearning evaluation.

entry.title: PRISM: Personalized Item Representations in User History

author.name: Renzhi Wu, Zikun Cui, Junjie Yang, Li Sheng, Yongjun Xie, Jerry Fu, Nipun Mathur, Sri Reddy, Hong Li

entry.summary: Proposes personalized item representations for sequential recommenders, where each item's embedding expresses its relationship to the specific user rather than using a shared embedding map, instantiated in PRISM by reusing upstream ranking computations and compressing tower layer states with an autoencoder. This supplies richer evidence for downstream sequence modeling in production-scale recommendation.

entry.title: Strongly Adaptive Online Learning Achieves Uniform Discounted Regret

author.name: Sifan Yang, Wenhao Yang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors prove that strongly adaptive regret bounds directly imply uniform discounted regret guarantees for convex, strongly convex, and exp-concave losses, via an exact decomposition of discounted regret into a convex combination of interval regrets. This extends prior uniform discounted regret results, previously limited to convex functions and specialized meta-algorithms. A clean theoretical unification in online learning.

entry.title: From MS/MS evidence to adaptive spectroscopic characterization: Reinforcement learning guided by candidate molecular structures

author.name: Bowen Gao, Lei Zhu, Yiying Wang, Wenjie Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a structure-informed deep Q-network that uses existing tandem MS/MS evidence to decide whether further characterization is needed, which measurement (IR or NMR) to request, and when to stop. Evaluated on ~79K held-out samples with simulated multimodal spectra, it offers an adaptive sequential measurement policy for small-molecule identification.

entry.title: New Multiple Descent Phenomena Induced by Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Mark-Anthony Moisescu-Pareja, Elvis Dohmatob

entry.summary: The paper studies linear random-feature models trained on mixtures of datasets with different covariance structures, deriving exact asymptotic test-error expressions for each data source in the high-dimensional regime. It shows heterogeneity in covariance scale and spectral structure can induce new, group-dependent multiple-descent phenomena in scaling curves.

entry.title: UnEZ: A Fully Unsupervised Self-Templating Neural Network for Redshift and Line Strength Estimation

author.name: Asha Abd, Karl Glazebrook, Colin Jacobs

entry.summary: UnEZ is a fully unsupervised, physics-informed model that predicts spectroscopic redshifts and emission/absorption line strengths for galaxies without any labels, using an encoder that infers line parameters and a fixed deterministic decoder that reconstructs the spectrum. Tested on Sloan Digital Sky Survey data, it avoids reliance on curated templates or redshift catalogs that limit scalability of large spectroscopic surveys.

entry.title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework

author.name: Yuanchao Xu, Claire Valva, Ben Gao, Isao Ishikawa

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage framework approximating the fixed-lag Kolmogorov backward solution operator directly from data (e.g., via Fourier Neural Operators), then compressing the Galerkin projection onto a chosen finite-dimensional observable space, with error analysis covering learning, sampling, and invariance/reconstruction properties. It enables deterministic linear evolution of observables for stochastic Markov processes.

entry.title: Robust LLM-Generated Text Detection through Matched Conditional-Response Probing

author.name: Junfeng Hao, Wenxian Wang, Tao Leng, Xingshu Chen, Hao Ren, Haizhou Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MCRP, a frozen-LLM probing framework for detecting LLM-generated text that measures how a candidate responds when a semantically matched condition is introduced, removed, or replaced, comparing token-level losses. Designed to stay effective under meaning-preserving edits like rewriting, polishing, expansion, and translation that defeat lexical and syntactic detectors. Addresses robustness, a central unsolved problem in AI-text detection.

entry.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

author.name: Adilet Metinov, Chingiz Arziev

entry.summary: Glance merges reranking into the generator for retrieval-augmented generation: a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head score candidate passages from a shared prefill, avoiding separate reranker residency and per-pair prefilling. A single 9B model handles generation, decisions, and reranking with only ~0.1 GiB per decision skill, matching or beating bge-reranker-v2-m3 on SciFact and NFCorpus after brief fine-tuning. This is a practical efficiency contribution for RAG deployments.

entry.title: VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation

author.name: Yuan Wang, Yuhang Yu, Mengting Chen, Tianrun Xu, Zihao Pan, Xuetao Feng, Wei Li

entry.summary: VEvo-Harness is a causally-guarded continual self-evolving system for agentic visual generation that addresses the shallowness of generate-verify-rewrite loops by governing skill-library updates and preventing experience poisoning. It aims to convert trial-and-error iteration into a continual self-improving harness.

entry.title: CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment

author.name: Aadith Warrier, Gnana Prakash Punnavajhala, Siddharth Tourani, Muhammad Haris Khan, Avinash Sharma, Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: Shows that supervising a single model on sparse patch-point 2D-3D correspondences, without scene- or instance-level contrastive objectives, is sufficient for both scene-level and instance-level cross-modal retrieval between 2D images and 3D environments. This targets spatial reasoning applications in robotics and AR/VR where prior methods learn only whole-scene or whole-object alignment.

entry.title: TACOS: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision for Visual Footstep Planning

author.name: Jean-Michel Fortin, William Larriv\'ee-Hardy, Gabriel Jeanson, Olivier Gamache, Daniele De Martini, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau, Philippe Gigu\`ere

entry.summary: TACOS derives a physically meaningful footstep instability score from factor-graph residuals in legged state estimation and projects it into preceding images to supervise a dense visual predictor, with hindsight (hard) and causal (soft) variants. This gives legged robots terrain-aware contact supervision grounded in actual stability rather than intuition-chosen labels. A solid step toward vision-driven locomotion planning on rough terrain.

entry.title: A Spectral Boundary for Independence Learnability

author.name: Senhan Yao, Yuxin Zhou

entry.summary: The paper identifies a class-level boundary for testing independence between time series from a single observation record, governed by shared nontrivial Koopman eigenvalues representing common persistent oscillatory frequencies. When no shared eigenvalues exist, it constructs a deterministic weakly consistent test via extended shift-based rank calibration with finite-window dependence witnesses.

entry.title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Yilei Zhao, Guangyan Gan, Shuo Sun, Lin William Cong

entry.summary: Introduces FilingLoop, an interactive benchmark and self-evolving agent framework for corporate disclosure review built from 380 reconstructed SEC IPO review tasks across 96 companies grounded in real SEC correspondence. The benchmark tests discovering unstated deficiencies, acquiring missing facts, and verifying evidence-backed revisions, capabilities beyond standard financial QA.

entry.title: Assessing Language Models for Scientific Applications: Inertial Confinement Fusion as a Use Case

author.name: P. B. Radha, D. D. Meyerhofer, M. Bhattarai, B. Cheng, L. Diaz, C. L. Rousculp, A. G. Seaton, G. Gupta, P. Gurumurthy, V. Gutta, A. Jhunjhunwala, A. Vem, P. Cook, G. Rowe

entry.summary: Develops an expert-curated 250-question benchmark for inertial confinement fusion spanning qualitative reasoning, numerical calculation, symbolic derivation, and equation formulation, evaluated with deterministic numerical and symbolic checks plus model judges. Compares frontier closed- and open-source LLMs against Prospero, a model specialized via domain-adaptive pretraining and supervised fine-tuning for ICF.

entry.title: SkillCT: A Multidimensional Benchmark and Execution-Free Baseline for Agent Skill Assessment

author.name: Mengyu Sun, Zunlong Zhou, Ziyuan Yang, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: SkillCT is a benchmark assessing agent skills (packaged instructions, scripts, resources) across nine dimensions covering specification quality, behavioral robustness, semantic alignment, and responsibility boundaries. Its execution-free evaluation addresses the scalability limits of task-execution-based skill benchmarks and enables pre-deployment assessment.

entry.title: Can LLMs Faithfully Solve Ontology Engineering Tasks? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study

author.name: Bohui Zhang, Albert Mero\~no-Pe\~nuela, Elena Simperl

entry.summary: The paper introduces MIOE, a causal-abstraction benchmark using interchange interventions to test whether LLMs encode ontological knowledge (entity typing, subsumption prediction) internally rather than just behaviorally. It extends mechanistic interpretability from instance-level facts to ontological, class-level knowledge structures.

entry.title: From Leniency to Suspicion: How an Open Post-Training Recipe Changes Whom LLM Fact-Checkers Believe

author.name: Nouar AlDahoul, Yasir Zaki

entry.summary: The study examines job-based doubt in LLM fact-checking — judging claims as false more often when the poster has a lower-status job — across base and post-trained checkpoints of six model families with randomized poster profiles. It finds the bias emerges only with the open Tulu-3 post-training recipe, with effects under one percentage point but statistically reliable and exceeding training-drift baselines. The paper illuminates how post-training choices shape social bias in fact-checking.

entry.title: Efficient Agentic Audio-Visual Question Answering through Toolset Pruning and Modality Consolidation

author.name: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Peter Bell

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether omni-modal AVQA agents need broad specialized toolsets, pruning the OmniAgent toolset down to essential perceptual capabilities and consolidating modality-specific tools. It shows comparable answer accuracy with compact workflows while reducing long execution trajectories and inference cost. This informs efficient design of active-perception agentic systems.

entry.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI

author.name: Pradeep Kumar GS, Ravi Tanniru

entry.summary: The paper presents a production architecture for financial AI that combines a financial knowledge graph with provenance, a deterministic optimization engine for calculations, and a multi-agent LLM layer for interpretation and validation, coordinated through context engineering. The design targets numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability that LLMs alone cannot guarantee. It offers a template for moving beyond naive LLM wrappers in regulated domains.

entry.title: Timbre: Reliability-aware harmonic consensus for label-free multimodal test-time rexinforcement learning

author.name: Haotian Lyu, Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Feng Ji, Ziwen Li, Jiaxian Guo, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: Timbre addresses failure of majority-voting pseudo-labels in label-free test-time RL for vision-language models, where consistent but wrong consensuses can form. It builds a 2x2 grid of original and perturbed images crossed with direct-solving and reframing modes, then selects pseudo-labels via weighted harmonic aggregation that accounts for how much each transformation degrades task evidence. This improves the reliability of self-supervised test-time adaptation.

entry.title: Emergence of the transformer architecture as the score of entropic laws of random measures

author.name: Giacomo Greco

entry.summary: The author derives the transformer architecture from first principles, showing it emerges as the score of last-token laws in a maximum-entropy statistical model of language where sentences are empirical measures of tokens. The derivation recovers the softmax choice rule with the attention cross-moment as its mean parameter via Luce's choice axiom.

entry.title: The Real Cost of Context: Predicting Compute Time and Energy Consumption in LLM Prefill and Decode Phases

author.name: Lars Krupp, Daniel Gei{\ss}ler, Francisco M. Calatrava-Nicolas, Stefan Gerd Fritsch, Paul Lukowicz, Jakob Karolus

entry.summary: The paper systematically profiles compute time and energy consumption of LLM inference across prefill and decode token lengths, showing decode scales linearly with output length while prefill exhibits additional regimes, and fits generalized linear models to predict costs. This enables estimating the energy footprint of agentic workflows that consume large input contexts.

entry.title: Hybrid AI Patterns: Thirteen Ways to Couple Language Models with Rules, and How to Choose Among Them

author.name: Siegfried Handschuh, G\"otz-Henrik Wiegand, Lorena Raichle

entry.summary: This work catalogs thirteen design patterns for coupling language models with executable rule languages, presented in the Gang-of-Four catalogue format covering intent, applicability, participants, and consequences. Patterns are organized by what crosses the model-rules boundary, control relationships, model participation in reasoning, and knowledge persistence.

entry.title: Neighborhood Elites: Quality-Diversity Search for Uncertainty Quantification in Question Answering

author.name: Mesut Ceylan, Arda Baris Basaran, Elgar Fleisch, Filipe Barata

entry.summary: The paper improves perturbation-based uncertainty quantification for QA by using quality-diversity search to construct controlled rewrite sets that explicitly vary the type of context change and how explicitly the context supports the answer. This removes generator-driven bias inherent in free paraphrasing or adversarial perturbation approaches.

entry.title: Where Planning Changes the Outcome of Orbital Games

author.name: Duncan Eddy, Mahdi Al-Husseini, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: OrbitalGym is a JAX-based simulation environment for adversarial orbital rendezvous games, designed to disentangle whether planning quality or vehicle capability determines outcomes. Unlike prior studies with passive defenders, it supports multi-agent differential-reward encounters with varying agents and state representations.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity Search: Knowledge Graph Metadata Enrichment for Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Fakabbir Amin

entry.summary: The authors test whether a knowledge graph storing metadata and fast-changing information improves enterprise RAG retrieval over pure embedding similarity search. They evaluate on a snapshot of SEC EDGAR with over 167,000 filings and roughly 509,000 embedded chunks, using a knowledge graph of about 430,000 nodes to simulate metadata enrichment.

entry.title: Statistical Detection of Positional Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems: Methodologies and Empirical Evidence

author.name: Carlos Pel\'aez-Gonz\'alez, Francisco Herrera, Andr\'es Herrera-Poyatos

entry.summary: The paper studies positional bias in single-turn LLM-based recommenders built on RAG, where the recommended item depends systematically on candidate order in the prompt. It proposes two detection methods: POB-ICM using contingency tables and Chi-square tests, and POB-UNBP, a sample-efficient permutation-based test with formal statistical guarantees that supports stochastic decoding.

entry.title: Making Smart Homes Fit for Autistic Children: Family Work and Monitored Independence

author.name: Tingting Xiang, Weihan Jiang, Hrishitva Patel, Haiqi Shen, Tianzhi He, Kyrie Zhou

entry.summary: A multi-source qualitative study (caregiver interviews plus Xiaohongshu and Weibo posts) examining how general-purpose smart-home technologies support or hinder families with autistic children. It finds families do substantial ongoing work adapting outputs, prompts, and interaction channels, while sensory intensity and opaque device states create barriers.

entry.title: Measuring Deep Learning Performance - An Empirical Study of Performance Distributions Across Architectures and Tasks

author.name: Kevin L Coakley, Odd Erik Gundersen

entry.summary: This empirical study addresses non-determinism in deep learning by treating model performance as a distribution rather than a single number. The authors ran 186 experiments on image classification and time series forecasting architectures, each repeated 100 times with different random seeds (18,600 runs total), to characterize how performance distributions vary across architectures and tasks and what this implies for robustness.

entry.title: EARS-Info: Information-Aware Event-Driven Reallocation for Multi-Robot Exploration

author.name: Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Vahid Tavakkoli, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: EARS-Info extends Event-Driven Ant Reallocation Search with information-aware elements such as marginal sensing gain, return-aware routing, sensing reservations, and cached shortest paths for multi-robot exploration on city-map grids. Across 168,000 episodes and 30 implementations on eight maps, it achieves the highest mean operational score, including under 3% communication dropout.

entry.title: Convex-SKM-Net: Low-Latency Block Halfspace Corrections for Neural Convex Constraint Satisfaction

author.name: Haoyu Zhu, Xiaochen Zhang, Qingchun Hou

entry.summary: Convex-SKM-Net is a differentiable convex constraint-satisfaction layer that forms linearization halfspaces from residual and gradient oracles, applying fixed-depth dual projected gradient descent with GPU-friendly matrix operations instead of constraint-specific projectors. The method jointly learns a predictor and a positive-definite mobility matrix, with proven convergence of the outer iterates and improved objective quality on constrained decision-making tasks.

entry.title: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation

author.name: Charin Polpanumas

entry.summary: Vendster is an evaluation arena measuring how a forecaster's bias and prediction-interval width affect outcomes of buyer-vendor discount negotiations between LLM agents, using the M5 dataset. It evaluates two closed-model families (Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.6 Sol) and two open ones (DeepSeek-V3.2 and Qwen3), all long-established models, as tool-consuming negotiators. The core idea is measuring decision value of forecasts rather than accuracy alone.

entry.title: Statutory Article Retrieval from Arabic Judicial Narratives: Family Law and Law of Evidence in Saudi Arabia

author.name: Zarah Shibli, Areej Alhothali, Lulwah Alharigy

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks retrieval of Saudi Arabian statutory articles from Arabic judicial narratives across 200 synthetic cases and 381 articles, comparing BM25 variants, dense encoders, reciprocal rank fusion, and a proposed Decompose-and-Refine pipeline that splits narratives into legal issues with multi-channel queries. It addresses the narrative-to-legal-rule abstraction gap in Arabic legal NLP. This is valuable for grounding legal reasoning in authoritative sources in a low-resource setting.

entry.title: Benchmarking decision models against generative large language models on medical multiple-choice questions
