entry.summary: This conceptual paper defines structure-encoded problems whose input-output maps are constrained by known structure (solvers, symmetries, physical laws, grammars) and introduces the structure gap: the finite-resource gap between learners that receive the governing structure and those that must learn it from data. It argues the key issue for such tasks is finite-data identification and certification, not expressivity, limiting claims that scale alone can make domain knowledge optional.

entry.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control

author.name: Athanasios Glentis, Dawei Li, Mingyi Hong

entry.summary: The paper analyzes norm control in the Muon optimizer via accumulated effective learning rate, showing vanilla Muon's norm control accumulates only logarithmically, which may explain its slower empirical progress. It proposes MuonGS with relaxed weight-norm control that improves pretraining performance, connecting weight decay and explicit norm constraints in a unified trajectory-level analysis.

entry.title: On the VC Dimension of Autoregressive Linear Threshold Functions

author.name: Ilan Doron-Arad, Idan Mehalel, Elchanan Mossel

entry.summary: Resolves the VC dimension of deterministic autoregressive linear threshold functions, proving Theta(d^2) for every T >= d^2 and closing a quadratic gap against the O(d^2) counting bound. It further shows an exponential separation between deterministic and stochastic autoregressive models: logistic sampling in place of deterministic signs can raise VC dimension from quadratic to exponential in d.

entry.title: Benchmarking Task Takeover Across Agent Handoffs

author.name: Wenyuan Li, Guang Li, Dongyuan Li, Keisuke Maeda, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: Introduces HSC-Bench, a 1,039-task benchmark evaluating how well receiving agent models can take over partially completed work from another model, measuring both repository-evidence recovery and continuation from conversational, tool, and file state. Evaluations across six receiving models show that task-success and memory-retention metrics alone miss key aspects of handoff quality. Relevant to the growing area of multi-agent and handoff-based workflows.

entry.title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding

author.name: Rui Yang, Yanwei Li, Sili Chen, Jingjia Huang, Yi Lin, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: GeoUG is a unified geometric understanding and generation model that integrates metric-depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding, studying how geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence at inference improve spatial reasoning. The paper also introduces 3DCueBench to control geometric difficulty while balancing task selection. It provides evidence that generation capabilities can transfer to understanding tasks, an important question for multimodal models.

entry.title: Identity or Evidence? Auditing Evidence Dependence in Agentic Life-Science Benchmarks

author.name: Danai Brilli, Maria Georgila

entry.summary: This audit examines whether agentic life-science benchmarks (Biomni, LAB-Bench) actually test reasoning over evidence or merely recall of entity knowledge, by independently varying identity and evidence. When prompts contain decisive sequences or passages, blinding identity matters little, but with mostly-name prompts performance collapses from 0.742 named to 0.082 blinded versus a 0.093 chance level. The findings question the validity of prominent scientific-agent benchmarks and how their results should be interpreted.

entry.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions

author.name: Haoyu Zhao, Yinzhou Tang, Zixuan Wang, Minghao Zhu, Dongchi Huang, Xingyue Zhao, Qin Zhao, Kehan Li, Siteng Huang, Xin Li, Zhenyu Zeng, Mingxiu Chen, Deli Zhao, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: RynnWorld-Latent is a cross-embodiment video world model using 3D-grounded latent actions as a shared conditioning interface, enabling joint pretraining on human videos, robot demonstrations, and simulation rollouts without a common action space. It pretrains on roughly 23 datasets and combines global action tokens with an identity-initialized local pathway.

entry.title: Remember Where You Walk: Learning Spatial Memory for End-to-End Legged Robot Exploration

author.name: Leon Magnus, Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz

entry.summary: This work introduces the Local Spatial Matrix Memory (LSMM), a Hadamard-memory architecture that lets reinforcement learning policies for legged robots store task-relevant information at position-indexed memory cells. Unlike generic LSTMs that lose information over long horizons, LSMM provides spatially grounded memorization for exploration. It addresses a core limitation of end-to-end learned navigation in complex environments.

entry.title: CogArena: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents on Interactive Behavioral Experiments

author.name: Kiant\'e Fernandez, Caitlin Chen, Jialu Zhou, Bartek Sadowski, Anthony C. Miceli, Ian Krajbich

entry.summary: CogArena is a benchmark of ten social and behavioral science paradigms that AI agents complete through a real web browser with the same visual stimuli and response interfaces as human online participants. This both tests claims about model cognition under realistic conditions and raises the flag that agent-generated data can contaminate online behavioral science datasets. The dual purpose gives it unusual breadth.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reliably Grade Olympiad Proofs? A Study of Mathematical Verification with LLMs

author.name: Azim Ospanov, Zijin Feng, Ding Ding, Chengwu Liu, Haoli Bai, Jiacheng Sun, Lifeng Shang, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates LLM verification of natural-language Olympiad proofs using a human-curated dataset of USAMO 2025 candidate solutions with expert grading, covering frontier model verifiers. It also proposes TROJAN, an iterative self-improvement method for verification. The question of whether LLMs can replace costly expert proof-grading is central to scaling math reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Bingchao Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Shunyu Liu, Chengyu Wang, Jun Huang, Jie Yang, Wei Liu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: GUI-JEPA is claimed to be the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, selecting actions in latent space of an encoder pretrained on unlabeled screenshots rather than decoding action text. Candidate-conditioned latent predictors let lightweight heads score all candidate actions, addressing slowness and memory cost of VLM-based GUI agents.

entry.title: TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information

author.name: Chanwoo Park, Jaywoong Jeong, Zachary Wojtowicz, Yubin Kim, Taekyun Lee, Kaiqing Zhang, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: TeamGym is an environment for training and evaluating LLM agents on team decision-making with distributed information, built from legal, finance, medical, and software corpora. Its pivotal-information method identifies a minimal set of facts that are individually necessary and jointly sufficient, enabling controlled study of how agents identify and integrate crucial distributed information. This fills a real gap since agents are usually benchmarked in isolation.

entry.title: Let the Gate Decide: Per-Lookup Precision for Quantized Conditional Memory in LLMs

author.name: Tianqi Chen, Xunchao Li, Linchuan Xie, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Peisong Wang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: The paper studies quantizing conditional memory layers such as DeepSeek's Engram, where removing them from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash costs 36.8 PopQA points, and shows that frequency-based bit allocation backfires because gate values are small for frequent n-grams and large for rare long-tail facts. GateRQ stores rows as ladders of 1-bit residual codes with level 1 in GPU memory, computing a per-lookup gate from a 1-bit code to allocate precision. This is a sharp, well-motivated insight connecting gate statistics to where quantization error matters most.

entry.title: Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss

author.name: Oz Amram

entry.summary: Building on the Persona Selection Model and subliminal learning, this single-author paper introduces persona-header likelihood evaluation (PHLE), which decodes covert traits by evaluating likelihood of model outputs under the base pre-trained model with an appropriate header. It demonstrates that number sequences from a post-trained model prompted with different hidden traits can be distinguished, implying base models retain information about hidden intentions that prompted classifiers miss.

entry.title: Balanced State Subspaces for Mamba-2 State Compression

author.name: Shang Tingyu, Cao Wenfei

entry.summary: Analyzes trained Mamba-2 recurrent states and finds that although state energy is nearly rank-one, the output reads content from a misaligned low-dimensional subspace concentrated in a bias-like recurrence direction. Based on this write-read misalignment, the paper proposes compression targeting the write-read subspace, improving on coordinate-wise quantization or pruning.

entry.title: Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training

author.name: Yue Wu, Yang Zhang, Weinan Gan, Chongming Gao, Xinsen Guo, Xiaoyuan Li, Fuli Feng

entry.summary: The authors show that In-Place TTT, which repurposes MLP down-projections as fast weights for test-time training, loses its benefit on realistic web long-context QA because every context chunk is written with equal strength. They propose Select-TTT, a query-conditioned rule that selectively modulates fast-weight updates to avoid diluting relevant information. This matters for scaling long-context LLMs beyond attention-only context handling.

entry.title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning

author.name: Daan van Hamersveld, Ewoud Smeur, Iurii Kriachko

entry.summary: The authors present a fixed-wing interceptor drone controlled end-to-end by a neural network mapping filtered monocular camera input to control commands, aimed at autonomously intercepting Shahed-type strike drones that are costly to counter with conventional air defense. This extends learning-based autonomy from quadcopters to long-endurance fixed-wing platforms capable of high-altitude, longer-range interception.

entry.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions

author.name: Tongkun Guan, Zhibo Yang, Mingkun Yang, Haocheng Wang, Wei Shen, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: PerceptRL targets the perception bottleneck in post-training multimodal LLMs by converting verified errors extracted from dense image captions into verifiable QA-pair rewards via a multi-agent pipeline. It strengthens perception at two levels, moving from static answer supervision toward interaction-based rewards that survive subsequent training stages.

entry.title: Calibrated for Which Policy? Conformal Uncertainty for Fixed World Models Under Intervention

author.name: Ayush Mittal, Dhruv Gupta

entry.summary: This paper studies how changing a deployment policy invalidates a world model's calibrated uncertainty and develops weighted conformal calibration that transports marginal coverage to the target law using an estimated density ratio, with error bounds tied to domain-classifier log-loss regret. The ratio factors into state-occupancy and action-propensity terms for policy-controlled dynamics.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimal Small-Loss Bounds for Online Linear Optimisation on $\ell_p$ Balls

author.name: Jack J. Mayo

entry.summary: For full-information online linear optimization on the unit l_p ball, the paper gives an FTRL algorithm with a bounded radial regulariser that achieves regret matching newly proven lower bounds for small-loss sequences, without knowing the horizon or cumulative best-action loss, switching at most once to a quadratic augmentation. The constants are shown optimal as p grows large.

entry.title: SpatialPC: Deep Computation with Sublinear Local Credit Propagation

author.name: Benjamin Prada, Shion Matsumoto, Ankur Arjun Mali

entry.summary: The paper proves a light-cone lower bound showing that any local learning rule with bounded communication range on a chain of N states needs Theta(N) rounds for loss influence to reach early parameters, and constructs a unit-range directed acyclic graph in d dimensions where credit propagation requires only Theta(N^(1/d)) rounds. This reframes gradient-latency limits as a property of communication geometry rather than depth.

entry.title: Provenance Signatures for Low Rank Adaptations of Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Tobias Cheung, Mohan Dantam, Marc Juarez, Rik Sarkar

entry.summary: Develops a protocol and threat model for detecting when an online image service is quietly serving outputs from a LoRA adaptation of a standard diffusion model rather than the advertised base model. It formalizes two identification problems arising from multiple model families and multiple adaptations, going beyond prior work limited to closed lists of known models.

entry.title: TDLM: Adaptive Temporal Integration for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Bohang Sun, Max Zhu, Francesco Caso, Christopher Irwin, Jialin Yu, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Introduces TDLM, which lets unresolved token positions attend to their own history of hidden representations across denoising steps in masked diffusion language models, reusing computation already performed. Training uses self-generated trajectories with a simple cross-entropy objective, and on LLaDA the temporal modules add only about 0.84% trainable parameters.

entry.title: Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR

author.name: Peize Ding

entry.summary: This paper explains why label-free RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR), where models reward agreement with their own majority vote, improves reasoning initially but eventually collapses into uniform answers. It models this as a collective instability: when many problems share parameters, any shared perturbation is amplified while the population-averaged slope of the self-reinforcement drift stays positive. The analysis captures the observed dataset-size dependence of collapse.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Aware Planning via Imitation-Free Speed Scoring for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Emad Aghajanzadeh, Thomas Schwarzfischer, Marc Kaufeld, Moritz Thoma, Ryan P\'egoud, Manoj Rohit Vemparala, Pierpaolo Mori, Nael Fasfous, Johannes Betz, Daniel Mueller-Gritschneder, Ulf Schlichtmann

entry.summary: Introduces a driving planner that learns the path via imitation while scoring candidate speeds across multiple criteria without imitation, addressing the limitations of open-loop imitation learning such as single-behavior supervision and inability to adapt to user preferences at test time. The approach exploits the observation that driving behavior diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. Enables multi-modal, preference-conditioned end-to-end driving.

entry.title: LLM Hallucination Detection via Low-rank Multilinear Decomposition

author.name: Devansh Sharma, Faizul Rakib Sayem, Shahana Ibrahim

entry.summary: Proposes LOTUS, a low-rank Tucker-based multilinear decomposition framework that extracts compact discriminative representations from LLM hidden states across layers, feature modes, and tokens for hallucination detection, reducing dependence on selected activations or pooling and on labeled data. This targets the reliability problem of fluent but factually incorrect LLM outputs. Improves on methods that discard information distributed across the transformer.

entry.title: HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Ahmad Abdel-Azim, Xihong Lin

entry.summary: Introduces HELICS, a phasing-free latent flow matching framework for conditional generation of genome-wide SNP-level synthetic genotype data at biobank scale, learning an ultra-high-dimensional discrete distribution over hundreds of thousands to millions of correlated variants. Applications include privacy-aware benchmarking, simulation, and augmentation for underrepresented ancestries and rare-disease cohorts. Tackles a hard generative modeling problem with significant biomedical relevance.

entry.title: Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions

author.name: Jose Blanchet, Lutong Hao, Renyuan Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies episodic value-based RL for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions and proves an O(log K) regret bound with constants uniform in the discretization timestep, resolving deterioration of finite-horizon guarantees as timestep refines. Extensions cover linear-drift dynamics. A rigorous theoretical contribution connecting continuous-time control and RL regret analysis.

entry.title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Xiaomi Embodied Intelligence Team, Yuechen Luo (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Chong He (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Fang Li (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Shaoqing Xu (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Jingkai Wang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Menglun Su (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Jiaxin Liu (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Shengyin Jiang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Zhiyi Lai (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Long Chen (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Longlong Wang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Liang Hu (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Haochen Liu (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Yuncheng Jiang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Hongwei Xie (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Jieming Cui (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Hanbing Li (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Junjie Huang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Zhixiang Duan (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Hexin Zhang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Weixiang Liang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Ying Gong (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Yuhan Wang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Yong Pan (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Pengna Li (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Kangyi Wu (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Ken Deng (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Kun Ma (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Fuxi Wen (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Zhi-xin Yang (University of Macau, Tsinghua University), Hangjun Ye (University of Macau, Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: OmniBrain-0 is a lightweight unified embodied agent from Xiaomi and academic collaborators that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model handling task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Its progressive training combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) to distill powerful multimodal agents into compact models. This targets task-level reliability for general-purpose robots without costly reasoning at inference.

entry.title: What Carries Forward? Pretraining Disclosure Across Language Model Releases

author.name: Md Sakib Ul Islam, S M Mehedi Zaman

entry.summary: This paper audits 41 language model entries from 17 families using 24 pretraining-transparency indicators from the 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index, tracking disclosure changes across 24 adjacent model-version comparisons. It finds scores decreased in 11 comparisons versus increases in only six, with stable aggregate scores sometimes concealing substantial indicator losses. This provides rare longitudinal evidence on transparency practices in model development.

entry.title: Any3R: Feedforward 3D Reconstruction from Any Camera Type

author.name: Jingong Chen, Qingwen Zhang, Youming Deng, Chulwoo Pack, Olaf Wysocki, Boris Jutzi, Kwanghee Won, Kyle Gao

entry.summary: Any3R removes the pinhole-camera assumption from geometry foundation models by conditioning positional encoding and training loss on dense per-pixel ray fields rather than lens-dependent image coordinates, with solid-angle weighting scaling the point loss by pixel footprint. This enables feedforward camera-pose and dense-geometry recovery from any central camera type without distortion coefficients or field-of-view bounds. It addresses a genuine architectural limitation of current 3D foundation models.

entry.title: Confident First, Reflective Second: Reinforcement Learning of Confidence-Preserving Reflection for Video Understanding

author.name: Zihao Lin, Jingyuan Liu, Yucheng Zhang, Yuguang Yao, Lifu Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies confidence erosion in RL-trained video models that reflect and revise answers: because errors can be repaired later, correct initial answers earn less reward and reliability degrades. The authors propose a confident-first, reflective-second principle where the initial answer must stay above a floor set by a reference policy before reflection is allowed to improve on it. This insight about RL reward design likely generalizes beyond video to any self-correction setup.

entry.title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling

author.name: Kang He, Wenshuo Peng, Chuanhao Li, Zihui Gao, Xiaojie Xu, Zhengyuan Lin, Yuzhe Ding, Donghong Ji, Kaipeng Zhang, Yongtao Ge

entry.summary: GameVerse is a minute-scale gameplay video dataset with 69.7K clips, 1,655 hours, and 349.6 million frames, purpose-built for long-horizon interactive world modeling where existing datasets top out at sub-ten-second clips with coarse captions. It includes richer annotation designed for controllable long-duration generation. This directly targets the data bottleneck limiting world model coherence beyond one minute of rollout.

entry.title: HC2Robot: Hyper-Connection Transformers with Predicted Foresight for Multi-Terrain Humanoid Parkour

author.name: Wenhao Xu, Yanheng Mai, Yifei Fu, Nan Zheng, Yanbo Zhou, Zirui Huang, Mingsheng Ling, Xinjue Wang, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: HC2Robot tackles humanoid parkour over discontinuous terrain by learning a deployable approximation of privileged simulator information: a Predicted Foresight Module forecasts future footholds from onboard observations, feeding a Hyper-Connection Transformer for whole-body control. This narrows the asymmetric actor-critic information gap without exposing privileged signals at deployment.

entry.title: From 12 to 200 Demonstrations: How ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA and $\pi_{0.5}$ Scale on a Low-Cost Arm

author.name: Simon Cowling

entry.summary: This empirical study trains ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA, and pi0.5 on nested subsets of 12 to 200 teleoperated demonstrations of one pick-and-place task, then evaluates all models on a physical SO-101 arm across 1,340 scored episodes under a fixed training recipe. Pi0.5 with a fine-tuned action expert wins when data is scarce while from-scratch ACT overtakes it from 100 demonstrations onward, offering rare like-for-like data-scaling evidence.

entry.title: Is Your LLM Relay Serving What It Claims? A low-cost and high-power test for LLM Relay Auditing

author.name: Fangran Miao, Shengjie Niu, Jian Huang, Ting Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes distributional fingerprint auditing (DFA), a statistical method to verify whether LLM relay or reseller APIs actually serve the models they claim, using only textual responses. DFA queries semantically simple finite-choice probes, builds endpoint fingerprints from categorical response distributions, and makes statistically interpretable decisions under black-box access. This addresses a real transparency gap in the growing LLM relay/reseller market.

entry.title: Measuring agent capabilities on open-ended AI R&D tasks

author.name: Alex Jackson

entry.summary: Arrow Research evaluates frontier agents on four long, open-ended AI R&D tasks using automated checks plus expert rubrics scored by calibrated LLM judges, finding aggregate capability doubling roughly annually since 2024. GPT-6.1 Sol, released one day before coverage, is the best model; agents do markedly better on engineering-heavy than conceptual tasks, where doubling times run 7 to 16.8 months.

entry.title: CASEL: Consequence-Aware Selective Execution for Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Yanyan Zhang, Fei Shen, Ting Yan, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: CASEL is a model-agnostic runtime policy that allocates scrutiny to each proposed tool call by combining calibrated failure probability, consequence, reversibility, ambiguity, and evidence freshness, choosing among execution, verification, sandboxing, clarification, approval, or abstention by minimizing per-mode cost. It formalizes direct execution as selective prediction with finite-sample validity conditions. This addresses a key gap in safeguarding agents that mutate external systems.

entry.title: Adapting Video Models for Robot Control via Motion-guided Asymmetric Prediction

author.name: Taeyoung Kim, Junyoung Sung, Heeseung Kwon, Minseop Kim, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: Studies how visual supervision should be spatially allocated when adapting pretrained video generative models into World Action Models for robot control, showing that concentrating supervision on dynamic regions substantially improves policy performance. The proposed MoGAP augments WAM training with motion-focused asymmetric prediction objectives.

entry.title: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents

author.name: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck

entry.summary: Gym-Anything-RT is a benchmark of procedurally constructed visual minigames requiring real-time interaction, where the environment evolves while the agent reasons or the model computes a forward pass. It targets the underexplored latency-constrained regime of vision-language agent evaluation, contrasting with deliberative domains like math and software engineering.

entry.title: Live-OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Proactive Streaming Large Video Models

author.name: Kaixuan Du, Xin Wan, Dai Guan, Ming Chen, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces Live-OPSD, an on-policy self-distillation method for streaming multimodal assistants that must decide when to speak and when to remain silent while events unfold. The model generates continuations from streaming context alone, then re-evaluates them with privileged training-time hints, training on its own response prefixes rather than recorded turns.

entry.title: Why and How to Do Science When AI Is Better at It: A Framework Grounded in Human Understanding and Direction

author.name: Hoda Heidari, Aydin Mohseni

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-science paper arguing that human scientific practice remains justified by its role in producing durable, collective human understanding, and deriving a two-part test (human understanding, human direction) for when research tasks can be responsibly delegated to AI. It links the question of how to use AI in science to why humans should keep doing science.

entry.title: From Solver Trajectories to Teaching Trajectories: Cognition-Aligned Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Yashuo Luo, Qianren Mao, Ziqi Qin, Junnan Liu, Haitao Li, Qili Zhang, Yuan Gao, Zhijun Chen, Xu Wang

entry.summary: This work argues that distilling reasoning from large reasoning models is hampered because RLHF-trained teachers are optimized as solvers, not as teachers, producing trajectories that are hard for smaller models to imitate. The authors propose cognition-aligned distillation that transforms solver trajectories into teaching trajectories matched to student cognitive capacity. This could make reasoning distillation substantially more sample-efficient.

entry.title: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds

author.name: Haoxi Li, Sikai Bai, Jianfei Ma, Qinglin Hou, Xiaocheng Lu, Tao Han, Jie Zhang, Song Guo

entry.summary: Dwell is a model-based RL framework that reframes a pretrained VLM as a recurrent latent transition operator, enabling latent world-model predictions that drive policy improvement through online interaction. It tackles the challenges of distribution shift between policy updates and expensive continual updates of large pretrained models.

entry.title: LiveSearch: Questions as Executable Verifier Code for a Live Benchmark of Professional-Source Financial Search Agents

author.name: Sinuo Wang, Wentao Zhao, Jiacheng Lu, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Qiming Shi, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: LiveSearch is a live financial benchmark that stores each question as executable verifier code calling a professional financial data service, so gold answers are recomputed at evaluation time rather than fixed at annotation. This prevents staleness and leakage, rewarding genuine search and analysis over memorized recall.

entry.title: SCOPE: Source Credibility and Outlet Profiling Engine

author.name: Ilyas Nagiyev, Miras Baisbay, Daniil Orel, Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: SCOPE is a multi-agent system that profiles news outlets for bias, factuality, and credibility by coordinating agents for article acquisition, content analysis, external evidence search, scoring, and report generation, following an MBFC-style methodology with inspectable intermediate outputs. On a 200-outlet benchmark it beats LLM-only, article-only, search-only, and background-check baselines on most metrics. The work is significant for misinformation mitigation and for evidence that decomposed, evidence-grounded agent pipelines outperform monolithic LLM judgments.

entry.title: Agent or Human? Detecting Commits by AI Coding Agents in the Absence of Authorship Signatures

author.name: Kosei Horikawa, Hao Li, Yutaro Kashiwa, Youssef Esseddiq Ouatiti, Mohammed Sayagh, Bram Adams, Hajimu Iida, Ahmed E. Hassan

entry.summary: Using nearly 7.8 million commits from 1,226 repositories covering five AI coding agents, this study investigates whether agent-authored commits can be distinguished from human commits once authorship signatures like bot accounts and co-author trailers are removed. The detectors retain substantial ranking ability after signature masking, establishing the signals and limits of signature-free AI-commit detection.

entry.title: Do AI Scientists Know What's New?

author.name: Miri Liu, Xiayu Zhao, Encheng Xie, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: Builds an analytical framework for evaluating novelty checks in AI scientific discovery pipelines, using temporal ground truth at both proposal and claim level across four datasets of 1,060 proposals drawn from published papers, reviewer disputes, and ideas later validated by the field. The audit finds that existing novelty checks have significant weaknesses in rejecting non-novel ideas without discarding genuinely novel ones.

entry.title: From Voiceprints to User Entities: Online Speaker-Memory Construction for Multi-User Spoken Agents

author.name: Yucong Zhang, Cancan Li, Bo Xiao, Ke Zeng, Ming Li

entry.summary: This paper addresses the gap between speaker identification and memory systems in personalized spoken agents, arguing that voiceprints are observations of identity rather than identities themselves. It introduces EvoSpeakerMem, a training-free layer for causal speaker routing, selective acoustic-state updates, and identity-partitioned memory writes, along with LoCoMo-ID, a new spoken-memory benchmark with hidden speaker identities and speaker-sensitive queries. This matters because multi-user voice assistants need reliable identity attribution before retrieving user-specific memories.

entry.title: EnergyCal: Taming Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training

author.name: Masato Fujitake

entry.summary: EnergyCal is a lightweight rule that attenuates routed-expert updates in Muon-family optimizers using the normalized squared Frobenius norm of Newton-Schulz directions, without changing the spectral transform or adding persistent state. On a 4B-parameter sparse MoE model it reduces thresholded loss-spike burden by over 99% and improves final perplexity by about 4% versus a tuned baseline recipe.

entry.title: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features

author.name: Yunlong Wang, Alyssa Wu, Cuiyun Gao, Jia Feng, Songyuanyi Lu, Zhichao Hu

entry.summary: FeatureArc is a new benchmark evaluating coding agents on features that evolve over successive extensions, requiring agents to build correctly on their own earlier code. It constructs tasks from repository histories, combines inter-stage dependencies with explicit interface contracts and executable checks across four programming languages.

entry.title: Bridging Exploration and Loss of Plasticity in On-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Andrea Vasco Grieco, Evelyn D'Elia, Edoardo Caldarelli, Raffaello Camoriano

entry.summary: Analyzes loss of plasticity (LoP) in PPO with isotropic Gaussian policies, identifying the policy standard deviation as a key causal factor and characterizing geometric conditions under which plasticity loss arises. The work also offers explanations for why widely used LoP mitigation techniques work. This connects two important RL phenomena — exploration and plasticity loss — that are usually studied separately.

entry.title: Nonlinear Direct Feedback Alignment for Scalable Backpropagation-Free Training

author.name: Wu Lin, Yan Fan, Chenxiang Ma, Yinglan Feng, Jia Wang, Ka-Chun Wong, Qiuzhen Lin

entry.summary: Proposes Nonlinear Direct Feedback Alignment (NDFA), which replaces the fixed feedback matrices of DFA with constructions capturing the nonlinear map from hidden representations to network output. This narrows the performance gap between backpropagation-free training and backprop while removing backward locking, enabling greater layer-wise parallelism.

entry.title: Sharpness-Aware Muon: Matrix-Aware Optimization with Momentum-Guided Perturbations

author.name: Zhiwei Zhai, Wenjing Yan, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MuSAM, which embeds Sharpness-Aware Minimization-style perturbations into the Muon optimizer's orthogonalized updates to bias training toward flat minima associated with better generalization. The authors also analyze the efficiency-stability tension this creates and propose a momentum-guided perturbation mechanism to mitigate it. This bridges two influential threads in optimizer research.

entry.title: Causal DAG-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Physical Activity Maintenance: Using Prior Data to Inform Future Deployment

author.name: Xueqing Liu, Young Hyun Cho, Bhanu Teja Gullapalli, Predrag Klasnja, Susan Murphy

entry.summary: Develops an online RL system for the forthcoming ADAPT trial that personalizes twice-daily physical activity suggestions to improve affective associations, using a causal DAG built from prior data to structure the policy under scarce per-participant data, partial observability, and infrequent outcomes. The work addresses real digital-health constraints including reward gaming and delayed measurement. Demonstrates how prior trial data can inform future RL deployments.

entry.title: SuperJEPA: Pretraining with a Supervision-Augmented Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for High Energy Physics

author.name: Dylan Sheldon Rankin, Ho Fung Tsoi

entry.summary: Introduces SuperJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture augmented with a supervised objective, and asks whether self-supervised pretraining still helps when large labeled simulation already exists, as in high energy physics. They find improved downstream jet-tagging across tasks, model sizes, and dataset sizes, with gains persisting for both frozen and fine-tuned encoders. The result challenges the assumption that labels make self-supervision redundant and informs future particle-physics foundation models.

entry.title: Privately Clipping Heavy-Tailed Data

author.name: Matthew Joseph, Alex Kulesza

entry.summary: Introduces a differentially private method for choosing a clipping bound from the data by optimizing residual coherence, the directional alignment of vectors exceeding the bound, against the noise-variance cost, and proves a close relationship between residual coherence and bias for heavy-tailed regimes. Empirically the method outperforms existing approaches across several datasets. Fills a real gap since DP libraries offer few tools for private bound selection.

entry.title: FASST: A Compact Stateless Atmosphere Model for Long-Term Ocean Coupling

author.name: Pratham Aggarwal, Duncan Watson-Parris, William E. Chapman

entry.summary: FASST replaces the expensive atmospheric and sea-ice components of a coupled climate model with lightweight U-Net emulators while retaining a prognostic ocean model, enabling 140-year stable unforced climate simulations. The emulator matches CESM2 piControl global-mean sea surface temperature closely and captures interannual Nino-3.4 variability. This demonstrates that ML emulators can make long-term coupled climate simulations dramatically cheaper.

entry.title: Second-order Sinkhorn Geometry and $\sqrt{n}$-Inference

author.name: Tristan Luca Saidi, Florian Gunsilius, Gonzalo Mena

entry.summary: This paper extends a recently constructed formal Riemannian structure on the space of probability measures that quadratically approximates the Sinkhorn divergence, enabling geometric operations like interpolation and barycentric averaging that the non-metric Sinkhorn divergence previously lacked. It also derives sqrt(n)-rate statistical inference guarantees. This bridges optimal transport geometry and statistical theory for a widely used computational tool.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Deep Kernel Tests for Structured Outcomes

author.name: Robin Leman, Bariscan Bozkurt, Sofiane Tanji, Arthur Gretton, Houssam Zenati

entry.summary: This paper proposes DR-KTE-Deep, a hypothesis test for whether two interventions yield the same outcome distribution when outcomes are structured and high-dimensional (images, text, graphs). It represents interventional distributions as mean embeddings on learned deep features and optimizes those features to maximize a power criterion, with theoretical guarantees including asymptotic signal-to-noise characterization and finite-sample bounds. This matters for causal inference in domains where treatment effects manifest in complex data types.

entry.title: Nothing Left Behind: Finding Evidence from a Large Randomized Evaluation Corpus

author.name: Giuliano Martinelli, Abelardo Carlos Martinez Lorenzo, Satvik Garg, Linxi Wang, Riccardo Orlando, Piriyakorn Piriyatamwong, Samuel Paul Fraiberger

entry.summary: Compares curated-vocabulary label-based search against an embedding-then-LLM-filter approach for exhaustive evidence finding, on a corpus of 7,354 randomized trials. Label search recovered only 45% of the evidence a systematic review would include, while the embedding-plus-LLM approach recovered 92%, at query costs rising with search depth. Strong evidence for meaning-based retrieval in high-recall applications.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Bias in MLLM for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Xusheng Liang, Jianqiao Sun, Hao Zhang, Yulei Niu, Hengshuang Zhao, Jiawei Ma

entry.summary: The authors argue that long-video QA performance in multimodal LLMs is constrained not only by frame sparsity but by shortcut biases from spurious linguistic correlations and salient-yet-irrelevant visual cues. They introduce S-MME, a benchmark for diagnosing such biased behavior, and propose a mitigation method. This matters because it reframes long-video understanding as a bias problem rather than purely a context-length problem.

entry.title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models

author.name: Yonghao Yu, Lang Huang, Runyi Li, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues that the VLA-versus-world-action-model debate conflates three separable design choices: backbone initialization, the future-observation objective, and whether the foresight machinery is kept at inference. The authors unify both families under a Just Action Model framework with an action loss and a foresight loss, clarifying what actually drives reported differences. This kind of decomposition is valuable for the rapidly growing robot learning field.

entry.title: ReferStream: Interactive Subject Injection for Streaming Video Generation

author.name: Shuolin Xu, Guanyuan Li, Boyu Li, Kelu Yao, Xiaogang Xu, Hongchuan Yu, Shuicheng Yan, Xiaobin Hu

entry.summary: ReferStream is a training-free framework for injecting new visual subjects into streaming video generation while preserving established subjects and scene context. It combines scene-conditioned reference construction with transient cache injection and joint latent placement of reference features.

entry.title: OpenJaws: An Open Hardware UMI Framework with Stereo Localization for Generalist Manipulation

author.name: Adithyavairavan Murali, Yash Oza, Karanbir Chahal, Neel Jawale, Silas De Vries, Hesam Rabeti, Erwin Coumans, Balakumar Sundaralingam, Stan Birchfield

entry.summary: OpenJaws is a fully open hardware and software framework for sensorized Universal Manipulation Interface data collection, pairing a 3D-printed modular gripper with stereo-based localization to fix scale ambiguity and drift of monocular approaches. It lowers cost and setup burden for gathering high-quality manipulation demonstrations in the wild.

entry.title: KEPT: Conformal Keepouts Kept in Planning for Enclosed-Space Navigation in Degraded Sensing

author.name: Eric Minwoo Kim, Jong-Kook Kim

entry.summary: KEPT combines conformal prediction with motion planning to keep autonomous vehicles safe in tunnels and mines where smoke, dust, and fog degrade range maps. The method conditions conformal margins on a label-free severity estimate to maintain coverage guarantees under varying degradation, and enforces a braking-distance constraint in the planner. This offers statistically grounded safety rather than ad-hoc obstacle inflation.

entry.title: When Retrieval Is Not Enough: Obsolete Facts in Agent Memory

author.name: Oleeviya Babu Poikarayil, Tony Basil Babu, Abdulrahman Nahhas, Het Darshan Mehta, Jawid Ahmad Baktash, Ernesto William De Luca, Klaus Turowski

entry.summary: The paper disentangles retrieval failure from evidence-usage failure in memory agents, showing on MemoryAgentBench that accuracy drops from 45% to 32% as evidence budget grows even when the newest fact is always retrieved, with errors concentrated on questions containing obsolete statement versions. The presence of a single outdated competing fact among otherwise equal evidence substantially degrades answer correctness.

entry.title: God Does Not Play Dice: Enforcing Batch Invariance in Agentic Kernel Generation

author.name: Youwei Bao, Chengpeng Wang, Simin Chen

entry.summary: This work identifies batch invariance violations in LLM serving kernels, finding 19 confirmed violations among 83 released batch-applicable artifacts, meaning identical requests can produce different numerics depending on dynamic batch composition. The authors propose a plug-in for kernel-generation agents combining contract-guided static dependency analysis with dynamic bitwise-consistency validation. This matters for reproducibility of LLM inference at scale.

entry.title: Correctness Conditioning as Selection in Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Evaluation

author.name: Yueer Pan, Yuexi Pan

entry.summary: The paper models the common practice of restricting CoT faithfulness evaluation to correctly answered instances as a selection problem in a seven-variable structural causal model, deriving the exact observed gap and distinguishing difficulty confounding from shortcut-induced collider bias. A review of 18 papers plus experiments on arithmetic tasks shows positive selection gaps across deployments.

entry.title: M4Bench: Evaluating Procedural Specification for Clinical EHR Derivation Agents

author.name: Hannes Ill, Rafi Al Attrach, Rajna Fani, Ahram Han, Ryohei Yamamoto, Marlene Louisa Moerig, Dukyong Yoon, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: M4Bench provides 28 clinical derivation tasks on MIMIC-IV and eICU to test whether AI coding agents can reproduce EHR-derived variables, decomposing the value of clinician-reviewed skills into specification completeness, delivery format, and schema familiarity. In Docker-isolated campaigns with GPT 5.4 Mini and GPT 5.5 (both existing models), skills raise reward by 0.136 with 26 of 28 tasks improving. It is a valuable benchmark at the intersection of clinical AI and coding agents.

entry.title: Specialization, Diversity, and Scaling in Child-Scale Language Models

author.name: Steven Y. Feng, Michael C. Frank

entry.summary: Trains small GPT-2 models on dense home recordings of child-directed speech (BabyView) and synthetic TinyDialogues to study language learning from small naturalistic datasets, finding strong per-child specialization that is largely lexical and reproducible by 5-gram models (r=.91), while multi-child training improves pooled held-out prediction. The work connects scaling behavior to developmental cognitive science.

entry.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception

author.name: Lai Wei, Yatai Li, Liangbo He, Jun Lan, Renjie Gu, Linhan Cao, Junkai Lin, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Linghe Kong, Yue Wang, Zhuosheng Zhang, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies connecting evidence — identifying relevant visual facts, binding them to entities, and composing relations — as the shared capability underlying spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding, and proposes EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-synthesize data pipeline targeting this capability. This matters because targeted training data for these perception tasks is otherwise difficult and costly to create.

entry.title: Action-Value Calibration via Continuation Sharing for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yingjian Chen, Lang Zhou, Zixin Zhao, Pingfan Li, Weishi Zheng, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: ConCal addresses credit assignment in long-horizon agentic RL by recursively combining continuation evidence shared across a rollout batch with each visit's own trajectory tail, matching visits by incoming state-action-state transitions. This reduces the sensitivity of per-action value estimates to later decisions compared with methods like GiGPO that use a single sampled continuation.

entry.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence

author.name: Shilong Li, Xingyuan Bu, Hao Shi, Yun Xing, Weixin Feng, Qiangpeng Yang, Shilei Wen

entry.summary: VideoLVR addresses visual forgetting in video-MLLM chain-of-thought reasoning by constructing reasoning over latent visual evidence tokens rather than textual coordinates or reinserted crops, letting the model revisit grounded visual content without the context blowup of frame reinsertion. This enables reasoning traces that keep visual evidence available throughout the chain of thought.

entry.title: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework

author.name: Jelmer van Lune, Miha Fuderer, Oscar van der Heide, Matteo Maspero, Martin B. Schilder, Jan Willem Dankbaar, Stefano Mandija, Alessandro Sbrizzi

entry.summary: The authors present a physics-guided self-supervised framework embedding a two-pool magnetization transfer signal model to estimate macromolecular pool fraction, a myelin-sensitive biomarker, directly from conventional T1w, T2w, and FLAIR clinical brain MRI without paired quantitative reference scans. This could enable large-scale retrospective studies of myelin integrity using existing clinical data. Strong translational medical imaging contribution.

entry.title: DocSkill: Skill-Integrated Agentic Reasoning for Multilingual Multi-Hop Document Question Answering

author.name: Jing Huang, Zhiya Tan, Changtao Miao, Shutao Gong, Yang Wang, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Jianshu Li, Ying Yan

entry.summary: Presents DocSkill, an agentic framework for multilingual multi-hop document QA with a learned skill-orchestration policy that adaptively selects, revisits, or skips skills based on evolving evidence state. Supervision for orchestration is constructed offline via bounded Monte Carlo Tree Search over skill trajectories. Targets coordinating evidence acquisition, cross-page integration, and answer verification.

entry.title: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Cross-View Temporal Object Correspondence

author.name: Siyoon Jin, Dahyun Chung, Honggyu An, Sangbeom Lim, Wonjin Nam, Jaewoo Jung, WonJun Moon, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: The paper defines the cross-view temporal object correspondence task, requiring object identity to be preserved across both views and time from a query mask, and proposes XTrack, which repurposes a pretrained video DiT for RGB-to-mask latent transport. It jointly models cross-view matching and temporal tracking while addressing failure modes where DiTs attend to semantically similar but incorrect objects.

entry.title: Trace-WAM: Learning to Act via 3D Motion Prediction for World Action Models

author.name: Xu Hu, Changjie Wu, Linzhe Shi, Hang Zhang, Chen Yang, Lingjun Zhang, Guowen Zhang, Mu Xu, Junran Peng, Qing Li, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: Trace-WAM augments world action models with future 3D motion prediction as an auxiliary objective, supervising temporal point correspondence plus image displacement and depth change to focus learning on robot-object interaction dynamics. A three-branch Mixture-of-Transformer architecture jointly handles video prediction and action generation.

entry.title: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule

author.name: Minh Pham Van, Cong Tran

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how retrieval-augmented LLMs should resolve conflicts between retrieved context and parametric knowledge, proving decision-theoretically that any fixed rule (always trust context or memory) is dominated where it is not exactly optimal. It argues for adaptive, prior-based approaches and shows that symmetric divergence between sources carries no information about which source is correct.

entry.title: RouteDRAG: Learning to Route and Control Agentic Execution for Multimodal Document RAG

author.name: Zekai Chen, Hao Zhu, Yu Liu, Xunkai Li, Zejian Kang, Rui Qian, Quanjiang Li, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: RouteDRAG is a learning-based framework that decides when agentic execution is warranted for multimodal document RAG, controlling both agent invocation and subsequent execution steps. The key insight is that agentic iteration helps some queries but wastes computation or degrades accuracy on others. This addresses a real efficiency-quality tradeoff as RAG systems move to long multimodal documents.

entry.title: The View from Nowhere: Population-Centered Agent Evolution

author.name: Shuo Yan, Ningning Hou, Haoyu He, Haochen Pei, Shang Gao

entry.summary: This paper identifies a substantial gap between population coverage and best-individual performance in self-improving agent evolution, showing that useful capabilities across evolved variants go unconsolidated into leading agents. It proposes the view-from-nowhere principle: improve each agent by interpreting its behavior through population-wide patterns of success, failure, and prior experience. This reframes agent self-improvement from parent-centric to population-centric.

entry.title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement

author.name: Hao Chen, Yukun Yan, Ziyu Han, Ye He, Chuanzhe Guo, Shangzhan Li, Qi Shi, Qingfu Zhu, Maosong Sun, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: RuHarness is a framework in which evaluation rubrics and agent harnesses co-evolve: behavioral criteria are continually discovered and reassessed from execution trajectories to guide targeted harness updates. This addresses the problem of static supervision failing to track changing agent weaknesses over rounds.

entry.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning

author.name: Haiqian Yang, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: Prospector is a compact model trained to traverse domain knowledge graphs step by step, calling tools to progressively build context and answer with an evidence chain checkable edge by edge against the graph. It targets scientific reasoning in specialized fields where knowledge is proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data.

entry.title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories

author.name: Zirui Ding (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Xinxin Fan (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, State Key Laboratory of AI Safety, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Hao Yuan (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, ShanghaiTech University), Shaoye Luo (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, State Key Laboratory of AI Safety, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Men Niu (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Yunfeng Lu (Beihang University)

entry.summary: CauTrace is a white-box diagnostic framework that traces why LLM reasoning fails using functional states, representation propagation, temporal-state coordination, and reasoning trajectories, asking whether ordinary and adversarial failures share internal signatures. Defining seven functional states to characterize support and constraint processing is a creative interpretability contribution. This could inform both debugging and adversarial robustness.

entry.title: Layerwise Repacking: Variable-Length Hybrid-Attention Training without an Extra Redistribution Pass

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Junwei Feng, Dongliang Huang, Xiaoling Zhou, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song

entry.summary: Layerwise Repacking tackles conflicting parallelism requirements in variable-length training of hybrid-attention models: full-attention layers need wide SP16/32 groups while sparse-attention layers are best balanced within node-local SP8 groups, and cross-node all-to-all communication is 7.0x slower. The method keeps each SP16 group alive and repacks work layerwise, avoiding a data redistribution pass at full-sparse boundaries. This is a meaningful systems contribution for efficient long-context MoE-hybrid training.

entry.title: Do Coding Agents Still Need a Debugger? Frontier-Model-Based Fault Localization at the Accuracy Ceiling

author.name: Christoph Daxerer, Johann Glock, Christian Macho, Rudolf Ramler, Martin Pinzger, Josef Pichler

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates whether coding agents based on frontier models (Sol 6.1, Luna 6, Qwen 3.8) still benefit from interactive debugger assistance for fault localization, testing 610 seeded single-line faults across 144 programs with behavior-preserving transformations. It measures static-reasoning accuracy, gains from debugger use, cost, and whether agents use the debugger when optional. The finding that frontier models approach an accuracy ceiling informs tool-design decisions for coding agents.

entry.title: Replication or Corroboration? An Axiomatic Framework for Evidential Dependence in Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Hoang-Loc Cao, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Phuc Truong Loc Nguyen, Vo Thanh Khang Nguyen, Phuc Ho, Hung Nguyen, Duc Pham, Long Tran-Thanh, Hung Cao

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a subtle problem in multi-agent debate judging: matching reports may reflect cheap replication of the same evidence or genuine independent corroboration. The authors define a minimal judgment game and prove that an axiom called root replication invariance exactly characterizes threshold-uniform replication immunity, giving judges a principled way to avoid over-weighting paraphrases and relays.

entry.title: Less is more: learning what to profile for GPU kernel optimization

author.name: Yihan Wang, Peiyu Liu, Runyu Chen, Wei Xu

entry.summary: Shows that for LLM-based GPU kernel optimization, more profiling metrics do not monotonically improve results and the most useful profiling information varies per kernel; the paper provides theory showing kernel-conditioned profiling selection can beat any fixed strategy. It proposes learning what to profile as part of the optimization loop.

entry.title: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution

author.name: Jia Gu, Liang Pang, Huawei Shen

entry.summary: This work identifies surface-form bias in gradient-based data attribution for LLM instruction tuning, where trivial wording or formatting changes produce inconsistent attribution scores. It proposes CIGA, a framework that selects robust gradient layers to achieve content-invariant attribution for data selection. This matters because reliable data attribution underpins efficient, high-quality fine-tuning data curation.

entry.title: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding

author.name: Ruilin Yao, Xinyu Qiu, Tianyu Zou, Yi Rong, Shengwu Xiong, Shuheng Shen, Changhua Meng

entry.summary: This work uses GUI grounding as a scalable source of supervision for active, task-oriented visual observation, training vision-language models via supervised initialization on teacher trajectories followed by RL for multi-turn crop-and-inspect decisions. The resulting LBS models, built on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B backbones, improve over baselines and transfer to general perception benchmarks beyond GUIs.

entry.title: Retrieve to Act: Motion Primitive Graph Retrieval for Robust VLA Execution

author.name: Pham Tri Quang, Bao-Ngoc Dao, Minh Duc Nguyen, Duc-Duy Nguyen, Hung T. Ho, Linh Dang Le, Trong-Bao Ho, Thien-Loc Ha, Tan Q. Nguyen, Tuan Dam, Vu N. Duong, Daniel Sonntag, Ngan Le, Khoa D. Doan, Jan Peters, An Thai Le, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien Anh Ngo

entry.summary: Retrieve to Act improves out-of-distribution robustness of vision-language-action policies by structuring successful training demonstrations into a spatiotemporal motion primitive graph and, at inference, using a query-dependent GNN to retrieve relevant kinematic priors, bypassing fragile visual features. It formulates test-time scaling for VLA execution as a geometric retrieval problem.

entry.title: How Reliable Is Individualized Functional-Network Attribution in Resting-State fMRI Cognitive Prediction in ADNI?

author.name: Sheethal Bhat, Mahfuzur Rahman Chowdhury, Imam Ahmed Shaik, Rose Dawn Bharath, Siming Bayer, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: This paper audits test-retest reliability of per-subject network-ablation attributions in a frozen resting-state fMRI predictor of cognitive scores trained on 875 ADNI subjects. While split-half reliability is near-ceiling, scan-rescan reliability drops substantially and attribution correlations persist even under a mismatched-subject permutation null, indicating strong subject-independent structure dominates the attributions.

entry.title: Orthogonal and Parametrized Multi-Attribute Steering of LLMs

author.name: Remy Ogasawara, Cullen Anderson, Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer, Foad Namjoo, Amir Abdullah, Jens Kristian Refsgaard Schou, Jeff M. Phillips

entry.summary: The paper improves activation steering of LLMs by identifying each steering vector's most steerable interval and rescaling for consistent, interpretable strength, then introducing parameterized steering that sets activations to a desired trait strength instead of pushing in a direction. For multi-trait steering, it develops orthogonalization methods to prevent interference between combined steering vectors.

entry.title: From Generation to Scoring: Scaling LLM-Based Semantic Labeling at LinkedIn

author.name: Jian Sheng, Sriram Vasudevan, Sundara Raman Ramachandran, Yang Hu, Junyu Zhou, Xiaojing Ma, Haolan Qin, Tiffany Zhou, Vedant Vipul Jhaveri, Ashwini Bhingare, Chinmay Kini, Qing Lan, Xiaoqing Wang, Suleyman Cetintas, Fedor Borisyuk

entry.summary: Presents LinkedIn's production recipe for LLM-based data labeling, reformulating multi-label generation as semantic scoring where each decision is a single answer-token score from a prefill-only pass, plus Multiple-Item Scoring with attention masking to score hundreds of candidates in one sequence. Deployed at scale for profile qualification labeling. A valuable industrial case study on efficient LLM inference for labeling pipelines.

entry.title: Meta Models: Models that Model Learning

author.name: Peihang Li, Ziming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes meta-models that predict the learning behavior of other models, unifying final-performance prediction, learning-curve prediction, and hyperparameter selection as queries to a single training response function. In an initial empirical study treating language-model training records as numeric data, an off-the-shelf tabular in-context learner (TabPFN) matches or beats a fine-tuned LLM meta-model across settings.

entry.title: SimplexLoRA: Dynamic Rank Updating via Alternating Minimization with Simplex Projection

author.name: Igor Shalygin, Grigorii Davydenko, Andrey Veprikov, Aleksey Antonov, Nikolay Bushkov, Stanislav Moiseev, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: SimplexLoRA is a LoRA variant that adaptively allocates adapter rank during fine-tuning by optimizing per-adapter importance weights on the simplex during a warm-up phase and then freezing them. It allocates parameter capacity where it matters most without increasing the overall parameter budget or inference cost. Evaluations span 12 language understanding and summarization tasks.

entry.title: A Simple Presentation of Robust Membership Inference Attacks

author.name: Renaud Gaucher, Ephraim Linder, Adam Smith, Jonathan Ullman, Lydia Zakynthinou

entry.summary: Provides a simple, unified presentation of robust membership inference attacks for mean estimation, covering multivariate Gaussian and binary product distributions, where robust means success despite arbitrarily introduced noise in the statistics. Includes a survey of the robust membership inference literature, its history, extensions, and connections to other areas. Clarifies theoretical foundations for a key privacy-attack model.

entry.title: Causal Localization of Evidence Effects in Transformers

author.name: Jipeng Li, Pramod Khargonekar, Yanning Shen

entry.summary: The paper introduces controlled evidence aggregation (CEA), a symbolic-input method for identifying attention heads in frozen Transformers that causally influence decisions based on natural language evidence, combined with a balanced-utility causal selection procedure. It derives conditional bounds relating head attribution to intervention effects. This contributes to mechanistic interpretability with a rigorous causal methodology.

entry.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well

author.name: Ian Chuang, Hiya Shah, Vamsi Chilamkur, Iman Soltani, Claire Tomlin

entry.summary: The paper trains LEAP-hand policies for in-hand object pose reaching, moving objects to nearly arbitrary poses at any wrist orientation over long sequences of consecutive goals, using simulation-only training with diverse resets, generated goals, and safety-aware techniques, without human data. It explicitly measures safety (not dropping the object), which is rarely evaluated in dexterous manipulation. This pushes dexterity well beyond simple grasps and repeated rotations.

entry.title: Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences

author.name: Xiang Ding

entry.summary: Investigates whether language models, like humans, retain traces of syntactic analyses they have abandoned after garden-path sentences. Across 24 open models from 124M to 70B parameters, a residue of the abandoned parse raises later object attachment at about three-quarters the strength of a genuine object-bearing sentence, appearing even in sampled text. Connects psycholinguistic phenomena to LLM internal processing.

entry.title: UCVE: Graph Structured Retrieval for Compliance Validation

author.name: Emily Chen, Michelle Menachery, Himanshu Kumar, Rahul Nenavath, Amirfarrokh Iranitalab

entry.summary: UCVE frames compliance validation as a coverage problem over a structured requirement space, representing requirements as a compliance requirement graph and performing retrieval via spectral reranking over an RL-weighted Laplacian. Edge weights are learned through reinforcement learning with traversal rewards grounded in violation detection. This domain-agnostic approach targets a practically important problem that standard independent-requirement retrieval handles poorly.

entry.title: Coverage Under Contradiction: A Benchmark for Negation-Aware Retrieval

author.name: Pasha Abrishamchian, Eugene Yang, Andrew Yates, Nazli Goharian, Ophir Frieder

entry.summary: The authors augment a nugget-based coverage benchmark with controlled contradictions, creating negated counterparts of information nuggets and editing supporting documents so the corpus contradicts retriever parametric knowledge. This tests whether retrieval systems find corpus evidence when it conflicts with model priors. The negation-aware evaluation addresses a real robustness gap in retrieval evaluation.

entry.title: Right Click, Wrong Box: Grading GUI Grounding by What a Click Does

author.name: Xiaokang Yuan, Binhui Yao, Luwei Yang, Ruimin Chen, Zeng Wang

entry.summary: The paper critiques box-overlap evaluation in GUI grounding benchmarks like ScreenSpot-v2, noting that multiple interface elements can produce the same action outcome. It proposes an execution-based judge that fingerprints about a thousand clicks per page to build outcome maps, grading clicks by their functional effect rather than annotation boxes.

entry.title: ScIntBench: Physical Interaction Plausibility in 3D Scene Generation

author.name: Wendi Ying, Daochang Liu, Leonid Sigal, Ajmal Saeed Mian

entry.summary: ScIntBench is a benchmark that evaluates text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation on interaction-time physical reliability by executing manipulation actions in physics simulation and measuring success, progress, post-interaction integrity, and dynamic plausibility. Evaluating 12 state-of-the-art scene generation systems across 10 room types reveals shortcomings in interaction readiness. This shifts evaluation beyond static visual fidelity toward functional physical plausibility.

entry.title: Image Modeling: From Handcrafted Priors to Foundation Image Models

author.name: A. Murat Tekalp

entry.summary: This survey-style paper unifies six decades of image modeling, from handcrafted priors for inverse problems to modern deep foundation image models, under a common Bayesian framework where image modeling is probabilistic characterization of a data manifold. It frames restoration and generation as answering what makes an image look real via the prior density.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Phase Robot Loco-Manipulation via Phase-Conditioned Policy Optimization

author.name: Simone Manni, Annika Wollschl\"ager, Dario Bellicoso, Abel Gawel, Marco Hutter, Simon Le Cleac'h, Jan Br\"udigam

entry.summary: The authors extend PPO with a phase-conditioned critic, phase-gated rewards, and termination criteria to train a single policy for long-horizon multi-phase loco-manipulation tasks across diverse robot hardware. The approach avoids dependence on human motion data and humanoid-specific platforms.

entry.title: ExecDiffuser: Closing the Sample-to-Execution Gap in Diffusion Planning

author.name: Shuo Pei, Bosun Liang, Saihui Zha, Chen Sun, Huachun Tan, Yong Wang

entry.summary: ExecDiffuser addresses the mismatch between trajectory samples evaluated in diffusion planners and the single trajectory actually executed in closed-loop driving, showing that better proposals alone can worsen executed decisions. It couples candidate generation, selection, and replanning through shared execution semantics via intent-guided diffusion proposals and execution-grounded selection.

entry.title: GAWM: A Compact Latent World-Action Model for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yang Liu, Xiaoli Liu, Liuzhao Li, Yuduo Song, Muyuan Liu, Xiang Gao

entry.summary: GAWM is a compact multi-task world-action model that predicts future observations in the latent space of a frozen DINOv3 encoder, using a lightweight task-conditioned predictor over compressed per-view tokens. It avoids the high training cost and inference latency of billion-parameter video backbones while still encoding future spatial layout via dense patch-feature supervision.

entry.title: Generalizable Target-Less Joint Intrinsic-Extrinsic Camera-LiDAR Calibration using Deep Pixel-Point Correspondences

author.name: Simon Bultmann, Daniele Cattaneo, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: This work presents a fully automatic, target-less framework that jointly estimates camera intrinsics, radial-tangential distortion, and camera-LiDAR extrinsics from raw images and LiDAR scans. Prior learned calibration methods required pre-rectified images with known intrinsics; removing that requirement makes deployment far easier. This is a practical contribution for multi-modal perception systems.

entry.title: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance

author.name: Jianyu Hou, Jiawei Fu, Weikang Wan, Minghui Jiang, Jiajun Li, Hao Su

entry.summary: EgoThumb is an open-source supernumerary robotic thumb with a compact tendon-driven design whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, controlled by an imitation-learning policy mapping egocentric palm-camera images directly to joint commands. It enables single-handed hold-and-manipulate tasks that normally require two hands. The fully open-source release and vision-driven autonomy distinguish it from prior bulky, trigger-based devices.

entry.title: A big case study of propensity entanglement

author.name: nielsrolf

entry.summary: A link-post for a paper from a SPAR project studying how 24 elicited propensities generalize out-of-distribution, comparing predictors of SFT-induced spillover onto non-targeted traits. Surprisingly, assuming post-elicitation profiles drift toward the base model predicts spillover better than most targeted methods, suggesting weight changes partially undo post-training.

entry.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Ai2 blog post introducing Old Ideas, Novel Problems, a study testing how reliably LLMs judge the novelty of research ideas. The key finding is that small changes to the evaluation setup can produce very different novelty verdicts, casting doubt on the growing use of LLMs as automated reviewers or novelty judges.

entry.title: ADTGuard: Adaptive Depth-Time Safeguard for Streaming Inference in Large Language Models

author.name: Chuming Wei, Churui Yang, Zihan Zhang, Ruien Li, Wusheng Zhang, Yan Zhang, Guangwen Yang

entry.summary: ADTGuard guards streaming LLM inference by checking each token before release, progressively refining token-level training targets, and adapting which network layers safety signals are read from rather than using fixed-layer readouts. This addresses the gap where post-hoc moderation exposes users to harmful content mid-stream. It targets a practically important deployment safety problem.

entry.title: Who Knows What - and What Does It Support? Perspective-Bounded Evidence Calibration for Multimodal Theory of Mind

author.name: Ziqi Liao, Jiaqi Shen, Yiming Na, Kedi Lyu, Shao-Yuan Lo, Hongxia Xie

entry.summary: The paper identifies perspective leakage in multimodal Theory of Mind tasks, where LLM and Bayesian models incorrectly use agent-inaccessible events when inferring beliefs and intentions. It proposes an evidence calibration formulation that distinguishes objective events from agent-admissible evidence during hypothesis evaluation.

entry.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training

author.name: Ziyang Zeng, Tingyang Chen, Jia Deng, Qiyao Wang, Shuo Tang, Yike Yang, Tao Ren, Wayne Xin Zhao, Feng Chang, Jujie He, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: WorkFactory is a scalable framework that constructs coherent, executable professional tasks from professional intents using information-level planning with a support graph, plus probe executions that identify and repair support failures. It generated 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations for supervised training of working agents with expert demonstrations.

entry.title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis

author.name: Ruijia Niu, Kaiwen Liu, Rose Yu, Kristina Klinkner

entry.summary: EMMA addresses adapting LLM agents to specialized domains via structured episodic memory at the system level, defining explicit update rules for multi-agent evolution to avoid ill-scoped changes driven by backbone model preferences and to reduce cross-task interference. It targets complex workflows like multi-application navigation and data-pool analysis without costly parameter training. The work contributes to making agent self-improvement interpretable and scoped.

entry.title: When Connectivity Misleads: Guiding Agentic Search with Contrastive Evidence Paths

author.name: Junchen Li, Liang Xu, Rongzheng Wang, Qizhi Chen, Junhao Wen, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: This work identifies a failure mode in graph-based agentic search where highly connected distractor documents dominate Personalized PageRank-style rankings without offering better evidence. It proposes Contrastive Evidence Paths (CEP), which scores candidate sources by their strongest individual evidence paths rather than flat node scores, enabling better multi-hop exploration.

entry.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

author.name: Donghyeon Cho, Joowon Kim, Seungho Shin, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: Observes that in diffusion vision-language models, visual tokens comprise 89-97% of input yet image content changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of decoding steps on average (as low as 7.9%). It proposes LOWN, a certificate-guided routing method that skips image processing at steps where it is provably unnecessary, reducing compute without information loss.

entry.title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Miso Choi, Daekeun Kim, Eunji Kim, Jungbeom Lee

entry.summary: V-LUMEN extends embedding-level scaling via lookup memory to vision-language models, using a frozen codebook to discretize visual features, spatial-aggregation hashing for memory keys, text-conditioned relevance modulation, and gated residual fusion. This matters because it offers a route to expand VLM capacity without increasing model depth or dense computation.

entry.title: Spine: Compiling Subtask Trees into Structured Context for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Jiahong Xiang, Kunqiu Chen, Lingming Zhang, Yuqun Zhang

entry.summary: Spine is an interface and runtime for long-horizon coding agents that aligns model context with nested subtask structure: agents declare explicit subtask boundaries via work scopes so completed subtasks are isolated without either unbounded sequential history or recursive subagent delegation. This avoids context inflation and the overhead of conflating subtask granularity with agent choice.

entry.title: Representing the Unseen: Rethinking Visual Imagination for Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Zengqi Zhao, Zun Wang, Shoubin Yu, Mohit Bansal, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: This work questions the default of RGB imagery as the representation for imagined (unobserved) states in visual world models for spatial reasoning. It introduces ImagiRep, a simulator-grounded benchmark of 922 questions across seven question types, showing that different spatial questions benefit from different representations such as top-down geometry versus panoramic views.

entry.title: Exploratory creative pre-ranking: Hierarchical empirical-Bayes Thompson sampling for real-time creative optimization

author.name: Jiale Han, Ajith Moparthi, Dan Xie, Xiaowu Dai

entry.summary: This paper introduces a creative pre-ranker for dynamic creative optimization in advertising, using hierarchical empirical-Bayes Thompson sampling over a hierarchy of audience segment, item, campaign, and creative so cold creatives borrow strength from parent levels, with closed-form shrinkage from historical logs. It addresses sparse feedback and tight latency budgets in real-time ad serving.

entry.title: What Should an Information Bottleneck Encoder Learn? Separating Representation Learning from Rate Control

author.name: Hassan Tavakoli, Bella Bose

entry.summary: For jointly Gaussian data the information bottleneck solution factorizes so that information-bearing directions are independent of the compression multiplier, which acts only through scalar gains; the paper asks whether this separation of representation from rate control survives beyond Gaussian models, introducing a separation gap controlled by a sufficiency deficiency measure and treating the rate budget as a fixed operating parameter.

entry.title: Simulated petrological labels enable probabilistic mineralogy prediction from whole-rock geochemistry

author.name: Matthew J. Liu, Aaron D. Kaplan, Michael L. Whittaker, Kristin A. Persson

entry.summary: Tackles the one-to-many inverse problem of predicting rock mineralogy from whole-rock chemistry by simulating nearly one million petrological labels expressing multiple formation conditions per composition. These supervise the middle of a three-part model whose encoder is self-supervised on about 788,000 whole-rock measurements, enabling probabilistic mineralogy prediction at scale. Authors include researchers associated with major materials-science ML efforts (Persson group), lending credibility.

entry.title: Log-Derivative Trick for Parametric Markov Chains

author.name: Arthur Gall, Ichiro Hasuo, Thomas Seiller

entry.summary: Presents a scalable Monte Carlo gradient estimator for parametric Markov chains, applying a measure-theoretic log-derivative trick to optimize expected rewards and reachability probabilities. This avoids the symbolic gradient computation and global linear-system solves of prior parameter-lifting methods, enabling gradient-based synthesis without finite-horizon bias.

entry.title: Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Stochastic Motion Tokenization

author.name: Michael Drolet, Oleg Arenz, Jan Peters

entry.summary: Proposes using concise stochastic motion token representations, generatable by a high-level controller from a behavior label or text command, as detailed references for whole-body humanoid tracking policies.
