entry.summary: The author argues that AI safety work depends on strong conceptual reasoning — philosophy-like, hard-to-verify tasks relying on informal a priori argumentation — and that differentially accelerating this capability in AI systems is important and currently neglected by the safety community. The authors describe having pivoted from direct conceptual research to building capabilities in this area and claim a shovel-ready research agenda that can absorb more contributors, with a follow-up post planned.

entry.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent

author.name: Junlin He, Junzhang Zhu, Yudong Li, Yihong Tang, Xuefeng Jiang, Wei Ma, Chengxiang Zhuo, Zang Li

entry.summary: TGR-EvoDAG is a DAG-based multi-agent framework for evolving recommendation code at Tencent, addressing cost blindness and short-sighted evaluation in recursive self-improvement for module-cascaded generative recommendation pipelines. The DAG structure captures stage-asymmetric retraining overheads and preserves promising upstream innovations. It combines industrial deployment experience with LLM-driven algorithm discovery.

entry.title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior

author.name: Seungyong Moon, Deokjae Lee, Hansang Lee, Munkhtselmeg Battsengel, Youngin Kim, Seonghyeon Yun, Sungjin Jeon, SongEun Kim, Jeongmin Park, Hyun Oh Song

entry.summary: Learns a speed prior from large-scale robot demonstration data that predicts a distribution over execution speed along a motion path given instruction, path, and images, then uses a chosen quantile as a consistent clock to retime demonstrations. This removes operator-specific timing artifacts that policies would otherwise inherit, without per-task refitting or annotation.

entry.title: What the Query Remembers: Query Abstraction Governs Lexical and Dense Retrieval of Classical Arabic Poetry

author.name: Omar Farouk Zouak, Selma Mani, Larbi Said Chikh, Raid Abderrezak Ouahioune

entry.summary: Benchmarking nine dense encoders and BM25 on Classical Arabic poetry retrieval, the paper shows that retriever superiority is governed by how much verbatim wording the query retains: BM25 beats even an 8B state-of-the-art dense model on tip-of-the-tongue queries, but drops to near-last on abstract queries. Perturbing query wording confirms the ranking reflects query composition.

entry.title: SOPO: Socratic Guided Policy Optimization for Span-Level Hallucination Detection

author.name: Jiawei Dong, Zilong Bai, Pengtian zhu, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces SOPO, a multi-turn RL framework for span-level hallucination detection that addresses localization ambiguity, reward sparsity on hard examples, and length inflation in RLVR. Its key mechanism is Socratic feedback in which a teacher model guides reasoning trajectories during rollouts to improve detection robustness.

entry.title: Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction

author.name: Ziang Zhang, Wenyou Yi, Zehan Wang, Jiachen Xu, Xintong Han, Chunchao Guo, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes Easy-3Dfy, a compositional workflow for single-image 3D scene construction that decouples object generation from scene layout estimation, letting specialized 3D object generators and 3D foundation models exploit their respective strengths, with an RPF-based aligner bridging object-local meshes and partial scene pointmaps. This improves fine-grained geometry and asset quality over end-to-end approaches like SAM-3Dfy.

entry.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations

author.name: Sadra Emami, Benjamin Weigell, Mohammad Reza Mousavi, Gunel Jahangirova, Hugo Araujo, Bernhard Bauer

entry.summary: This empirical study challenges the assumption that LLM-optimized code reduces energy consumption, measuring hardware-level energy across 11 open-source models on all 1,000 EffiBench problems under four decoding configurations. It evaluates whether execution savings from self-refinement pipelines offset the energy cost of running the LLM optimization itself. The findings inform sustainable AI-assisted software engineering.

entry.title: A curated multi-endpoint drug-protein bioactivity dataset with construct-aware protein targets

author.name: Lina Abou-Abbas, Nour Mhanna, Hasan Bazzi, Sleiman El Hajj, Abdulkader Helwan, Rabah Omrani, Khadidja Henni

entry.summary: Curate-DTI is a construct-aware drug-protein bioactivity dataset built from the July 2026 BindingDB export, processing IC50, Ki, Kd and EC50 independently and pairing UniProt accessions with reported experimental sequences to preserve protein constructs that accession-only pipelines would merge. It comprises roughly 2.9M measurements across nearly 1.3M ligands and 9.7k sequence-defined protein entities.

entry.title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG

author.name: Robert Hogan, Sean R. Mathieson, Aurel Luca, Soraia Ventura, Sean Griffin, Geraldine B. Boylan, John M. O'Toole

entry.summary: U-NeXt is a semantic-segmentation framework for neonatal EEG event detection that uses a convolutional encoder-decoder over long input segments, trained across three large datasets totaling over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. One shared architecture handles low-voltage intervals, artifacts, and seizures, with evaluation on independent held-out seizure datasets.

entry.title: RADIANT: Object-Centric Feed-Forward Global Illumination

author.name: Sarah Zhang, Zhiyang Dou, Minghao Guo, Benjamin Tod Jones, Wojciech Matusik

entry.summary: RADIANT introduces an object-centric architecture for feed-forward neural rendering of global illumination, moving away from per-triangle tokenization whose quadratic attention scaling inflates compute without changing radiative transport physics. The design is discretization-agnostic and synthesizes illumination across novel 3D scenes without per-scene optimization or ray tracing.

entry.title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate

author.name: Raul C. S\^impetru, Amin Olamazadeh, Devon Rohlf, Vlad Cnejevici, Alessandro Del Vecchio

entry.summary: The paper shows that compact causal tokens from label-free EMG tokenizers preserve information for 3D hand-pose decoding while drastically reducing wireless transmission payload, evaluated on 320-channel EMG from nine participants with matched decoders. Tokenization changed mean decoding error by essentially zero (+0.01 mm for a SPAR-based tokenizer). This enables high-density wireless EMG interfaces without bandwidth bottlenecks.

entry.title: Recursive Semantic Divergence for LLM Agent Consistency

author.name: Harshavardhan Abichandani, Penny Chong, Atin Ghosh, Daniel Dahlmeier

entry.summary: The paper introduces Recursive Semantic Divergence (RSD), an unsupervised metric for measuring behavioral inconsistency of LLM tool-using agents across independent runs from identical states, capturing how inconsistency propagates across future turns rather than just single-response variability. The work addresses a reliability gap left by completion-based evaluation metrics.

entry.title: What Makes a Question Curious? Measuring Model Curiosity in Human-LLM Interactions

author.name: Angana Borah, Rachana Ramchandar, Inderjeet Nair, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: The authors introduce a theory-grounded taxonomy of model curiosity, distinguishing curiosity-oriented epistemic questions from generic questioning in human-LLM conversations. Across four datasets they find such questions are rare (17-28%) but associated with more exploratory, epistemically rich user responses, and a human study evaluates their usefulness. This reframes assistant quality as including the ability to ask good questions, not just answer well.

entry.title: Adaptive Retrieval, Selective Answers: Evaluating Conformal Factuality in Agentic RAG

author.name: Muhammad Aimal Rehman, Chi-Kuang Yeh

entry.summary: Evaluates claim-level conformal factuality filtering in agentic RAG, where an LLM policy adaptively issues follow-up retrieval queries or terminates retrieval before answering, across GPT-6 Luna and Llama 3.1 8B on HotpotQA, Natural Questions, and TriviaQA. Using many seeded calibration-test partitions and five conformal target levels, it studies how adaptive retrieval interacts with statistical factuality guarantees. Relevant to trustworthy retrieval-augmented systems.

entry.title: RAGing Against Misogyny: Improving Implicit Misogyny Explanations

author.name: Ivana Crescenzi, Arianna Muti, Maarten Sap, Tommaso Caselli, Debora Nozza

entry.summary: Proposes a RAG framework for detecting and explaining implicit misogyny in English and Italian, drawing on encyclopedic, slang, and feminist knowledge sources and evaluating on ImplicIT-Mis and SBIC+. RAG improves recall on ImplicIT-Mis but not SBIC+ detection, yet human evaluators prefer RAG-based explanations in both languages, with feminist sources contributing distinct value. Advances content moderation for subtle hate speech with attention to explanation quality.

entry.title: Prospect Theory in Large Language Models: A Meta-Analysis of Loss Aversion, Diminishing Sensitivity, and Probability Weighting

author.name: Adi Tarabeih

entry.summary: Meta-analyzes 102 fitted estimates from 11 studies covering 32 language models to test whether LLMs exhibit prospect theory's components as humans do. Finds modest loss aversion (pooled lambda of 1.26 vs. human 1.96), with diminishing sensitivity and probability weighting emerging differently across components.

entry.title: Grounding on Request: Learning Modality Control in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Maxime Dassen, Alexander Martin, Andrew Yates, Reno Kriz, William Walden

entry.summary: This work evaluates whether users can control which modality a VLM follows when image and caption conflict, using conflict-preserving counterfactual interventions with Flip and Stay metrics that distinguish evidence-following from lucky parametric answers. It extends neologism learning to introduce new words for visual and textual grounding, training only their embeddings while freezing the model.

entry.title: MIS-VQA: An Annotation-Driven Surgical Vision-Language Dataset for Complex Surgical Understanding

author.name: Mohamed Hamdy, Iheb Zouari, Fatmaelzahraa Ahmed, Muraam Abdel-Ghani, Muhammed Arsalan, Ponnuthurai Suganthan, Khalid Al-Jalham, Abdulaziz Al-Ali, Shidin Balakrishnan

entry.summary: The authors present MIS-VQA, a surgical vision-language dataset built from EndoVis18 and CholecT50 that converts phase, instrument, interaction, triplet, and segmentation annotations into structured textual scene representations for multimodal VQA. The dataset targets complex surgical understanding beyond single-task supervision, addressing gaps in template-based or sparsely annotated medical VQA resources.

entry.title: Linear Probes Transfer from Base to Distilled Language Models despite Rotation

author.name: Marios Tsatsos

entry.summary: This single-author study shows that linear probes trained to detect unsafe requests on base models (Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B) transfer, unchanged, to their DeepSeek-R1-distilled and instruction-tuned successors. Although the unsafe-safe separating direction rotates by 17-35 degrees, probes retain much of their effectiveness on XSTest.

entry.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access

author.name: Zetian Song, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Bohan Zhou, Bowen Ping, Yuqi Ye, Haocheng Tang, Haotian Zhang, Qizhe Wang, Shiyu Huang, Jiaqi Zhang, Siwei Ma, Wen Gao

entry.summary: Identifies decoding-efficiency bottlenecks when sequentially-optimized video codecs serve the random temporal sampling workloads of AI training, pinpointing sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reference-chain reconstruction as sources of decode amplification. The paper proposes storage formats that break cross-frame dependencies to improve random-access decoding without the storage blowup of independent JPEG frames or short GOPs.

entry.title: Support-guided OOD Removal with Diffusion

author.name: Alireza Kheirandish, Sara Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: Proposes SORD, an iterative diffusion-based algorithm recovering clean signals from observations corrupted by localized, unknown-distribution perturbations such as watermarks, shadows, or background noise, requiring only a binary corruption support map and a single pretrained diffusion model. No paired data or statistical model of the corruption is needed, demonstrated on natural images and faces.

entry.title: Patch-Derived or Register Tokens? Comparing Variable-Length Image Tokenizers

author.name: Philipp Schenkel, Tobias Sch\"urmann, Omer Sahin Tas

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares two variable-length image tokenization strategies for generative modeling: patch-derived tokens, which retain spatial organization and are computationally efficient, and register tokens, which lack predefined spatial layout. Patch-derived tokens win under extreme compression, register tokens are slightly better at intermediate budgets, and both converge at high budgets, with differing downstream generative behavior. This informs tokenizer design for autoregressive and diffusion-style image models.

entry.title: VTC-AUDIT: An Interventional Reliability Audit for Visual-Token Compression under Paired Image Shifts

author.name: Isaac (Rucheng), Li

entry.summary: VTC-AUDIT estimates incremental risk from visual-token compression by testing pairs where the uncompressed model is correct on both images but the compressed model fails under shift. It audits two training-free compressors across three 8-9B VLMs, four tasks, and eight pre-specified shifts using a four-arm interventional design.

entry.title: ToDoPro: Faster and Better Reference-Based Generation: Early Token Reduction via Downsampled Self-Probing

author.name: Caiyi Sun, Yujing Sun, Siu-Ming Yiu

entry.summary: ToDoPro accelerates reference-based image generation in Diffusion Transformers by reducing reference tokens early via a downsampled self-probing scheme, avoiding the O(N^2) token explosion from multiple reference images. Unlike prior approaches, it requires no external auxiliary models and reduces both compute and peak VRAM while preserving generation quality.

entry.title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Self-Supervised Representation Forcing for Few-Step Video Generation

author.name: Junyi Chen, Haiyu Zhang, Zhoujie Fu, Tengfei Wang, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: Identifies that Distribution Matching Distillation for few-step video generation relies solely on output-space objectives and degrades in spatial structure and temporal coherence as step counts shrink. Introduces a self-supervised representation forcing regularization on the student's internal representations to preserve fine-grained structure during aggressive distillation.

entry.title: Spectrally optimized implicit neural representations mitigate acquisition-related image quality trade-offs in intracranial 4D Flow MRI

author.name: Oliver Welin Odeback, Nerea Gonz\'alez-Aranceta, Sebasti\'an Jofre, Javier Bisbal, Edward Ferdian, Alistair A. Young, Pia Callmer, Sameer A. Ansari, Mia Bonini, David Nordsletten, Patrick Winter, Susanne Schnell, Tobias Granberg, Alexander Fyrdahl, David Marlevi

entry.summary: Presents an unsupervised, spectrally tuned implicit neural representation framework for super-resolution of intracranial 4D Flow MRI, avoiding the need for paired training data while remaining robust across anatomy and acquisition quality. This addresses resolution, acquisition time, and noise trade-offs in neurovascular imaging.

entry.title: WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU

author.name: Bingnan Liu, Ruini Xue

entry.summary: Addresses memory limits of interactive world models on consumer hardware, showing that KV retrieval memory for Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of bf16 video and demonstrating the access set is predictable from camera pose. WorldPager uses an analytical spill model to enable zero-stall tiered memory across a single RTX 4090, host memory, and NVMe SSD for long-horizon sessions.

entry.title: Functional Superoscillations in a Wave Processor

author.name: Yuntian Wang, Md Sadman Sakib Rahman, Aydogan Ozcan

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate optical processing of superoscillatory functions in a diffractive wave processor, where a scalar argument is encoded on a wavefront and the processor synthesizes function outputs in parallel, with frequencies not bound by diffraction limits in the usual transverse sense. This reframes superoscillation as an input-output functional dependence rather than a predetermined field pattern.

entry.title: Memory-Aware Keyframe Management for Dense Maps on Memory-Constrained Robots

author.name: Huichang Yun, Jaeyeul Kim, Seungho Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes bounding dense-map memory directly in bytes rather than keyframe counts, with pre-computed per-keyframe resident sizes known before admission, for robots running language models and dense 3D maps on one shared-memory device. This prevents out-of-memory failures and improves admission decisions over pose-radius or fixed-cell schemes.

entry.title: From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes

author.name: Diana Cerdas-Vargas, Alejandro Romero, Richard J. Duro

entry.summary: This paper explores using LLMs and VLMs as cultural enablers to align open-ended learning robots with human purposes: natural-language human goals are translated into motivational components (missions and drives) inside the robot architecture, guiding self-generated skills and goals. It addresses the alignment problem for developmental autonomous agents rather than task-specified robots. The framing is conceptual with an implemented multimodal process.

entry.title: MetaARIMA: Configuration-Level Transfer Learning for ARIMA Models

author.name: Vitor Cerqueira, Ricardo In\'acio, Carlos Soares

entry.summary: Proposes MetaARIMA, a metalearned pretrained policy that selects ARIMA configurations by learning from historical experiments which configurations achieve top-quantile performance on new series, bringing transfer learning to classical forecasting at the configuration level. This counters the practice of configuring ARIMA independently per series with heuristic in-sample criteria.

entry.title: GoCo: structure-guided conformal calibration for error-controlled Gene Ontology annotation release

author.name: Chong Wang, Yongzhao Shao, Peng Liu

entry.summary: GoCo calibrates scores from existing gene-function predictors into released Gene Ontology annotations while certifying hierarchy-aware gene-level false discovery control, constructing a nested release path under the same asymptotic guarantee. Applied to co-essentiality modules, it offers the first explicit error-controlled calibration framework for GO annotation at scale.

entry.title: Inference for Causal Path-Specific Effects in Longitudinal Studies with Repeated Treatments and Multiple Mediators

author.name: Xiaxian Ou, Xinwei He, Razieh Nabi

entry.summary: This work develops semiparametric inference for path-specific causal effects in longitudinal settings where treatments recur and the number, type, and ordering of mediators vary over time. Under standard causal assumptions plus cross-world restrictions, path-specific means are identified via the edge g-formula, and the authors derive two parameterizations of the efficient influence function enabling estimation. This is a meaningful extension of mediation analysis to complex longitudinal structures.

entry.title: Behaviour analysis for large language model-driven agents

author.name: Tianqiang Yan, Lizhen Qu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a general framework for analyzing language-agent behavior that connects data-driven behavioral discovery with interpretable hypotheses, statistical testing in held-out contexts, and perturbation experiments such as prompt steering. A case study of iterative self-reflection illustrates the framework's use.

entry.title: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets? Experience Reuse in Molecular Optimization for Agentic Structure-Based Drug Design

author.name: Zaifei Yang, Weiyu Chen, Yaqing Wang, James Kwok

entry.summary: Investigates whether experience bases from agentic structure-based drug design, where LLM agents probe protein pockets with controlled edits and docking, can transfer across pockets. Using full logs over CrossDocked2020 test pockets, it analyzes which record properties (keys) recur and govern pooling and lookup of past editing experience.

entry.title: Rethinking Structured Generation: Can Graph-Based Reasoning Resolve Ambiguity?

author.name: Ratun Rahman, Atit Pokharel

entry.summary: The paper reframes structured generation as an ambiguity-aware inference problem, arguing that the standard deterministic input-to-single-output formulation suppresses semantically valid alternative structures. It adopts graph-based reasoning over sets of plausible outputs to handle underspecified inputs more stably.

entry.title: MI-MIDI 2: From Observation to Control with Sparse Autoencoders in Text-to-MIDI Generation

author.name: Jakub Po\'cwiardowski, Mateusz Modrzejewski

entry.summary: This work builds an end-to-end protocol for discovering and validating sparse-autoencoder features in text-to-MIDI models (text2midi and MIDI-LLM), testing whether SAE feature interpretations actually predict controllability of musical outputs. Each characterization method is paired with its own control, addressing the known unreliability of SAE interpretation evidence.

entry.title: Representation Learning via Composite Subspace Flow Matching

author.name: Jos\'e Afonso, M\'ario Figueiredo

entry.summary: Proposes composite subspace flow matching (CSFM), which formulates representation learning as variance-minimizing inversion of a deterministic degradation curriculum across spectral, color, and illumination subspaces, instead of corrupting data with isotropic noise. The goal is to bridge joint-embedding methods that discard too much variance and generative models that preserve pixels but obscure semantics.

entry.title: Beyond Copying: Lifelong Smart Contract Security Task Construction via Protocol Mutation

author.name: Zifan Peng, Peng Huang, Jingyi Zheng, Yingjie Xue, Xuechao Wang, Xinlei He, Xia Hu, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: CONSTRAINTDIAL is a framework for automatically generating smart contract security benchmark tasks via protocol mutation, using local contract reconstruction and attack execution to validate that tasks remain exploitable while defeating memorized answers. It addresses benchmark contamination where agents reward copied attack code from public blockchain transactions. The context includes roughly $38.6 billion in ecosystem losses reported by SlowMist.

entry.title: Multiplicative vs. Additive State Coupling in Learned Optimizer Schedules

author.name: M. Harper Langston, Pierre-David Letourneau, Dalton Jones, Roland Memisevic, Peter Scott, Mingu Lee, Richard A. Lethin, Christopher Lott, Fatih Porikli, Harris Teague

entry.summary: This paper studies learned schedules for a continuous relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver, comparing state-blind, state-adaptive bilinear (multiplicative), and additive coupling of model state. The bilinear schedule generalizes out of distribution while a statistically matched additive ablation fails, suggesting multiplicative state coupling is key. Findings persist across a 30-value weight-decay sweep.

entry.title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?

author.name: Sachin Konan, Jonathan Liu, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: PaperScorer is a family of models predicting peer-review accept/reject decisions from paper text or page screenshots, trained with author identity and formatting shortcuts removed. Vision-based models are most predictive (68% on ICLR, 77% on arXiv ML papers), beating text-only and frontier reasoning models, raising questions about how much review decisions reduce to content signals. It offers a quantitative probe into the peer-review process relevant to automated research evaluation.

entry.title: Cautious Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient Methods

author.name: Damian Hattler, Qiang Liu, Nils Thuerey

entry.summary: The paper addresses gradient conflicts among competing loss terms in PINN training, improving the Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient (ConFIG) method so it remains stable when combined with adaptive optimizers like Adam. The authors identify a vulnerability introduced by optimizer preconditioning of the conflict-free direction and propose a cautious variant.

entry.title: DBCM: Dual-Branch Calibration Module for Test-Time Adaptation in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jaebyeong Jeon, Kunwoo Kang, Sang Yup Lee, Kibok Lee

entry.summary: The paper observes that forecast residuals in time series forecasting exhibit substantial shared structure across channels, contradicting the fully channel-wise adapters used in prior test-time adaptation work. DBCM introduces a dual-branch calibration module around frozen forecasters that exploits both shared and channel-specific residual structure, updated incrementally from test-time observations.

entry.title: Contextual Decision Making: Predictive or Generative

author.name: L. Jeff Hong, Weihuan Huang, Xinyao Li

entry.summary: This theory paper compares predict-then-optimize and generate-then-optimize approaches to contextual decision making, deriving regret bounds showing how smoothness differences can offset generative modeling's dimensional burden and proving lower bounds limiting gains within nonnegative-weight PtO methods. It gives principled guidance on when each paradigm is preferable.

entry.title: On the Limits of Sparse Linear Model with Shuffled Differential Privacy

author.name: Yan Zhang, Jiong Tuo, Meng Ding, Yuheng Ma, Di Wang

entry.summary: This paper establishes lower bounds for sparse linear regression under shuffled differential privacy, showing any non-interactive protocol incurs an l2 estimation error of Omega(sqrt(dk)/(n*epsilon)), exposing a dimensionality barrier. It also analyzes interactive protocols, mapping out the gap between central and local DP models in the shuffled regime.

entry.title: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control

author.name: Muhammad Zeeshan Karamat, Syed Talal Hassan, Christiana Chamon Garcia

entry.summary: Using a frozen Qwen3-VL-4B (an existing model), the paper localizes safety-sensitive representations across layers, finding non-uniform safety geometry: early vision layers support strong bidirectional refusal control via activation steering, while later layers respond to magnitude scaling with a substantial safety-selectivity trade-off. The framework requires no retraining or parameter modification.

entry.title: PROVE: Probabilistic Visual Grounding via Patch-Level Evidence for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mayank Nautiyal, Tianru Zhang, Li Ju, Ekta Vats, Prashant Singh

entry.summary: PROVE is a post-hoc evidential adapter that maps frozen CLIP patch features to per-patch Beta distributions, casting visual grounding as evidence accumulation so a query can match zero, one, or many patches. Unlike deterministic relevance maps, it indicates localization reliability and whether the referent is present. This addresses a real reliability gap in vision-language grounding.

entry.title: Entity-Aware Evaluation of OCR Systems for Historical Document Transcription

author.name: Camilo Mari\~no (UDELAR, CB), Diego Belzarena (UDELAR, CB), Marina Gardella (CB), Ignacio Ram\'irez (UDELAR), Gregory Randall (UDELAR), Jean-Michel Morel (LU - Hong Kong)

entry.summary: The paper argues that Character Error Rate poorly reflects whether meaningful information like names, dates, and identifiers is preserved in historical OCR, and proposes entity-level error analysis as a complementary evaluation. Using 175 documents from the Berrutti Archive with 5,209 manually annotated entity mentions, it compares sequence-recognition OCR, OCR-specialized VLMs, and general-purpose VLMs.

entry.title: EviGround-CT: Sentence-to-Volume Grounding for Verifying LLM-Generated Chest CT Reports

author.name: Ziyuan Li, Juncheng Ni, Feng Li

entry.summary: EviGround-CT verifies LLM-generated chest CT reports after generation by extracting positive-finding sentences and using a 3D grounding model to predict an evidence mask per sentence, retaining anatomical location and laterality in the grounding query. Sentence-grounded verification raises evidence-supported precision from 0.263 to 0.365 across 137 in-scope findings on CT-RATE and a ReXGroundingCT subset.

entry.title: Hey, guess what: CUES lead to inferences about typicality

author.name: Alison Chi, Sanghyeok Choi, Hannah Rohde, Emily Allaway

entry.summary: Constructs two new corpora (EventTyp, EventTypGold) and runs large-scale human and LLM experiments on how people infer typicality from conversational cues like commonsense knowledge, emphasis, and snark. Finds that LLMs generally lack the commonsense knowledge needed to assess event typicality the way humans do.

entry.title: Small Edits, Shifting Decisions: Benchmarking LLM Accuracy and Reliability on French Input Variants

author.name: Jiaming Yu, Xiaotian Xie, Jian Ma, Yingjie Li

entry.summary: Builds a controlled French benchmark of 4,200 original-low-high perturbation triplets across seven tasks (12,600 instances) covering apostrophe, diacritic, and typo variants. Shows accuracy drops and calibration (Brier, NLL) degrades with perturbation intensity, with larger models more accurate but not necessarily better calibrated.

entry.title: TriageRAG: Failure-Aware Self-Training for Adapting Retrieval-Augmented Language Models to Specialized Domains

author.name: Samarth Varshney, Ritu Yadav

entry.summary: TriageRAG improves self-training for domain adaptation of RAG systems by triaging retained synthetic examples: it asks whether the student already knows the answer, extracts it correctly from context, or fails, and whether failures stem from the reader or retriever. This contrasts with prior approaches like SimRAG that treat all retained examples identically. The work targets adaptation to specialized domains such as medicine with only an unlabeled corpus.

entry.title: The LALA Benchmark: Evaluating Literary and Linguistic Analysis in LLMs

author.name: Michael Foster, Barbara McGillivray, Gard B. Jenset, Jakub M\'acha, Jason Harding, Marcus Perlman, Devyani Sharma, Patrick Skeels, Jana Willer-Gold, Jeannette Littlemore

entry.summary: LALA is a benchmark of 236 open-ended expert-written questions in linguistics and literary studies with expert-provided ideal answers, administered to 17 models and judged by both human experts and two LLM judges (Sol and Qwen). Base models show little of the assessed linguistic competence while post-trained versions perform substantially better, enabling analysis of what post-training contributes to humanistic analytical skill. It fills a gap in evaluating deep domain competence outside STEM and code.

entry.title: CoLink: Global Compression and Knowledge Linking for Multi-Turn Dialogue Modeling

author.name: Lian Yan, Zhenbo Xia, Haotian Wang, Chen Tang, Yi Guan, Jie Liu, Jingchi Jiang

entry.summary: CoLink improves LLM handling of long-horizon dialogues by clustering history into topic graphs that link cross-semantic associations, followed by global compression of conversation context. It is motivated by cognitive-science views of dialogue as sense-making and memory association, targeting information loss and myopic attention in current methods.

entry.title: Semantic Atoms for Scalable Text Analysis in Data Analytics in the Era of LLM-Based Agents

author.name: Jinxiang Xie, Zihao Li, Rui Ding, Bartuer Zhou, Shi Han, Dongmei Zhang

entry.summary: Defines TADA (Text Analysis in Data Analytics) workloads where LLM-based semantic processing of text columns interleaves with SQL/Python operations in agentic analytics pipelines. The paper proposes two query-driven semantic atoms that decide which work should be neural versus symbolic and enable reuse of semantic outputs across steps. This is relevant to scalable hybrid neuro-symbolic data analytics systems, likely from a Microsoft-affiliated team.

entry.title: Synthetic Child-Adult Interactions Are Not Developmentally Plausible

author.name: Bastian Bunzeck, Francesca Padovani

entry.summary: Compares the synthetic TinyDialogues dataset to natural child-adult dialogue across broad linguistic measures, finding that synthetic data matches lexical statistics but drastically underestimates the messy, fragmented nature of real spoken interaction. The authors propose instruction-tuning on data derived from real dialogues and show in a pilot that a small parameter-efficient model better approximates natural statistical tendencies. A caution for using synthetic data in developmentally plausible language modeling.

entry.title: Beyond Words Alone: Disentangling Distributed Evidence for Visually Grounded Cultural Translation

author.name: Dingming Li, Yiwen Qiu, Linjuan Wu, Hongxing Li, Zixuan Wang, Xinze Lyu, Ye Guo, Daoxin Zhang, Zhe Xu, Weiming Lu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Culture-MMT is a diagnostic benchmark of 498 curated social-media instances requiring evidence distributed across text, images, and cultural knowledge, categorized as Symbol, Visual, or Hybrid evidence types. The authors also develop a human-aligned domain-specific judge to disentangle whether translation errors stem from missing visual evidence or inadequate cultural adaptation.

entry.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR

author.name: Yuchen Zhang, Haralambos Mouratidis, Ravi Shekhar

entry.summary: Studies expanding connector-based Speech LLM ASR to new languages without forgetting source languages or replaying source data, evaluating target-update construction and merging strategies. Finds SSU-Wanda+TIES merging gives the best source-preserving trade-off in single-target expansion, while update merging is more stable in multi-target cases.

entry.title: PathKGen: Pathology Knowledge Assisted MLLM for Explainable Histopathology

author.name: Nadun Rajapaksha, Sandun Herath, Devnith Wijesinghe, Isiri Amani Withanawasam, Hasindri Watawana, Ranga Rodrigo

entry.summary: PathKGen injects knowledge-graph-derived structured pathology knowledge into multimodal LLMs for whole-slide-image analysis, making the reasoning component visible and interpretable for histopathology report generation. This addresses the black-box reasoning and limited parametric knowledge of MLLMs in clinical settings.

entry.title: Intuition with Evidence: Adaptive Dual Memory for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Qiuhe Hong, Jingya Wang, Cuzhen Geng, Shenyao Peng, Munan Ning, Yuyang Liu, Yonghong Tian

entry.summary: The authors propose a dual-memory framework for multimodal agents combining a model-native latent memory as an intuitive prior with a multi-indexed episodic memory for exact evidence reconstruction via retrieval-conditioned joint alignment. This unifies internalized experience with fine-grained recall for sustained multimodal interactions.

entry.title: Aerial-R1: Reinforcing Aerial Reasoning and Segmentation in MLLMs

author.name: Jisheng Dang, Huaiyuan Peng, Yixuan Wang, Kun Wang, Zhang Li, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Aerial-R1 is the first framework to reinforce visual reasoning for aerial imagery in multimodal LLMs, drawing on DeepSeek-R1-style reasoning-incentivizing mechanisms and using cross-view consistency as a signal for trustworthy perception. It targets hallucination problems caused by extreme scale variation and ambiguity in aerial scenes, where SFT leads to blind guessing on tiny objects.

entry.title: PhaseBreak: Proactive Temporal Protection against Unauthorized Image-to-Video Animation

author.name: Jiashu Zhang, Xuanyou Li, Qixin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes PhaseBreak, a white-box spectral retiming protection that lets image owners apply bounded, imperceptible perturbations disrupting downstream image-to-video diffusion animation of their photos. Its key insight is that generated dynamics depend on the temporal ordering of feature events, not just their strength, enabling spatially localized and subtle motion disruption beyond global spectral attenuation.

entry.title: Fast Instinct, Slow Reason: A Dual-Speed Agentic Framework for Self-Configuring Multi-Object Tracking in Satellite Video

author.name: Fan He, Baining Wu, Yan Li, Xiaoyang Zeng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a dual-speed agentic framework pairing an offline-compiled fast instinct with slow LLM-style reasoning for self-configuring multi-object tracking in satellite video, instantiated as the AUSPEX algorithm for arbitrating unlabelled tracker-configuration shortlists. It enables onboard tracker adaptation within observation windows of tens of seconds without relabelling or retraining detectors. This addresses a genuine gap in autonomous Earth-observation systems.

entry.title: Rethinking Microscopy Generation: Co-Designed Diffusion for Biologically Interpretable Single-Cell Synthesis

author.name: Shumpei Takezaki, Duway Nicolas Lesmes-Leon, Ryoma Bise, Gillian Lovell, Bianca Migliori, Andreas Dengel, Sheraz Ahmed

entry.summary: This work recasts microscopy image generation at the single-cell level with BioVAE, an encoder-decoder diffusion model whose latent space is explicitly aligned with named, measurable semantic cell axes such as size, elongation, and texture. Co-designing input controls and internal representation yields biologically interpretable controllable synthesis. It matters for generating biologically meaningful training data and hypothesis testing in cell biology.

entry.title: End-to-end prostate lesion segmentation and detection from undersampled diffusion-weighted MRI

author.name: Lukas T. Rotkopf, Marco Schlimbach, Kevin Kr\"{o}ninger, Stefan O. Schoenberg, Heinz-Peter Schlemmer, Jens Kleesiek, Moritz Rempe

entry.summary: VarNet-Seg is an end-to-end network that combines a k-space variational network with an image-space 3D segmentation U-Net to perform prostate lesion segmentation directly from complex multicoil undersampled DWI data and coil sensitivity information, evaluated on 269 fastMRI prostate exams with voxel-level annotations. Bypassing conventional reconstruction keeps acquisition information that image-only pipelines discard. This could improve clinically deployable lesion detection at reduced scan time.

entry.title: Road Infrastructure Perception for Autonomous Driving: Taxonomy, Representations, Tasks, and Challenges

author.name: Guoyang Zhao, Weiqing Qi, Kai Zhang, Zhihai Bi, Tianshuai Hu, Zeying Gong, Dezong Zhao, Jun Ma

entry.summary: This survey provides a function-oriented synthesis of road infrastructure perception for autonomous driving, organizing work into geometric-structural, functional-spatial, and regulatory-semantic categories across lane detection, drivable-space estimation, traffic-sign recognition, and online mapping. It unifies a fragmented field around task definitions, representations, datasets, and evaluation protocols. Valuable as a reference for researchers and practitioners.

entry.title: Grounded Exploration for Open-Ended Image Editing

author.name: Jieyu Zhou, Mehdi Ben Ayed, Shubham Gupta, Zhenyu Tan, Jiajing Xu, Dmitry Kislyuk, Eric Tzeng, Christopher J. MacLellan, Charles Rosenberg

entry.summary: This paper, with industry authors including Eric Tzeng and Charles Rosenberg (eBay), proposes a two-stage framework for open-ended image-editing requests that first identifies diverse feasible edit scopes and then realizes them as executable instructions. It achieves 24.6% higher semantic dispersion and 17.1% higher groundedness than direct diversity prompting across 300 tasks. Addresses a real gap between underspecified user intent and generative variation.

entry.title: Fovea-JEPA: Overcoming Geometric Blind Spots in V-JEPA for Camera Motion Recognition

author.name: Xiangkun Shi, Hanhui Li, Shiyue Zhang, Chang Liu, Junwen Pan, Zhenbang Sun, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: This work shows that V-JEPA-style joint-embedding predictive architectures underrepresent geometric cues needed for camera motion recognition, exhibiting geometric blind spots where performance degrades under temporal-reversal supervision. Fovea-JEPA identifies and addresses these underrepresented regions, improving robustness across camera motion families.

entry.title: EditDistill: Is It Possible to Guide Video Editing with Image Editing?

author.name: Guojun Lei, Hong Li, Hongbing Yang, Lixue Gong, Chi Wang, Zheng Dong

entry.summary: Proposes EditDistill, a framework that applies an off-the-shelf image editor to the first video frame, distills the resulting transformation into a compact edit descriptor, and uses it to guide consistent video editing. This targets precise local edits, temporal effects, and cross-frame lighting consistency.

entry.title: Learning Dual-Camera Smooth Zoom via Decoupled Geometric-Photometric Data Synthesis

author.name: Junjie Fan, Zhilu Zhang, Renlong Wu, Dazhi Zhang, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: The paper defines the dual-camera smooth zoom task for smartphones, synthesizing continuous intermediate frames between cameras with mismatched perspective and color rendition. ZoomGS v2 generates high-fidelity training data by decoupling geometric and color transformations from 3D scene representations, sidestepping the impossibility of capturing real ground-truth zoom sequences.

entry.title: Understanding and Repairing Cooperative Perception under Adverse Weather

author.name: Mengxu Ma (Northwestern Polytechnical University)

entry.summary: This is presented as the first controlled study of how weather-induced exterior context changes degrade cooperative 3D detection even when LiDAR points on annotated objects are unchanged, termed Weather-Induced Context Interference. Restoring object-neighborhood features recovers 30 of 31 induced failures on real roadside inputs, and the failure reproduces across a second fusion model, motivating repair mechanisms.

entry.title: HiFiPix: Bringing High-Fidelity Real-World Super-Resolution Back to Pixel Space

author.name: Wenjie Li, Du Chen, Hui Wang, Linlong Fan, Youwei Lv, Zeyi Chen, Zehan Chen, Jinwei Chen, Heng Guo, Zhanyu Ma, Qingnan Fan

entry.summary: Proposes HiFiPix, a pixel-space diffusion framework for real-world image super-resolution that avoids fidelity loss from VAE latent compression. It suppresses patch boundary artifacts by penalizing unrealistic high-frequency periodic components with a cross-scale mechanism, achieving ultra high-fidelity reconstruction with fine-grained generative detail.

entry.title: Benchmarking Obstacle-Conditioned Safety in Household Robot Navigation

author.name: Hyunwoong Bae, Jisu Han, Jiyeon Choi, Dohoon Kim, Taesup Moon

entry.summary: Introduces OSMA-Bench, which uses spatially matched scenario sets differing only in obstacle type to test whether robots modulate clearance and speed according to obstacle semantics, plus a Semantic Sensitivity Index metric. Evaluations find that neither VLM-based nor VLA policies consistently adapt their motion to obstacle caution levels.

entry.title: Understanding the Co-evolutionary Solution Exchange of the MOEA/D: Already the Smallest Communication Radius Gives the Best-Possible Speed-Up

author.name: Benjamin Doerr, Moaad Elmoutassim, Martin S. Krejca, Guy Mushiata Kibulu

entry.summary: The authors provide the first mathematical runtime analysis of solution exchange among subproblems in the mutation-based MOEA/D on the OneMinMax benchmark, varying the communication radius r. They find the smallest communication radius already achieves the best-possible speed-up, clarifying when co-evolutionary communication actually helps.

entry.title: MDPO: Multi-constraint Dexterous Policy Optimization with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ao Zhou, Zongyou Yu, Ke Wu, Tao Xu, Junqiao Zhao, Wenchao Ding, Alois Knoll, Guang Chen

entry.summary: MDPO extends constrained RL to dexterous manipulation by handling multiple heterogeneous safety constraints simultaneously, including joint limits, unsafe finger configurations, arm collisions, and unstable object interactions, going beyond the cumulative-cost focus of prior constrained RL methods.

entry.title: HARP: Handoff-Aware Recovery Planning for Active Target Acquisition in Multi-UAV Handoff

author.name: Heegyeong Kim, Alice James, Avishkar Seth, Endrowednes Kuantama, Richard Han

entry.summary: HARP is a recovery planner for multi-UAV target tracking handoffs, registering bounded sender predictions in the receiver's map, distinguishing field-of-view failure from occlusion, and generating failure-specific viewpoint trajectories checked against clearance, observability, and deadline constraints. It enables receivers lacking prior target observations to actively acquire usable views without disrupting coverage.

entry.title: Localization-Uncertainty-Aware UAV Swarm Search for GNSS-Denied Maritime Surveillance

author.name: Siyuan Yang, Junning Lyu, Xiaoyu He, Lakmal Seneviratne, Shaoming He

entry.summary: This work proposes an uncertainty-aware control barrier function framework for UAV swarm search in GNSS-denied maritime environments, approximating cascading localization covariance through Fisher information matrices. The covariance model captures how ranging noise and neighbor uncertainty accumulate along multi-hop localization chains, and uncertainty-tightened CBFs enforce connectivity maintenance and collision avoidance with conditional invariance guarantees. It handles uncertainty propagation rigorously in a practically important setting.

entry.title: MATE-BT: A Behavior-Tree-Based Framework for Hierarchically Decentralized Mission Autonomy in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Teams

author.name: Sunbeen Lee, Hoseon Gi, Jik Hur, Inmo Jang

entry.summary: MATE-BT is a hierarchically decentralized multi-robot framework separating mission execution, allocation, and task execution, with an onboard leader whose authority transfers on failure and behavior trees governing local robot behavior. Webots simulations and real-robot experiments demonstrate mission continuity under runtime changes and robot failures. It is a practical robustness framework for heterogeneous teams.

entry.title: TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains

author.name: Elias Hofele, Thomas Trapp, David Timmermann, Tristan Schnell, Georg Heppner, Arne Roennau

entry.summary: TrySee is a modular closed-loop robot task planning pipeline that couples general-purpose VLM reasoning with domain-specific perception preprocessing for online grounding, requiring no VLM fine-tuning or end-to-end demonstrations. A dynamic preprocessing selection mechanism supports scalability across specialized domains. It targets the known weakness of VLMs in niche visual domains relevant to robotics.

entry.title: Online Covariance Estimation for Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent on Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Jingrong Guan, Liwei Jiang, Sen Na

entry.summary: Develops online covariance estimators for averaged Riemannian SGD enabling statistical inference when parameters lie on manifolds, using vector transport to handle varying tangent spaces across iterations. The overlapping and non-overlapping batch-means estimators are online and memory-efficient, supporting asymptotically valid inference for Riemannian optimization.

entry.title: Not All Mislabels Are Equal: Efficient Task-Aware Auditing with Confidence Sequences

author.name: Fangyuan Lin, Noah Krever, Jakub \v{C}ern\'y, Lily Xu

entry.summary: The ATLAS framework couples anytime-valid confidence sequences with a task-aware adaptive policy that prioritizes which dataset labels to audit based on uncertainty and downstream-score sensitivity, motivated by biodiversity-credit verification. For linear scores it certifies label error rates to within two percentage points while reducing required inspections.

entry.title: Constrained Gradient Equilibrium: Approachability under Locally Constrained Adversaries

author.name: Kaicheng Zhang, Lujing Zhang, Yifei Pang, Yuxiao Wen, Zhun Deng, Yanjun Han

entry.summary: The authors extend the gradient equilibrium (GEQ) framework in online learning to settings where the learner faces constraints, showing constrained GEQ can be impossible even with simple constraints. They then build a Blackwell-style approachability characterization for CGEQ under locally constrained adversaries and derive an algorithmic principle for converting existing methods. This advances the theory of when adversarial equilibrium concepts survive realistic restrictions.

entry.title: LUCID: Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with Conditional Density Estimation

author.name: Yixiao Wang, Srikar Katta, Jon Donnelly, Emanuele Borgonovo, Cynthia Rudin

entry.summary: LUCID introduces a model-agnostic local variable importance metric and estimator that uses conditional density estimation to respect feature dependence when perturbing inputs, avoiding unrealistic counterfactuals that plague naive permutation-based importance. Authored by a team including Cynthia Rudin, it improves the reliability of local explanations. Better local importance measures support trustworthy model interpretation in high-stakes settings.

entry.title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves

author.name: Garima Agrawal, Prasun Das, Akshay Sarvade, Priyanka L, Minisha N, Sravani Joshna, Hemath Manivannan, Lavanya Korada, Sambhrit Pattanayak, Srashti Gupta, Siddu R, Prasad Kalyanasundaram

entry.summary: Describes an enterprise system in which a seven-agent pipeline reverse-engineered behavioral logic from 241 repositories across 18 services, and a knowledge layer organizes recovered rules by service and operational context before retrieval. This prevents flat vector retrieval from returning near-identical rules from the wrong service in multi-agent workflows.

entry.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection

author.name: Luke Beddow, George Mavroghenis, Rodrigo Chacon Quesada, Kamil Dreczkowski, Cong Sun, Jiankai Wang, Oscar Kwong-Fai Pang, Antoine Cully

entry.summary: AWARE is a world-model framework for detecting anomalies in robotic systems using only external camera monitoring, via system dynamics estimation and state prediction, avoiding reliance on onboard sensors unavailable on legacy hardware. Evaluated on 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories including payload collisions and motor degradations, it improves anomaly classification by 26%. This has direct value for safety in industrial automation.

entry.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning

author.name: Yuhan Liu, Lianhui Qin, Shenji Wan

entry.summary: SceneBloom is an agentic framework for generating simulation-ready indoor environments, combining diffusion-based hierarchical layout sampling within functional zones with contract-guided 3D compilation that performs geometric fitting and pose correction. It targets realistic and diverse training scenes for embodied agents across five room types. It bridges visual generative priors and physically valid 3D scene construction.

entry.title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation

author.name: Vigneshwaran Subbaraju, Obaidullah Zaland, Monowar Bhuyan

entry.summary: This position-style paper examines the intersection of vision-language-action policy adaptation from human interventions and federated learning across robots, arguing that shared updates improving mean success can suppress rare safety interventions or produce unsafe behavior on other embodiments. It articulates three requirements: preserving context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections, per-robot assessment of candidate updates, and safety-sensitive aggregation. It frames an important open problem in robot learning safety.

entry.title: SLICE-Mem: Salience-Gated Lightweight Information Curation for Efficient LLM Agent Memory

author.name: Xiaobin Chen, Dian Jin, Lin Shu, Defeng Sun, Xiaoming Tao

entry.summary: SLICE-Mem is a lightweight LLM agent memory framework using a compact salience classifier to decide which user turns to retain and a semantic-dependency-based extractor to produce concise memory entries, requiring no generative LLM calls during the online pipeline. Offline consolidation handles cross-entry reconciliation, and evaluation on Memora and LongMemEval-S with 8B models shows competitive memory quality at much lower cost.

entry.title: Self-Evolution Reasoner: Continuous Optimization via Policy-Intrinsic Exploration and Exploitation

author.name: Wenhang Shi, Yiren Chen, Zhe Zhao, Jinhao Dong, Wei Lu, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: SEPO addresses exploration bottlenecks in RLVR and self-supervised on-policy distillation by driving continuous reasoning improvement through policy-intrinsic exploration and exploitation, avoiding reliance on off-policy external demonstrations. It aims to escape local optima when the policy fails to sample valid solutions.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Towards a Universal Latent Space for Computational Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Dibaloke Chanda, Praveen Madiraju

entry.summary: MOSAIC systematically studies latent-space similarity, alignment, and interoperability across 12 patch-level and 6 slide-level pathology foundation models, quantifying how architecture, pretraining objective, depth, and magnification shape latent geometry. It evaluates strategies for mapping independently learned representations into a common space, probing whether PFMs learn shared representations or alternative coordinate systems.

entry.title: SWIFT-Cell: Segmentation Without Iterative Flow Tracking

author.name: Devansh Lalwani, Swapnil Bhat, Muralikrishna H H, Anand Reddy, Maulik Shah

entry.summary: Distills Cellpose-SAM into SWIFT-Cell, a 0.63M-parameter U-Net trained only on CPSAM masks from 1,202 H&E and IHC tiles, achieving seconds-scale interactive cell segmentation that the 58-303 second teacher cannot deliver. Runs 2.0-5.2 s per 8192x8192 region on 4 CPU cores, 2.5-5.1x faster than QuPath's watershed detector while approaching generalist accuracy.

entry.title: Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection

author.name: Arda Baris Basaran, Mesut Ceylan, Elgar Fleisch, Filipe Barata

entry.summary: Analyzes what fixed text anchor pairs contribute to few- and full-shot vision-language anomaly detectors, separating semantic content, effective scale, and joint anchor geometry. The finding is that a single anchor pair contributes only through effective scale, as a trained adapter collapses the score to the anchor difference.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Imbalance in Class Incremental Surgical Instrument Segmentation

author.name: Shifang Zhao, Long Bai, Kun Yuan, Feng Li, Jieming Yu, Wenzhen Dong, Guankun Wang, Mobarakol Islam, Nicolas Padoy, Nassir Navab, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: The paper addresses catastrophic forgetting and segmentation-head bias in class incremental surgical instrument segmentation, analyzing two forms of data imbalance: between old and new data and within a single time point. It proposes methods to mitigate imbalance-driven bias in continual learning for surgical scenarios, with a strong multi-institution author team.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Relay Thinking

author.name: Xu Liu, Jungang Qiao, Guikun Chen, Xiaojuan Qi, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a relay thinking topology for multi-agent collaboration in which reasoning ownership dynamically transfers across agents, allowing each to inherit and refine an evolving reasoning trajectory. Its MACR framework uses confidence-guided relay triggering and a bidding mechanism to decide when to relay and which agent continues.

entry.title: Matching Particle-Arrival Rates for Low-Count Image Denoising

author.name: Huazhen Liu, Zipei Yan, Jizhou Li

entry.summary: Introduces PARM, a self-supervised denoising framework that models particle accumulation over exposure as a Poisson counting process and identifies the particle-arrival-rate field as the posterior mean of the latent clean rate. This targets microscopy settings with signal-dependent Poisson shot noise and no paired clean/noisy data.

entry.title: Valid Early Detection of Memorization in Diffusion Models

author.name: Yixiao Jing, Chia-Yu Hsu, Milad Hoseinpour, Zekai Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose prompt-free memorization detection for diffusion models by combining split conformal calibration with sequential monitoring across denoising timesteps, comparing per-step Bonferroni calibration against direct trajectory-level calibration of maximum memorization scores. This addresses false-alarm control when tests are repeated along the denoising trajectory. It matters for auditing generative models for training-data leakage with statistical guarantees.

entry.title: Correct Answers, Closed Gates: SolveBind for GUI Agents at the Verification Barrier

author.name: Xinhao Song, Haoxuan Peng, Su Su, Hongliang Wu, Sirui Song, Gongshen Liu, Linfeng Zhang, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies protected GUI environments where CAPTCHAs and anti-automation systems judge behavioral signals like trajectories and timing, not just task outcomes. SolveBind combines hierarchical solving (Perceive, Ground, Solve, Act, Verify) with runtime supervision to convert correct solver outputs into accepted interactions under time constraints. The framing of a verification barrier distinct from task-solving capability is a novel lens on GUI-agent reliability.

entry.title: DealsFlow: An Evidence-Gated Agentic Harness for Venture Capital Deal Triage

author.name: Ming Ze Tang, David Cutting, Boyd Carson, Vasiliki Carson

entry.summary: Presents DealsFlow, a deployed human-in-the-loop agentic system at a UK early-stage fund that prevents LLM score inflation when triaging startup pitch decks. It combines evidence-cited category ratings with mechanisms that can only lower scores, including corroboration ceilings and a skeptic call, evaluated on 243 SEIS/EIS investments.

entry.title: LLaCO: Continuous Diffusion for Large Language Models with Competition-Aware Semantic Scheduling

author.name: Zijian Jia, Peixuan Zhang, Genying Li, Di Wu, Yujie Fu, Si Li, Boxin Shi, Shuchen Weng

entry.summary: Studies continuous diffusion as a non-autoregressive text generation paradigm, identifying that embedding norm decay causes Euclidean distance to produce spurious token overtaking and temporal compression. It formalizes pairwise token dynamics as Competition Threshold Theory and builds a scheduler aware of directional token competition.

entry.title: Validating the Comparison, Not Just the Scorer: Why Overall Accuracy Can Mislead in Interactive LLM Evaluation

author.name: Ancil Crayton

entry.summary: This paper argues that validating an automatic LLM judge with a single overall accuracy or F1 score can hide prompt-specific scorer errors that distort measured differences between prompting conditions, potentially reversing conclusions. It proposes methods for auditing comparisons rather than just scorers.

entry.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation

author.name: Yuanzhe Peng, Jie Xu

entry.summary: The paper formulates indoor radio map estimation as a collaborative in-context learning problem and proposes Poly-Ripple, where multiple clients use large autoregressive vision models without weight updates, prompting each with private demonstrations. This avoids costly labeled data and accommodates privacy constraints on building layouts.

entry.title: Rethinking Multi-View Fusion for Urban Representation Learning

author.name: Sean Bin Yang, Zongyi Xu, Jilin Hu, Ying Sun, Kristian Torp, Bin Yang, Torben Bach Pedersen, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: The paper identifies two structural failures in urban region representation learning: modality utility varies across regions, and multi-objective training suffers persistent gradient imbalance. It proposes an adaptive approach to multi-view fusion that addresses these issues, with implications for downstream tasks like crime forecasting and service demand estimation.

entry.title: TTT in VLA Models: Exploring Training with Human Demonstrations

author.name: Qiangong Zhou, Jiafeng Liang, Yimin Dong, Yang He, Hongxiang Li

entry.summary: The authors integrate Test-Time Training (fast-weight context memory) into InternVLA-A1 and Pi0.5 and train on paired human demonstrations and robot trajectories, studying memory transfer, truncated backpropagation, objectives, and gradient coverage. Notably, adding TTT and paired-data training at the current scale did not yield consistent demonstration-conditioned target selection, and the paper reports these negative results.

entry.title: Anti-coherence Regularized Absolute Scaling for Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Donghwan Kim, Youngwoong Jin, Hyunsoo Yoon

entry.summary: Fixes a degeneracy in the SCALE post-hoc OOD detection method, whose percentile-based magnitude ratio is ill-defined when negative activations cause cancellation, and which fails on backbones like ViT. The Absolute Fix computes ratios over absolute-valued activations, and Anti-coherence regularization further refines scaling, improving training-data-free OOD detection.

entry.title: Complementing DINO Features with Image Structure for Part Discovery

author.name: Samyak Rawlekar, Nikhil Chowdary Paleti, Amey Gupta, Narendra Ahuja

entry.summary: Analyzes why DINO-based training-free part discovery produces imprecise boundaries, attributing it to the rigid ViT patch grid where boundary-straddling patches yield higher-entropy, lower-confidence features. The paper proposes complementing DINO features with image structure to sharpen part boundaries, validated with experiments on over 26K foreground patches.

entry.title: PASTA: Prompt-Aware Annealed Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Ren Ajiki, Ryugo Morita, Stanislav Frolov, Brian Bernhard Moser, Ko Watanabe, Riku Takahashi, Andreas Dengel, Jinjia Zhou

entry.summary: PASTA is a training-free framework for text-to-image diffusion that strictly preserves designated clean regions (for headlines, logos, UI elements) during generation. It uses prompt-aware shared-latent annealed sampling to avoid the flat regions and style inconsistencies produced by prior attention-manipulation or noise-level intervention methods. This matters for real-world design and editing workflows.

entry.title: Internal Discrepancy for Contrastive Learning: Generalization Bounds and Downstream Behaviors

author.name: Jialiang Wang, Qing Ma, Xiong Zhou, Gangfeng Hu, Haoliang Li, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces internal discrepancy, a measure quantifying the difference between the mean representation of positive samples and latent cluster centers, and proves a generalization bound for downstream supervised tasks after contrastive learning without additional assumptions. The theory both explains prior empirical observations and suggests practical ways to improve contrastive learning. This adds theoretical rigor to the understanding of contrastive representation learning.

entry.title: AI Alignment for Digital Democracy: Fairer Voters Representation against LLM Biases

author.name: Yi Qi, Srijoni Majumdar, Evangelos Pournaras

entry.summary: This work examines demographic biases in LLM-emulated electorates, testing how faithfully closed- and open-source LLMs reproduce individual votes across three U.S. presidential elections and whether some demographic groups are represented less accurately. It studies whether alignment techniques can reduce these representation disparities without degrading overall accuracy. The topic is timely as AI voter emulation enters digital democracy platforms.

entry.title: Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Model Inference via Per-Query Modality Selection

author.name: Shuqi Liu, Yuzhou Cao, Luke Ong

entry.summary: The paper observes that the accuracy benefit of extra modalities varies per query in omni-modal LLMs, and formulates per-query modality selection as an accuracy-cost optimization solved with a cost-sensitive learning approach while keeping the model fixed. Evaluation on WorldSense with Qwen2.5-Omni shows meaningful inference savings. This is a practical efficiency lever as omni-modal models proliferate.

entry.title: Sharp Bounds on the Winner's Bias under Independent and Nonnegatively Correlated Noise

author.name: Ivan Viakhirev, Kirill Borodin, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: This arXiv paper resolves sharp constants bounding the winner's curse — the upward bias that arises when selecting the maximum of M noisy scores — filling the gap between the previously known extreme cases of arbitrary dependence and i.i.d. noise. The authors derive exact constants for independent but non-identically distributed noise and for pairwise nonnegatively correlated noise, provide finite constructions attaining the bounds, and apply the results to sharply bound the bias of cross-validation estimators.

entry.title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning

author.name: Akila Ayanthi, Darshana Priyasad, Tharindu Fernando, Sridha Sridharan, Clinton Fookes, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: REDAR frames the selection of regularization strength in class-incremental learning as a sequential decision problem, training a lightweight RL agent to set per-phase distillation coefficients based on performance metrics and incoming data statistics. This replaces fixed, offline-tuned coefficients that ignore phase-specific variation in data volume, task difficulty, and class similarity.

entry.title: EVOLVE: Uncertainty-Aware Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Prediction with Adaptive Prototype Memories

author.name: Jianxin Jin, Kai Zhao, Shiyan Hu, Yang Shu, Peng Chen, Meng Wang, Zhongwen Rao, Yijie Li, Jing Wang, Bin Yang, Chenjuan Guo

entry.summary: EVOLVE improves unsupervised multivariate time series anomaly prediction by replacing shared, random perturbations with variable- and context-dependent perturbations, recognizing that the same perturbation can be amplified or absorbed depending on context. Adaptive prototype memories and uncertainty estimates provide early-warning signals for proactive intervention.

entry.title: Amortized Thompson Sampling and Efficient Information-Directed Sampling for Simulator-Based Design

author.name: Michal Kobiela, Michael U. Gutmann

entry.summary: The authors amortize Thompson sampling ahead of data collection for simulator-based experimental design, so that an approximation of the full Thompson sampling distribution is immediately available once observations arrive, avoiding costly per-step optimization especially in continuous action spaces. The approach is extended to efficient information-directed sampling.

entry.title: CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning

author.name: Arundhati S. Shanbhag, Brian B. Moser, Federico Raue, Tobias C. Nauen, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: CARES is a computationally lightweight continual learning replay buffer method that selects exemplars using class-aware, density-weighted coverage of a frozen pretrained feature space, avoiding costly gradient-based coreset optimization. It is reported to be 2.3 to 8.8 times faster than prior coreset methods on Tiny-ImageNet while performing well under imbalanced and noisy streams.

entry.title: Combinatorial Characterizations of the Learnability of Conditional Distributions

author.name: Mihir Dhanakshirur, Ambuj Tewari

entry.summary: This paper characterizes PAC-learnability of function classes mapping inputs to distributions over finite spaces, introducing the fat-gamma Natarajan dimension and proving its finiteness at every positive scale is necessary and sufficient for learnability under bounded proper losses. It also introduces a fat-gamma Graph dimension and establishes comparison inequalities.

entry.title: NUViT: Vision Transformers for Fourier Space Data

author.name: Jeffrey Gu, Robert C. Heeter, Ellen D. Zhong

entry.summary: NUViT redesigns ViT tokenization, data representation, and positional encoding so the architecture respects the frequency and phase structure of Fourier-space data, which standard Cartesian patch tokenization handles poorly. It shows gains across Fourier-domain classification, crystal lattice identification, and MRI annotation tasks.

entry.title: Do Halting Heads Really Save Compute in Looped Language Models?

author.name: Tsung-Han Wu, Minsuk Heo, Kenny Tan

entry.summary: Pretraining looped language models from scratch up to 1.3B parameters, the authors show halting heads suffer two problems: mixed-iteration training mispredicts stopping points, and reported compute savings may be overstated under standard stopping rules. Scoring every iteration fixes prediction only with a strong early-stop penalty, questioning common claims about adaptive-compute savings.

entry.title: On the Limits of Stochastic Push-Pull over Time-Varying Digraphs

author.name: Feiming Wang, Yutong He, Sulaiman Alghunaim, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: This theory paper constructs counterexamples showing that stochastic Push-Pull, which achieves linear speedup on static strongly connected digraphs, can fail to attain linear speedup over time-varying networks. It identifies an effective node count governing convergence and proves matching upper and lower bounds of order Theta(1/sqrt(n_eff * T)). This clarifies fundamental limits of decentralized optimization over dynamic topologies.

entry.title: ARENA: Active Region attENtion Aggregation for interpretable solar flare prediction

author.name: Luis Bauer, Annalena Kofler, Andr\'es Asensio Ramos, Aparna Venkataramanasastry, Valent\'in Mart\'inez Pillet, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: ARENA predicts solar flares from a variable number of active-region cutouts using multiple-instance learning under weak supervision, requiring only flare/no-flare labels. Its attention mechanism localizes the active region driving a prediction without explicit origin annotations, aiding interpretable space-weather forecasting. This addresses a genuinely useful operational problem with a well-suited learning setup.

entry.title: Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding for Mixed Natural Language and Structured Symbolic Corpora

author.name: Pietro Di Nicco, Lucio La Cava, Andrea Tagarelli

entry.summary: The paper identifies limitations of standard Byte Pair Encoding, which treats whitespace as a fixed semantic boundary and performs poorly on multiword expressions and formal languages like LaTeX. It proposes Adaptive Frequency Threshold BPE, which adapts merging behavior to token length and the needs of underrepresented domain-specific languages, improving tokenization of mixed natural language and symbolic corpora.

entry.title: Parametric Session States Recover Retrieval Intent without Replaying History

author.name: Qingsen Ma, Dianyun Wang, Jiahong Liu, Irwin King

entry.summary: The paper introduces Parametric Session States, which encode conversational history into parameters so long-running assistants can resolve underspecified follow-up queries (e.g., referring to a previous configuration) without replaying full history or maintaining explicit textual memory. This bridges the gap between costly long-context replay and RAG approaches that assume information-sufficient queries.

entry.title: Perturbation-Based Data Selection for Medical Question Answering

author.name: Yuexin Wu, Dayou Yu, Vasile Rus

entry.summary: Proposes Representation-Sensitivity Prioritization (RSP), selecting compact fine-tuning subsets for medical QA using prediction-change frequency and margin contraction under Gaussian perturbations of representations. Evaluated with MedGemma-4B across five medical QA datasets at small data budgets.

entry.title: When the Weakest Language Keeps Moving: ARMOR-DP for Multilingual BabyLM

author.name: Hanyu Liao, Yijing Chen, Tao Ji

entry.summary: Presents ARMOR-DP, a modular framework for multilingual BabyLM training that dynamically updates language sampling proportions using per-language validation loss rather than fixed ratios. Reveals that equal character budgets create representation artifacts for Chinese and that static protection can shift imbalance to other languages.

entry.title: Words Are the Voice of the Mind: Depression Severity Estimation from Social Traces via Mental-Guided Evidence Reasoning

author.name: Nada Xu, Xueqin Chen, Qiang Gao, Hongru Liang, Wenqiang Lei

entry.summary: Proposes UMer, a framework for estimating depression severity from social media traces using user-specific mental priors, diversified semantic retrieval, and fine-grained reasoning over mental evidence, moving beyond classification and LLM questionnaire simulation.

entry.title: Gender Associations in LLM-Mediated ADHD Self-Diagnosis

author.name: Matilde Elene Hansen, Ross Deans Kristensen-McLachlan

entry.summary: This study adapts the Context Association Test to examine whether GPT-4o (an existing, widely deployed model) responds to gendered associations in zero-shot ADHD self-diagnosis settings. Explicit gender cues amplify certain ADHD subtype associations while implicit cues yield near proxy-aligned distributions, suggesting explicit demographic cues may trigger over-correcting bias-mitigation mechanisms. The findings matter for equitable deployment of LLMs in health contexts.

entry.title: "High-Quality" Data for Early-Stage Instruction Tuning: An Empirical Study of Data Quality Metrics

author.name: Vladimir Necula, David Gvadzabia, Sofia Serrano

entry.summary: This empirical study operationalizes data quality for instruction tuning by testing which simple example-level metrics best predict training utility under fixed fine-tuning budgets. Each metric bins examples into low/mid/high quality, trains separate models, and compares validation perplexity and LLM-judge scores as a function of training tokens. The key result is that answer-dense supervision (response ratio) is a stronger, more portable predictor than other popular quality metrics.

entry.title: Xing USP: A Cross-Family Semantic Contract for Information Extraction and Intent-Slot Parsing

author.name: Zhongqiu Li, Boyang Wang, Ruiyu Fang, Shiquan Wang, Di Wu, Jiayi Liang, Feilong Zhang, Hongfeng Du, Xiaomeng Huang, Mengjiao Bao, Luwen Pu, Xuewei He, Yu Zhao, Chao Wang, Kaidong Yu, Bingkai Yang, Qingjun Zhu, Shaoyi Du, Shuangyong Song, Yongxiang Li

entry.summary: USP defines a cross-family semantic contract covering categories, fields, values, and instance associations across NER, relation extraction, event extraction, and intent-slot parsing, paired with five diagnostic matching views that expose errors current category-level metrics miss, such as wrong instance bindings or slot values.

entry.title: RubriX: A Fast, Fine-Tunable Non-Autoregressive Rubric Judge

author.name: Balamurugan Paramasivam (CobuildX), Sudalai Rajkumar (CobuildX)

entry.summary: Presents RubriX, a contrastive-language-model-inspired rubric judge that embeds responses and rubric level descriptions with a LoRA-adapted encoder and scores levels via cosine-similarity softmax, avoiding generative LLM-judge calls. It achieves 75.4% exact accuracy on held-out rubrics, beating TypeSafe's Jev (57.1%) and a Qwen3-8B judge (49.8%), with cost scaling independent of rubric length. Practical for cheap, scalable rubric-based evaluation.

entry.title: Quality over Quantity: Rethinking Data and Model Assumptions for Bengali Coreference Resolution

author.name: Zenith Biswas, Andrew Thomas Dyer

entry.summary: Evaluates transformer models for Bengali coreference resolution across zero-shot, fine-tuning, data augmentation, and cross-lingual transfer settings, showing that a small amount of high-quality annotated data significantly outperforms larger mixed-quality datasets. The results challenge common assumptions about multilingual generalization and data efficiency in low-resource NLP for a language of over 250 million speakers. Useful guidance for low-resource annotation investment.

entry.title: A Contextual Measure of Ambiguity in Prescriptive Text

author.name: Sally Dong, Luke Thorburn, Andrew Konya, Michiel Bakker

entry.summary: The authors propose quantifying ambiguity in prescriptive texts like laws and contracts as disagreement among simulated stakeholders about how policies apply in concrete scenarios, capturing contextual interpretation rather than isolated text perception. This measure aims to predict real-world outcomes such as adaptive flexibility versus arbitrary discretion.

entry.title: Veracity labels flip the emotional tone of language models but leave racial disparities intact

author.name: Nouar AlDahoul, Myles Joshua Toledo Tan, Yasir Zaki

entry.summary: Audits four LLMs (GPT-5.4 mini, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano, Llama 4 Scout, Claude Haiku 4.5) rating simulated affect for fact-checked true and false headlines across 12 personas varying race, gender, and age. Finds veracity labels strongly shift emotional tone but racial disparities in framing persist regardless, indicating fact correction does not fix identity-biased framing.

entry.title: Meta-CLIP: Metadata-Conditioned Contrastive Learning for Zero-Shot Disease Inference

author.name: Haozhe Luo, Nirosh Sivanesan, Shelley Zixin Shu, Francesco Nitti, Mauricio Reyes

entry.summary: Meta-CLIP improves medical vision-language pretraining by conditioning contrastive learning on DICOM acquisition metadata, using a kernel over acquisition fields to reweight cross-modal negatives. This emphasizes distinctions among studies with similar imaging conditions, improving transfer across scanners and protocols for zero-shot disease inference.

entry.title: Humans in Space: Can MLLMs Construct Human-Centric Spatial Understanding via Active Exocentric Exploration?

author.name: Tianchen Guo, Tengyue Zhang, Chen Liu, Ling Chen, Xin Yu

entry.summary: SATE-Bench is an interactive benchmark of 316 real-world scenes and 2,525 multi-turn QA pairs evaluating visual self-awareness and active exocentric exploration, where models start from a heavily occluded view and must iteratively query adjacent viewpoints to gather geometric evidence. It contrasts passive multi-view control with active exploration settings.

entry.title: CRIM: Composable and Reusable Item Memory for Efficient Personalized Retrieval

author.name: Haolin Li, Haipeng Zhang, Mang Li, Zhaohui Xia, Xun Zhu, Miao Li, Yu Zhang, Ji Wu
