entry.summary: CRIM separates item-level semantic encoding from request-level history modeling for personalized search and recommendation, compressing each item into compact learnable summary tokens that are user- and query-independent and thus reusable across requests. Segment-level readout tokens add predictive supervision, and inference composes cached item memories to avoid repeatedly feeding item text to the LLM.

entry.title: GMoE-FTI: A Universal Facial Template Inversion Method Adopting Genuine Mixture-of-Experts Mechanism

author.name: Zixuan Shen, Zhihua Xia, Kaikai Gan, Peipeng Yu

entry.summary: GMoE-FTI is a universal facial template inversion method that reconstructs identity-consistent faces from templates across five categories of template distributions, using a genuine mixture-of-experts mechanism. It highlights a serious biometric privacy threat: systems storing templates instead of raw images remain vulnerable to inversion from unseen template types.

entry.title: VLMProbe: An Open-source Library for VLM Probing and Interpretation

author.name: Gexin Huang, Haisheng Fu, Yanting Yang, Chen Zhao, Ruinan Jin, Jiaqi Liu, Xiaoxiao Li

entry.summary: Presents vlmprobe, an open-source library unifying lens readouts, attention attribution, causal interventions, and sparse autoencoder analysis under a common interface for probing vision-language models. Shared adapters, calibration utilities, and evaluation pipelines enable cross-architecture comparisons, with matched case studies showing that readout and spatial explanations depend on the analysis objective.

entry.title: Learning Pathology-Sensitive Representations for Unsupervised Retinal OCT Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tania Haghighi, Sina Gholami, Behafarin Emam, Jennifer I Lim, Theodore Leng, Atalie C Thompson, Hamed Tabkhi, Minhaj Nur Alam

entry.summary: Introduces an unsupervised framework for retinal OCT anomaly detection and localization that adapts pretrained visual foundation model representations to normal retinal anatomy via anatomy-aware reconstruction and contrastive triplet learning with synthetic structural perturbations, requiring no disease-specific annotations. This enables detection of rare or previously unseen pathologies beyond fixed disease categories.

entry.title: Tight Learned Event-Inertial Odometry (TLEIO): a Transformer-Based Architecture for End-to-End Motion from Event Streams

author.name: Matteo Cascone, David Jensen, Alessandro Pirini, Angelo Stefanini, Pietro Ven\`e, Marta Tintor\'e Gazulla, Javier Hidalgo Carri\`o

entry.summary: TLEIO is a compact filter-based odometry pipeline that learns short-window relative motion directly from voxelized event streams via an EventsFormer front-end and tightly fuses learned constraints with IMU propagation. It avoids feature tracking and optimization-heavy backends that undermine event sensing efficiency. This advances robot state estimation under fast motion and challenging illumination using neuromorphic sensors.

entry.title: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement

author.name: Zekai Zhang, Yanran Zhang, Shengming Yin, Yan Shu, Zhening Liu, Bingxuan Zhao, Chenyang Zhu, Donghao Zhou, Jiahao Li, Jiahao Wang, Jie Zhang, Kaiyuan Gao, Kun Yan, Lihan Jiang, Ningyuan Tang, Qihang Ai, Rui Song, Shuo Cao, Xiao Xu, Xiaoyue Chen, Yuxiang Chen, Zhendong Wang, Zhouyang Li, Zihao Liu, Zikai Zhou, Bo Zheng, Huishuai Zhang, Dongyan Zhao, Chenfei Wu

entry.summary: Qwen-Image-PE is a prompt-enhancement model that turns underspecified text-to-image requests into coherent visual specifications, trained in two stages: supervised fine-tuning with Caption-Based Reverse Distillation and reinforcement learning with a Groupwise Design Reward refining lighting, composition, layout, and detail. It evaluates on Qwen-Image-Bench with fine-grained design dimensions. The work makes prompt enhancement a first-class learned component of the T2I pipeline.

entry.title: UltraFlash: Accelerating Megapixel Visual Synthesis

author.name: Phuc Lai, Anh Nguyen, Phong Nguyen, Anh Tran

entry.summary: UltraFlash identifies the repeated VAE encode-decode transitions (pixel-space transitions) in cascade diffusion pipelines as an underexplored bottleneck for megapixel image synthesis, beyond the usual denoising cost focus. It accelerates latent diffusion generation at extreme resolutions. This is relevant to practical deployment of high-resolution generative models.

entry.title: FreeView: Robust 3D Reconstruction from Uncurated Views

author.name: Junho Kim, Hyunyoung Choi, Seongwon Lee

entry.summary: FreeView is a training-free framework for robust 3D reconstruction from uncurated image collections that jointly selects a filtering reference via collection-level consensus and rejects distractor views. It removes the dependency of prior reference-conditioned filtering on a curated clean reference. This makes feed-forward reconstruction practical for real internet photo collections.

entry.title: Late Breaking Results: Audio-Language-Action Models with Direct Speech Conditioning for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Enfu Nan, Pu Zhao, Yixiao Chen, Lin Zhao, Juyi Lin, Chen Wang, Weiwei Chen, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Speech-pi0.5 maps raw speech directly to robot motor commands built on the existing pi0.5 VLA model, using cross-modal projection of voice frames into audio tokens to avoid ASR latency and error propagation, with split LoRA adapters and two-stage training. Removing the transcription step makes natural spoken robot instruction-following more responsive. Timely direction as VLA models move toward natural interaction.

entry.title: Learning the Autoregressive: Direct Score-Difference Estimation with Amortized Future Credit for Video Distillation

author.name: Zixuan Duan, Yabo Chen, Xunzhi Xiang, Xin Zhang, Haibin Huang, Yin Chen, Chi Zhang, Qi Fan

entry.summary: Leta is a few-step distillation framework for autoregressive video generation that introduces ScoreDelta, which directly estimates teacher-student corrections from score differences, and FutureCredit, which amortizes credit assignment across future chunks to overcome detached-history training limitations. This improves on distribution matching distillation pipelines for AR video models.

entry.title: StickFigure: Enabling Pose-Only IoT Cameras for Privacy-Preserving Edge Vision

author.name: Aveline Xiaoyuan Han, Chenshu Wu

entry.summary: StickFigure is a system for IoT cameras that keeps raw RGB frames local and ephemeral, exporting only compact skeleton pose streams sufficient for downstream human activity recognition. The authors introduce an activation-aware pose backend and other co-designs to make on-device pose estimation feasible on severely resource-constrained cameras. The result is privacy-preserving sensing for assisted-living and activity-aware environments.

entry.title: MuSTEL: A Large-Scale Multilingual Synthetic Text-Line Image Dataset for OCR

author.name: Majid Adibian, Hossein Saberi, Hossein Zeinali

entry.summary: MuSTEL is a large-scale synthetic multilingual OCR dataset with over 14.5 million annotated text-line images, targeting the underexplored combination of Persian, Arabic, and English with mixed writing directions, fonts, and styles within single lines. It includes predefined training and test partitions generated from natural-language corpora.

entry.title: CrossPair: Unlocking Generalist Visual Transformation Learning in Image Editors

author.name: Yibo Zhao, Lifan Jiang, Senlin cheng, Tianrun Wu, Bolei Xu, Xiaobo Li, Can Ye, Xiaofei He, Dehai Zhao, Boxi Wu

entry.summary: CrossPair adapts a pretrained multimodal image editor to learn diverse visual transformations (restoration, editing, stylization) from a single before-after exemplar pair, rather than requiring separate specialized systems. It uses fixed roles for exemplar-before, exemplar-after, and query images across VLM and VAE pathways, with a training-only change-aware DINOv3 objective that aligns feature-change directions across content-distinct scenes. This enables task switching by demonstration, analogous to how language models learn from examples.

entry.title: No Cones, No Duals: A Fast and Scalable Solver for NRSfM

author.name: Suryansh Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes a fast solver for non-rigid structure from motion that eliminates costly semidefinite programming cone solvers and ADMM used in shape-space factorization methods. A differentiable Euclidean correction directly optimizes small rotation factors, enabling scaling to long sequences and dense point tracks.

entry.title: Factorized Gradients for Scalable Highly-expressive Parametric Diffeomorphisms

author.name: Amit Aflalo, Eran Treister, Chaim Baskin, Oren Freifeld

entry.summary: The paper develops factorized gradient techniques to make CPAB (continuous piecewise-affine based) diffeomorphic transformations more scalable and expressive, exploiting the fact that parameter dimension depends on tessellation fineness rather than data resolution. This enables highly expressive, topology-preserving deformations for scientific and vision applications.

entry.title: LayoutMamba: Efficient Document Layout Analysis with Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Networks

author.name: Kehua Chen, Mingyi Chen

entry.summary: LayoutMamba combines sparse-attention Transformers for local feature extraction with Mamba state-space modeling for linear-complexity long-range dependencies across the document canvas, in a two-stage paradigm for document layout analysis. It aims to resolve the trade-off between quadratic-cost Transformers and detail-poor state-space models in resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: Revealing Imaging Characteristics of Thermal Wakes from Underwater Vehicles Without Cooling-Water Discharge

author.name: Guoyi Zhang, Yanjin Du, Guangsheng Xu, Zhengyao Zhao, Siyang Chen, Jingjing Gao, Yuezheng Zhou, Yiyang Wu, Bin Wu, Tongsu Zhang, Lejia Ye, Donghe Wang, Jie Wang, Kaiye Hu, Zhipeng Ren, Han Wang, Boo Cheong Khoo, Xiangpeng Xu, Xiaohu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents AVP-IR-Wake, the first large-scale real-world benchmark (161,485 frames over three years) of infrared thermal wakes from small underwater vehicles, showing wakes are extended structures of discrete vortices that violate compactness assumptions of common detection methods. It addresses maritime security threats from small uncrewed vehicles that evade sonar and magnetic detection.

entry.title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yan Wang, Jiangyong Huang, Baoxiong Jia, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: MemVLN is a streaming episodic memory framework for vision-language navigation that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and relative poses, producing compact memory tokens via cross-attention. Training uses a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, paired with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder.

entry.title: OVM-Occ: Open-Vocabulary Monocular Occupancy Prediction via Geometry-Aware Vision-Language Distillation

author.name: Shuyang Yu, Haibo Qin, Shaohan Hu, Wei Shan, Xiaoqing Guan, You Wang, Guang Li

entry.summary: Presents OVM-Occ, a Gaussian-based framework for open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction in indoor scenes, using language-embedded Gaussians as the scene representation and an instance-aware vision-language teacher. A geometry-aware deformable attention module refines Gaussian semantic features to generalize beyond predefined categories.

entry.title: Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark: A mechanically annotated dataset for evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction

author.name: \'I\~nigo Cirauqui-Viloria (Universidad de Zaragoza)

entry.summary: Introduces a synthetic benchmark of 5,580 RGB images for evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction, generated with an open-source toolkit called LumenMorph. The dataset provides ground truth for camera motion, surface deformation, depth, deformation fields, and persistent material correspondences across multiple scene families and camera conditions.

entry.title: Beyond Visible Speakers: Context-Aware Active Speaker Detection with Speaker Registration

author.name: Pu Wang, Hugo Van hamme

entry.summary: Extends active speaker detection with contextual reasoning across simultaneously visible candidates and registered-speaker representations from enrollment speech, enabling detection even when a speaker is not visually observed. ROAM-ASD-C achieves state-of-the-art performance across five ASD benchmarks.

entry.title: Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters

author.name: Muhammad Saeed, Fatema Al Hajri, Mohamed H. Alhosani, Dmitry Mikhaylov, Yasser F. Al Wahedi

entry.summary: Benchmarks empirical, machine-learning (LightGBM), and deep-learning (U-Net ensemble) approaches for satellite-derived bathymetry in turbid Arabian Gulf waters against 285,619 multibeam soundings across six port areas, using rigorous leakage-free spatial validation. Notably, the validation design changed results more than model choice.

entry.title: DecoyCount: Evaluating Visual-Reasoning Misalignment in Counting

author.name: Qiuyi (Richard), Zhang, Zhen Xu, Jing Gu, Seojin Bang, Arnav Mohanty Das, Yaning Hu, Gautam Kumar, Jared Lichtarge, Le Xue, Bettina Catoto, Akul Datta, Daniel Luo, Farha Khan, Marcella Valentine, Yinfei Yang, Andrew M. Dai

entry.summary: Introduces DecoyCount, a benchmark of 1,660 real-world images with decoys across seven mechanisms and paired prompts that separate perception failures from reasoning failures in visual counting. It reveals a reasoning-alignment gap: models can execute correct counting when cue-guided but fail to select the right process unaided.

entry.title: TRON: Transferring Naturally Evolved Network Architectures into Neuroevolution

author.name: Konstantinos Zacharopoulos, Alexandra Bekou, Jose M Serradell, Foteini Paraskevopoulou, Apostolos Fournaris, Ioannis Arapakis, Oscar Lao

entry.summary: TRON is a neuroevolution framework that uses experimentally characterized protein-protein interaction networks as architectural priors for neural architecture search, instead of random initial topologies. By reusing biological interaction patterns as structural building blocks, it aims to preserve functional organization under mutation and recombination and improve evolvability.

entry.title: Causal-based approaches to explain and learn from self-extension - A review

author.name: Rebeca Marfil, Pablo Bustos, Antonio Bandera

entry.summary: A review of causal reasoning approaches enabling robots to internalize why perceptions and actions occur, arguing that deep learning alone cannot bridge the gap between reactive behavior and genuine understanding. It surveys work on self-extension, explanation, and learning grounded in causal models to improve reliability and trustworthiness.

entry.title: AdaDexTrack: Dynamic Modulation for Adaptive and Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation Tracking

author.name: Jianibieke Adalibieke, Qianwei Han, Xueyi Liu, Yuzhe Qin, Li Yi

entry.summary: Proposes a modulator-in-the-loop framework for language-conditioned dexterous manipulation tracking, where a distilled generalist tracker is dynamically corrected via reference modulation, object-latent adaptation, and positional-target adjustment. This prevents small errors from snowballing in long-horizon, contact-rich hand-object interactions.

entry.title: Networked Humanoid Intelligence: Communication, Coordination, Collaboration, and Social Interaction

author.name: Loc X. Nguyen, Huy Q. Le, Ji Su Yoon, Nguyen H. Tran, Eui-Nam Huh, Choong Seon Hong

entry.summary: This survey frames networked humanoid intelligence through four functions of information exchange: communication, coordination, collaboration, and social intelligence, connected via a common factory scenario. It reviews literature across these axes and identifies open questions as humanoids move from laboratory platforms to connected fleets. The framing is timely given accelerating humanoid deployments.

entry.title: Learning Direct Control from Optimization for Dynamic Target Tracking

author.name: Bing Sun, Yue Lin, Canhui Wen, Xin Chen, Yang Liu, Dong Wang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: LECO transfers tracking optimization into offline learning of a direct-control policy by predicting control sequences and mapping them to trajectories through a differentiable kinematic model, letting trajectory-level objectives guide control learning without repeated online numerical solving. A decaying expert-guidance curriculum initializes tracking behavior and progressively shifts toward learned autonomy. It combines the expressiveness of optimization objectives with the speed of neural policies.

entry.title: Reward-Guided RRT* for Budgeted Task and Motion Planning

author.name: Vin\'icius Ara\'ujo de Oliveira, Gabriel Ferreira Mendes Louren\c{c}o, Paulo L. J. Drews-Jr, Armando Alves Neto, Douglas G. Macharet

entry.summary: The paper proposes Reward-Guided RRT*, a sampling-based framework that jointly performs task-site selection and motion planning under a travel budget, working directly in continuous state space without a precomputed task-transition graph. A return-feasibility check ensures each selected task keeps the mission within budget. Experiments across varying obstacle complexity show competitive solutions.

entry.title: SPECOLA: A Tool for Specification Driven Robot Evaluation

author.name: Immanuel Ampomah Mensah, Hadas Kress-Gazit

entry.summary: Specola is a tool that uses Signal Temporal Logic monitors in simulation to evaluate robot behavior beyond binary success rate, capturing margins of success, sensitivity to goal parameters, specification violations, and persistence of success. It handles the engineering of exposing simulator state and mapping it to specification-relevant signals. This improves the rigor of robotics benchmarking infrastructure.

entry.title: Kernelised covariance matrices, dimension reduction and imbalanced spectral clustering

author.name: Xiaoyu Dong, Subhro Ghosh, Soumendu Sundar Mukherjee, Himasish Talukdar

entry.summary: Investigates kernelised covariance matrices using truncation kernels with pairwise separation constraints as an alternative to PCA for dimension reduction and spectral clustering of Gaussian mixture data. The approach, motivated by statistical mechanics of repulsive particle systems, is particularly effective for severely imbalanced clusters where PCA-based methods degrade.

entry.title: Macro Mondrian Conformal Risk Control

author.name: Julien Combes (SVH, Michelin), Jean-Francois Coeurjolly (SVH), Alexandre Dervill{\'e} (Michelin)

entry.summary: The authors extend Conformal Risk Control to provide group-wise (rather than only marginal) risk guarantees by combining Mondrian conformal prediction with macro-coverage, targeting high-dimensional tasks like semantic segmentation where rare-object regions can be underprotected. Applied work from Michelin researchers with a practical orientation.

entry.title: When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?

author.name: Peyman Morteza, Stephen Wright

entry.summary: The paper characterizes when Nesterov accelerated-gradient trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, showing equivalence to nonnegativity of an associated Schrödinger operator and proving that among power objectives the property holds exactly when the exponent equals four. The exceptional exponent is connected to stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.

entry.title: Synthetic Data Augmentation for Functional Data: Wasserstein Risk Bounds and Diffusion-Based Conditional Generation

author.name: Yuhao Qi, Wenlin Dai, Xuehu Zhu

entry.summary: This paper develops theory for synthetic data augmentation with functional (curve) data using a class-conditional diffusion generator, giving Wasserstein-1 risk bounds that compare training on synthetic plus real curves to training on real curves alone. It derives the optimal number of synthetic samples and conditions under which synthetic data beat real data, including allocation under class imbalance. Useful guidance for small-sample functional data problems.

entry.title: Prior Predictive Matching for Bayesian LoRA

author.name: Tomasz Ku\'smierczyk, Eliezer de Souza da Silva, Marcin Sendera

entry.summary: This paper addresses prior hyperparameter selection for Bayesian LoRA fine-tuning by introducing a closed-form prior-predictive estimator computable before fine-tuning. Using a second-order expansion, the authors quantify how the low-rank prior drives function-space deviations from pretrained outputs and show prior-predictive quantities depend on the prior only through rank times the fourth power of the prior scale. This makes uncertainty-aware LoRA more practical for foundation model adaptation.

entry.title: A Descriptive Framework for Large Agent Systems (v0.1)

author.name: Stephen Elliott

entry.summary: A working paper proposing a descriptive framework for characterizing large-scale multi-agent systems — swarms, agent markets, and agent societies — in terms of common design properties, aiming to identify which design features produce different safety outcomes. The author applies the framework to the Hugging Face swarm and outlines planned case studies on an agent market and an agent social media platform.

entry.title: Do Language Models Trust Their Own Justifications? A Study on Functional Consistency

author.name: Alisson Rosa Pereira, Bruno Iochins Grisci

entry.summary: Investigates whether tokens that LLM classifiers highlight as decisive in their explanations are behaviorally consistent with model predictions under targeted interventions, a property termed functional auto-consistency. The framework moves beyond judging explanation plausibility to testing whether explanations reflect actual model behavior.

entry.title: Do "True" and "False" Add Up to One? Complement Consistency in LLM-Agent Opinion Simulations

author.name: Anouar Imel, Jin Qi

entry.summary: Tests complement consistency in LLM-agent opinion simulations: rewriting a claim as its complement and replacing probability p with 1-p should yield reports summing to one if models report positions rather than surface text. Across 2,304 agent states with Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Gemma-3-4B, paired reports systematically exceed one, such as Qwen averaging 1.18, on simulated and real fact-checking claims.

entry.title: Reuse, Rewrite, or Reject: Evidence-Constrained Trace Reuse for Repeated Mobile GUI Control

author.name: Bingyu Bai, Cheng Zhang, Erhu Feng

entry.summary: The paper proposes graph-text templates for selective reuse of execution traces in mobile GUI agents, validating individual transitions against current task context and interface state rather than accepting or rejecting whole traces. This taxonomy of six variation categories and selective reuse reduces redundant LLM inference in repetitive mobile tasks.

entry.title: Searching with Sparse Histories: Cross-Task Architecture Search from Incomplete Search Logs and Zero-Cost Proxies

author.name: Yuefeng Xu, Jun Yu

entry.summary: Presents a risk-robust neural architecture search method that transfers knowledge across tasks from sparse search histories combined with zero-cost proxies, using champion-based initialization and joint pairwise-ranker pretraining. On TransNAS-Bench-101 it sharply reduces worst-case failures (worst-10% rank from 290 to 43 on one target, 465 to 45 on another) while keeping competitive average performance.

entry.title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Dianye Huang, Jiamei Guo, Yue Zhou, Mingde Li, Yi Xiong, Wei Wang, Nassir Navab, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: HAD-VLM is a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement, addressing the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token prediction by predicting caliper endpoints and lengths via a diffusion process in a shared backbone. A coordinate-length consistency mechanism and ensembling improve robustness. This is relevant to making VLMs handle continuous numeric outputs in medicine.

entry.title: CuraLoc: Repository-Level Fault Localization via Planned Code Inspection

author.name: Sangeeta Warrier, Anush Sankaran, Ryen White

entry.summary: CuraLoc restructures repository-level fault localization by having the model plan inspection in a single decision: selecting starting symbols, choosing code relationships to inspect, and forming edit hypotheses, followed by deterministic retrieval and ranking, instead of letting the LLM iteratively decide what to inspect. This reduces repeated model calls and token usage. It is relevant to cost-effective agentic software engineering.

entry.title: Recommender regret for improving regularised RL estimation with bandits and MCTS

author.name: Danilo Vucetic, Alexandre Larouche, Mohammad Pedramfar, Audrey Durand, Gauthier Gidel

entry.summary: The paper formalizes estimate generation in regularized RL as a recommendation process, defining regulariser-aware recommender regrets for bandit-based sampling and proving simple algorithms like uniform sampling can achieve lower bounds. It unifies bandit- and search-based target improvement under a recommender-MCTS framework.

entry.title: Solving and Learning Navier-Stokes Dynamics with the Neural Basis Method

author.name: Yuhe Wang, Zhu Wang, Min Wang

entry.summary: The neural basis method (NBM) tackles Navier-Stokes modeling via a representation-then-projection principle: fixed neural bases define the solution space and projection of governing equations determines coefficients, recasting operator learning as parameter-to-coefficient mapping. This addresses weaknesses of physics-informed learning where small PDE residuals do not guarantee small solution errors and scaling is poor.

entry.title: Universal neural network approximation of symmetric polyconvex energies and envelopes

author.name: Florian Gammer

entry.summary: The paper introduces symmetric polyconvex neural networks (SPCNNs) for approximating symmetric polyconvex energies in small-strain elasticity, proving that naive weight restrictions on input-convex ReLU networks fail to give universal approximation of the lifted representers. The proposed architecture achieves universal approximation while preserving the monotonicity structure needed for weak lower semicontinuity. This is a rigorous contribution to physics-informed constitutive modeling.

entry.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Bernardo Perrone Ribeiro, Erkut Akdag, Egor Bondarev

entry.summary: Flownomaly casts few-shot industrial anomaly detection as recovering the normal counterpart of a query image in frozen DINOv2 feature space using conditional flow matching. A learned velocity field transports noise toward normal features, and a single evaluation step along straight paths yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without trajectory integration.

entry.title: Task Format as a Factor in Adaptation: A Controlled Comparison of LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning for Prompt-Safety Classification

author.name: John Alderete, Srirakshith Betageri, Jennifer Flynn, Alex Greenhalgh, Josh Rubin, Yoshita Varma Annam

entry.summary: This controlled study compares LoRA and full fine-tuning for prompt-safety classification using a matched 400M encoder-decoder pair across three task formats with up to 15 seeds per cell. Full fine-tuning leads by 2-3 points at pre-specified learning rates, but the gap closes under a shared rate search; training LoRA to write a reason after its verdict closes the gap entirely, while content-free text of equal length does not. The work shows task format is an underappreciated confounder in adaptation comparisons.

entry.title: When the Persona Contradicts the Line: Diagnosing Plan-to-Synthesis Failures in Chain-of-Thought TTS

author.name: Joonyong Park, Jerry Li

entry.summary: Introduces a bilingual Japanese-English benchmark pairing lines with congruent and conflicting personas to diagnose where expressive intent is lost in chain-of-thought TTS pipelines. Findings show planner outputs are usually direction-correct while downstream components (emotion vector generation and rendering) lose fidelity, and bypassing QwenEmotion yields only modest gains. Useful for building more faithful expressive speech synthesis systems.

entry.title: Lessons from Luck: Do LLM-Written Lessons Carry Chance into an Agent's Next Decision?

author.name: Kazuki Nakayashiki

entry.summary: A registered study across 256 synthetic worlds measuring whether lessons written from noisy run outcomes carry chance into later decisions, using scripted runs with two tools of known reliability and ReasoningBank memory-writing instructions. Quantifies how a single outcome-fluke lesson shifts a fresh session's subsequent tool choice.

entry.title: Dynamic Query as Budgeting for Tiny Object Detection

author.name: Yi Zhang, Di Xiong, Ge Gao, Xiangyue Zhang, Yihang Qiu, Yuxuan Zhou, Shuo Chen

entry.summary: This paper disentangles the two effects hidden in DETR dynamic query mechanisms for tiny object detection, showing that dynamic queries primarily act as capacity budgeting according to object density rather than sophisticated query selection. It formalizes a monotonic, conservative budgeting principle and proposes BUTR, a streamlined detector that removes learned predictors and heuristic filtering. The conceptual clarification could simplify future detector design.

entry.title: BoundedGS: Memory-Efficient High-Resolution Training for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Xiaobin Deng, Changyu Diao, Min Li, Duanqing Xu

entry.summary: BoundedGS makes high-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting training memory-efficient by separating rasterization and projection backward passes and bounding the active local rasterization working set, releasing per-region caches after their gradient contributions are collected. Additional components address view-level memory peaks and CPU-assisted structure rebuilding.

entry.title: RacerGS: Residual-Autoregressive Context for 3D Gaussian Splatting Compression

author.name: Wenqing Wang, Huimin Zeng, Yun Fu

entry.summary: RacerGS is a compression framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting that drastically reduces storage while preserving rendering fidelity for novel-view synthesis. It uses a hash projection model to produce compact, spatially coherent context features and a FiLM-modulated autoregressive GRU context model that exploits causal dependencies among anchor feature groups to refine entropy-model parameters and improve bitrate efficiency. This addresses 3DGS's large parameter footprint, a key barrier to storage and transmission.

entry.title: Task Relevance-Driven Prompt Expansion for Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Jiahua Dong, Wenqi Liang, Yang Cong, Yichen Li, Hongyuan Yu, Henghui Ding, Yulun Zhang, Salman Khan, Fahad Shahbaz Khan

entry.summary: TRPE addresses federated continual learning without prior knowledge of new task arrival times or category counts, using an out-of-distribution-style task detection mechanism. It also exploits positive inter-task semantic relationships while filtering irrelevant old-task relationships via task relevance-driven prompt expansion to reduce catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Towards Spatio-Temporal Intelligence Systems in Urban Space: A Twin-Agent Perspective

author.name: Zhen Dong, Haiping Wang, Wei Tu, Yuan Liu, Bing Wang, Xuan Sun, Jinzhou Cao, Ronald Clark, Zhiheng Fu, Mohammed Bennamoun, Danfeng Hong, Yuanzheng Cui, Gemine Vivone, Pedram Ghamisi, Bisheng Yang, Qingquan Li, Deren Li

entry.summary: This is a system-level survey proposing urban Spatio-Temporal Intelligence (STI) systems that integrate digital twinning and agentic AI for city governance, covering monitoring, analysis, intervention planning, and feedback adaptation. It organizes disparate techniques under a twin-agent framework spanning infrastructure, mobility, environment, and emergency response.

entry.title: Fed-MAPTrack: Federated Modality-aware Prompt Tuning for RGB-X Tracking

author.name: Xiangyu Liu, Yijie Shen, Yue Yin, Zhitong Yin, Yongqi Pan, Wentao Fan

entry.summary: Fed-MAPTrack is a federated prompt-tuning framework for multi-modal object tracking that keeps raw videos local while handling heterogeneity between RGB-only clients and sensor-equipped (thermal, depth, event) clients. Clients optimize and exchange modality-aware prompts over a frozen pretrained tracking backbone, addressing the mismatch between parameter-sharing domains and contributing clients.

entry.title: Reading the Registers of Honorius III without Manual Line Transcription: Forced-Aligned HTR, End to End, Modular or Hybrid

author.name: Tamas Kovacs, Daniel Luger

entry.summary: The paper shows that existing line-break-free expert transcriptions (edition drafts) suffice to train end-to-end handwritten text recognition that jointly transcribes and expands heavily abbreviated Latin, applied to Pope Honorius III's registers. Forced alignment on 860 entries across 394 pages bootstraps 13,122 training lines without manual line alignment, substantially improving on the 18.9% CER CATMuS baseline in this domain.

entry.title: CVTSplat: Multi-view Reconstruction Using an Adaptive Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation

author.name: Briac Toussaint, Diego Thomas, Jean-S\'ebastien Franco, Edmond Boyer, Christian Theobalt

entry.summary: Explores adaptive centroidal Voronoi tessellations (CVTs) for multi-view shape and appearance reconstruction, modulating cell size by an evolving signed distance field so sites concentrate near the surface zero level set. The regularity of CVT cells enables specialized GPU algorithms for nearest-neighbor queries, making repeated re-tiling during optimization efficient.

entry.title: Seeing Through Distractions: Context-Stable Attribution via the Least Core

author.name: Sai Ganesh Nagarajan, Toshinori Yamauchi, Hiroshi Kera

entry.summary: Formalizes contextual distractors in feature attribution and analyzes them via semivalues and the least core, deriving gap bounds under weak monotonicity assumptions. Shows that shifting semivalue weights toward larger contexts reduces attribution instability, validated on image classification and saliency benchmarks.

entry.title: SCET-CBF: Speed-Calibrated Soft Guidance for One-Step Dynamic Navigation

author.name: Xiaoyu Han (University College London), Dongkun Han (The Chinese University of Hong Kong)

entry.summary: Proposes a speed-calibrated soft control-barrier-function guidance law for steering-limited bicycles in dense dynamic encounters, where braking trades off reduced closing speed against slower lateral escape. A short lateral escape maneuver sets an allowable approach speed whose derivative feeds a quadratic program weighing acceleration and steering with soft penalties.

entry.title: AdaPolicy: Action-Driven Anticipatory Robot Policies via Next-Chunk Prediction

author.name: Fan Yang, Yuting Su, Chen Zhao, Fugui Fan, Peiguang Jing

entry.summary: Proposes AdaPolicy, which elicits anticipatory future-aware representations directly from the action signal via cascaded next-chunk prediction rather than explicit future-observation supervision in pixel or latent space. An online action head jointly produces the current action chunk and an evolved latent state, avoiding added architectural and computational complexity.

entry.title: Context-dependent Runtime Construction of Safe Regions of Attraction from Design-Time Identification for Multi-Candidate Simplex Architectures

author.name: Georg J\"ager, Nils-Jonathan Friedrich, Norman Seyffer, Jos\'e Cec\'ilio, Ant\'onio Casimiro

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage Region of Attraction certification procedure using contraction metrics to reduce Simplex runtime-assurance conservatism, constructing context-dependent safe regions at runtime from design-time identification for multi-candidate architectures. It targets the gap between provably stable but conservative classical control and high-performance but unverified learning-based controllers. The work contributes to making formal runtime assurance less restrictive.

entry.title: Affine-invariant Cubic Newton with Weak Learners

author.name: Nikita Zozoulenko, Daniel Falkowski, Thomas Cass, Lukas Gonon

entry.summary: Generalizes the affine-invariant cubic Newton scheme to convex optimization with weak learners, improving on gradient-regularized Newton boosting whose analysis suffered from a heavy worst-case dependence on a weak-gradient-edge parameter. Using average cosine values and directional improvements in the Hessian-induced norm, the paper achieves better global convergence rates for Newton-based boosting.

entry.title: Causal Inference in Metric Spaces via Distance Profiles

author.name: Zheye Song, Zhiheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes the profile causal effect, a metric-ball-based contrast of potential-outcome distributions that captures where and at what scale treatment shifts probability mass for object-valued outcomes such as distributions, networks, and trees. This extends causal inference beyond mean-level summaries and special geometries to general metric spaces.

entry.title: A Nonconvex Framework for Joint Sparse Sample Weighting and Parameter Estimation

author.name: Hassan Nojavan, Chul Moon, Miju Ahn

entry.summary: This paper introduces SWAPE, a framework that jointly optimizes model parameters and per-sample weights during training, supporting convex, weakly convex, and difference-of-convex losses plus weakly convex sparsity penalties on the weights. The authors solve the bivariate problem with an alternating minimization scheme using majorize-minimize approximations for each subproblem. This matters because data-quality-aware weighting can improve robustness to outliers and noisy labels.

entry.title: Minimax Rates for Conditional Generative Learning under Wasserstein Loss

author.name: Sungwon Park, Kyoung-Sook Moon, Hongjoong Kim

entry.summary: The paper derives minimax rates for conditional generative learning under integrated Wasserstein loss with Holder continuous conditional laws and unrestricted covariate distributions. The expected-loss rate matches the uniform-covariate case, while higher moments incur an additional n^{-1} contribution from unobserved covariate regions, with matching adaptive upper bounds. This clarifies where conditional generative estimation is fundamentally limited.

entry.title: WiMoT: Replay-Free Continual Wi-Fi Sensing via Moment Transport

author.name: Chunchun Yang, Yang Cao, Zhitang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a continual Wi-Fi sensing method that stores per-class feature means and covariances instead of raw channel data, addressing privacy and storage constraints. When representations drift, an affine map transports stored statistics to stay valid, combined with supervised contrastive learning and a closed-form loss to preserve separability of earlier classes.

entry.title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models for Microservice Systems

author.name: Yixiang Tang, Fagui Liu, Guoxiang Zhong, Xi Yao, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: LLMMAD is an autoregressive LLM-based framework for multimodal anomaly detection in microservice systems that preserves modality-specific characteristics and addresses the identity-shortcut problem in feature reconstruction. It aims to detect failures that propagate across services before they severely impact end-to-end behavior.

entry.title: ACVA-Bench: Beyond Prompt Following in Abstract Concept Visualization Ability for Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Mengyan Wang, Jiyuan An, Yining Liu, YaoWen Zhang, Liner Yang ang Erhong Yang

entry.summary: ACVA-Bench measures whether text-to-image models can autonomously translate abstract concepts without fixed visual referents, such as loyalty, into accurate, diverse, and distinguishable visual representations, grounded in psycholinguistic norms. It goes beyond prompt-following to probe deeper semantic understanding in T2I systems.

entry.title: MG-REPA: Multi-Granularity Representation Alignment for Generative Target Speaker Extraction

author.name: Dohwan Kim, Jung-Woo Choi

entry.summary: Proposes MG-REPA, extending representation alignment (REPA) for generative target speaker extraction by aligning diffusion transformer hidden states with an SSL teacher at both frame and utterance granularity, since frame-level alignment leaves global speaker traits implicit and utterance-level alignment leaves time-varying content implicit. The method addresses slow training convergence of generative TSE models.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Help Robotic Engineers? Lessons from Two Focus Days in Industry

author.name: Salim Fares, Steffen Herbold

entry.summary: This case study examines AI coding agents used by a small-to-medium enterprise programming industrial robots in vendor-specific languages with simulation-based visual feedback. Agents did not improve engineer productivity except for highly repetitive code generation, though results improved over time as engineers and the agent adapted to the domain. It provides rare empirical evidence on agent limits outside mainstream software stacks.

entry.title: Shared Is Not Enough: Predictor Width and Factor Readability Under Masked Latent Prediction

author.name: Nilotpal Kakati

entry.summary: Using a controlled simulator where all latent factors behind images are known, the author shows that I-JEPA's retained information about a shared factor is heavily dependent on predictor width: at ViT-B-style proportions its probe score is about 40% of SimCLR's, but widening the predictor to encoder width reverses the ordering across seeds. This clarifies an architectural confound in what masked latent prediction learns.

entry.title: Autoregressive Physics-Informed Neural Operator Surrogates and Joint 4-D Seismic-Production Bayesian History Matching

author.name: Clement Etienam, David Blom, Hari Pattathil, Tsubasa Onishi, Harpreet Sethi, Lalson Vincent, Suraj Pawar, Kishan Ramesh Kumar, Pandu Devarakota, Faruk O. Alpak

entry.summary: The paper presents a surrogate-accelerated Bayesian history-matching framework for reservoir modeling, replacing the forward map with a physics-informed Fourier neural operator trained in a closed loop, and assimilating production data with 4-D seismic using adaptive regularized ensemble Kalman inversion. It is demonstrated on a realistic synthetic model with over 100,000 cells.

entry.title: Exact Global Minimax Risk near Nonidentification

author.name: Kaiyue Yang, Yunan Wu

entry.summary: This theory paper gives sufficient conditions under which the largest critical-path minimax risk equals the exact asymptotic minimax risk over the full parameter space in models with higher-order profile expansions where a nuisance parameter is unidentified on a submodel. It constructs an estimator attaining the leading constant uniformly, with the constant expressed via a bounded-normal decision problem. This advances statistical decision theory near nonidentification boundaries.

entry.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary

author.name: Dario Bocchi, Matteo Negri, Flavio Nicoletti, Francesco D'Amico

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a solvable minimal model - the token perceptron, a linear predictor over embedded tokens with per-position weight matrices - using the replica method to compute generalization error in the teacher-student setting with finite embedding dimension and vocabulary size. This connects classification geometry induced by embeddings to learnability in language-model-like settings. It offers theoretical insight into how embedding and vocabulary structure shape generalization.

entry.title: AdaptTok-Indic: Script-Aware Adaptive Tokenization for Indic Languages

author.name: Binayak Mukherjeea, Moitreya Nandi, Arindam Panja

entry.summary: AdaptTok-Indic extends adaptive tokenization for Indic languages with Unicode-normalized preprocessing, explicit conjunct handling, script-aware routing, and learned byte-level boundary prediction trained jointly with a small Transformer LM. Across Bengali, Hindi, Gujarati, Tamil, and Telugu it achieves lower token fertility than SentencePiece BPE and MAGNET-style baselines, reducing script-based tokenization disparity.

entry.title: MARC: Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction for Articulated Object Code Generation

author.name: Xiong Yang, Junkun Hao, Zijian Xiao, Zipeng Ye, Yuchen Xie, Ran Yi

entry.summary: MARC generates articulated objects from images and text using a shared executable kinematic graph across program construction, motion solving, and correction, representing loop closures and joint-coordinate couplings. A numerical solver computes follower motion from prescribed driver inputs and attributes errors to specific connections, enabling mechanism-aware reflective correction of closed-chain and coupled mechanisms.

entry.title: KINESYS: Test-Time Adaptation for Reference-Based Effect Editing in Images

author.name: Noah Frahm, Luchao Qi, Haoze Li, Dan B Goldman, Sambit Bhattacharya, Roni Sengupta

entry.summary: Introduces KINESYS, a test-time adaptation framework for effect-reference editing where a reference image demonstrates a desired visual effect and language specifies which properties to transfer. It combines reference-aware and source-aware feedback with a robust optimization approach to transfer effects while preserving source composition, addressing failures of single-pass editing methods.

entry.title: Can One Hear Geometry? Gauge-Invariant Spectral Descriptors for Text-to-B-rep Retrieval

author.name: Hongzhu Yi, Hao Liu, Tao Yu, Tiankun Yang, Yujia Yang, Zhenghao Zhang, Tianyu Zong, Zhenyu Guan, Bingkang Shi, Haopeng Jin, Yuanxiang Wang, Zhongtian Luo, Jungang Xu

entry.summary: The authors propose a text-to-B-rep retrieval framework using group actions and spectral geometric invariants to make invariance to translation, rotation, reflection, scaling, and recording conventions an explicit constraint on descriptor construction. This avoids information loss from discretizing CAD solids into point clouds or meshes. It matters for natural-language search over precise engineering geometry in CAD workflows.

entry.title: Freeze What Is Settled, Cache What Is Smooth: Spatial Freezing Keeps Step Caching in Its Low-Error Regime

author.name: Baiyan Li, Ganxuan Yang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how to split a speed-up target between region freezing and step caching in instruction-based diffusion transformer editors, showing that freezing lowers per-step cost so caching can use conservative thresholds with small error. A fitted per-step cost model predicts held-out latency with 4.0% median error and reproduces speed ceilings of re-implemented methods.

entry.title: DiffAuction: An Auction-Driven Framework for Generative Image Advertising

author.name: Yijie Su, Ruiyang Si, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: DiffAuction integrates controllable diffusion generation, click-intent evaluation, and auction design so multiple advertisers can compete for exposure within a single generated image. It contributes training-free residual share calibration for joint-attention updates, share-conditioned prompting, and an evaluator-plus-pricing mechanism for allocation outcomes.

entry.title: Uncertainty Evaluation to Support Safety of the Intended Functionality Analysis for Determining the Applicability of Performance Targets Across Triggering Conditions in ML-Based LiDAR Object Detection

author.name: Milin Patel, Rolf Jung

entry.summary: The paper presents a statistical uncertainty evaluation for SOTIF analysis under ISO 21448 for ML-based LiDAR object detection, testing whether an uncertainty rejection threshold selected on one condition transfers its performance-target guarantee to other triggering conditions. It provides a decision procedure with a stated error probability for whether the target is applicable, not applicable, or undetermined in a new condition.

entry.title: SG-Splat: Stable Geometry Learning under Pose Uncertainty for Pose-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Xiaohan Lu, Jiaqi Zhang, Weijia Jiang, Siwei Ma

entry.summary: Presents SG-Splat, a pose-free feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that improves robustness to residual pose errors in unposed input images. It decouples geometry estimation and Gaussian attribute prediction into dedicated components to stabilize learning of Gaussian primitives under pose perturbation.

entry.title: AdShot: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Video Advertisement Clipping

author.name: Wen Xie, Om Rastogi, Sai Siddhartha Vivek Dhir Rangoju, Gijs Overgoor, Yakov Bart, Sarah Ostadabbas

entry.summary: Introduces AdShot, a benchmark of 823 professionally edited ad pairs (30-second sources and 15-second edits) annotated with shot boundaries and content features, evaluating 15 MLLMs on shot selection for advertisement clipping. The task tests a specialized editorial capability not covered by general video understanding benchmarks.

entry.title: Duration-Aware World Models for Sleep Staging with Dwell-Time Constraints

author.name: Junhui Gao

entry.summary: This paper presents a world model for sleep staging in closed-loop neuromodulation, using a recurrent state-space model that learns dwell structure endogenously via duration-aware latent sampling, a survival-curve dwell prior, and transition-matrix calibration. A trajectory-level hard-constraint layer guarantees stage-specific minimum dwell times, addressing fragmentation that discriminative classifiers and hidden semi-Markov smoothing fail to eliminate.

entry.title: Quantum Closed Loop Inverse Kinematics Through Hilbert-Space Encoding of Robot Kinematics

author.name: Andrea Morghen, Pierluigi Arpenti, Roberto Schiattarella, Giovanni Acampora, Bruno Siciliano

entry.summary: Introduces a structure-preserving quantum representation of rigid-body transformations and serial-manipulator kinematics, encoding spatial directions as single-qubit Bloch-sphere states and reproducing frame transformations via quantum rotations. This enables closed-loop inverse kinematics formulated on parameterized quantum circuits.

entry.title: I Won't Know Until I Try: Interactive Information Gathering for Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Linfei Yuan, Rachel Holladay

entry.summary: Presents a TAMP framework, built on PDDLStream, that integrates task-directed interactive information gathering into interleaved planning and execution for long-horizon manipulation. The planner acts optimistically with interactive actions, verifies outcomes during execution, and replans minimally while retaining still-applicable actions.

entry.title: PushAround: Collaborative Path Clearing via Physics-Informed Hybrid Search

author.name: Zili Tang, Zongyuan Li, Zishao Qiao, Meng Guo

entry.summary: PushAround couples geometric connectivity reasoning (repeated W-clearance connectivity graph queries) with short-horizon physics simulation to generate executable plans for robot teams clearing paths among movable obstacles. Unlike prior NAMO approaches that abstract away robot dimensions, obstacle mass, and contact forces, it selects obstacles, directions, and contact strategies yielding physically feasible pushing plans. This improves the realism of multi-robot cluttered-environment navigation.

entry.title: Joint Independence Testing for Latent Position Random Graphs

author.name: Xiaoyi Wen, Zoltan Szabo

entry.summary: Develops kernel-based tests for joint independence of latent position random graphs, a widely used network model, extending reproducing kernel Hilbert space independence measures to graph-valued data. The work addresses computational aspects tied to Gram matrices and convergence rates for measuring independence among multiple random graph objects.

entry.title: Identities, Not Pairs: Distribution-Free False-Accept Control for Embedding-Based Verification

author.name: Salim Khazem

entry.summary: The paper shows that calibrating false-accept thresholds on impostor pairs is limited by hub identities, proving worst-case bounds on what calibration alone can guarantee, and proposes COVE, which ranks the trial pair among all pairs formed by augmenting calibration units with probe and reference. This yields distribution-free FAR control for embedding-based verification systems.

entry.title: Tradeoff-Aware Territory Design: A Multi-Objective Decision System for Enterprise Customer-to-Seller Allocation

author.name: Nan Wang, Mitchell Turiel

entry.summary: This paper presents a production decision system for customer-to-seller territory allocation in enterprise go-to-market planning. It combines a multidimensional account-value scoring layer with multi-objective optimization to balance growth, balance, capacity, and feasibility tradeoffs that are typically handled manually.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded SLM Behavioral Prediction Architecture for Future Assistance Use

author.name: Adeyemi Adeseye, Aisvarya Adeseye, Hannu Tenhunen, Jouni Isoaho

entry.summary: The paper proposes using small language models for on-device prediction of when users will seek assistance, based on pre-request changes in interaction behavior. It motivates local processing for privacy and data sovereignty in high-stakes environments and addresses the underexplored question of whether SLMs can reliably reason over low-level sequential interaction events. The architecture emphasizes evidence-grounded prediction rather than opaque inference.

entry.title: Beyond Post-Hoc Rewards: Privileged Reasoning Exploration for Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Tianyu Yang, Yijun Tian, Lars Benedikt Kaesberg, Jan Philip Wahle, Bela Gipp, Terry Ruas, Daniel Kurzawe

entry.summary: Improves multimodal embeddings by addressing how self-generated reasoning traces used to augment inputs are trained, since pairwise retrieval supervision does not directly guide the reasoning itself. The method uses privileged information to explore retrieval-relevant reasoning traces rather than optimizing reasoning conditioned on the input alone.

entry.title: LGMT: A Tool for Testing the Logical Reasoning Reliability of LLMs

author.name: Zenghui Zhou, Xiaoke Fang, Zheng Zheng

entry.summary: Presents LGMT, an open-source tool that detects LLM reasoning inconsistencies using metamorphic relations grounded in first-order logic: it generates logically equivalent follow-up cases and checks whether entailment predictions agree across pairs without ground-truth labels. It includes 20 built-in metamorphic relations for software testing use.

entry.title: An Agentic Approach with Evidence-Grounded Verification for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning in Conversation

author.name: Elyas Rashno, Farhana Zulkernine

entry.summary: The authors present an agentic framework for multimodal emotion recognition in conversations, where modality-specific perception agents post evidence-cited observations to a shared board and an integration agent produces emotion labels with supporting evidence. Built from frozen models, it avoids costly instruction tuning while enabling traceable error attribution.

entry.title: ENCL: Enabling Efficient Neuromorphic Continual Learning with Local Learning Rule and Sub-Network Freezing Strategy

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Shuochen Zhou, Hassan Raza, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: ENCL improves neuromorphic continual learning by replacing memory-hungry experience replay and global surrogate-gradient backpropagation with a lightweight local learning rule plus sub-network freezing. The goal is power- and memory-efficient continual adaptation on neuromorphic hardware.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representations for Variational Problems on Graphons

author.name: Taeyoung Kim, Jineon Baek, Joonkyung Lee, Hongseok Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a neural framework for solving variational problems over graphons (limits of dense graph sequences), which arise in extremal graph theory and large deviation theory of random graphs. Graphons are represented by implicit neural networks with a multi-scale sinusoidal residual architecture and optimized by gradient descent. This connects deep learning tooling to classical combinatorics questions.

entry.title: AutoMIL: Automated Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification

author.name: Jonas Waibel, Frank Kramer, Dominik M\"uller

entry.summary: AutoMIL is an open-source AutoML framework that automates preprocessing, training, and evaluation for multiple instance learning on whole-slide pathology images. It achieves competitive ROC-AUC on UBC-OCEAN, PCam, and a TCGA-NSCLC subset with default settings. The framework reduces the expertise barrier for computational pathology pipelines and shows ensembling helps mainly on imbalanced data.

entry.title: InferSlice: A Reference Architecture for SLO-driven LLM Inference over a Telco Wide-Area Network

author.name: Juan Parra-Ullauri, Anthony Chiu, Hari Madhukumar, Zhaozhou Wu, Anderson Bravalheri, Alex Healing, Andy Corston-Petrie, Dimitra Simeonidou, Nektaria Efthymiou

entry.summary: InferSlice presents a reference architecture for SLO-driven LLM inference distributed across telco infrastructure, integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving, and observability. It targets sovereignty, compliance, latency, and locality constraints that limit centralized cloud deployments. The work addresses the gap between datacenter-designed serving frameworks and geographically distributed heterogeneous resources.

entry.title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control

author.name: Ash Simmons, George De Ath, Richard M. Everson

entry.summary: The authors propose training human-teaming agents against simulated partners whose diversity arises from procedurally imposed cognitive constraints from human physiology literature, such as reaction delays and perceptual limits, rather than reward shaping or population checkpoints. In a modified Lunar Lander, these partners appear more human-like and support zero-shot coordination. This offers a cheap alternative to live human feedback for human-AI teaming.

entry.title: Topological Equivalence of Spectral and Density Cluster Hierarchies

author.name: Sajjad Hashemian

entry.summary: The paper proves conditions under which a spectral clustering hierarchy from diffusion distances is topologically equivalent to the density cluster tree from superlevel sets, up to monotone rescaling. It extends this equivalence to k-NN graph implementations, providing a finite-sample bridge between spectral methods and density-level-set topology.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy AI-Enabled Emergency Medical Dispatch: Uncertainty-Aware Ambulance Travel Time Estimation

author.name: Muhammad Adil Abid, Johan Holmgren, Fabian Lorig, Jesper Petersson

entry.summary: The paper proposes uncertainty-aware estimation of ambulance travel times for emergency medical dispatch, addressing the limitation that point predictions convey no reliability information in safety-critical dispatch decisions. It accounts for domain shifts in real-world trip logs to produce estimates with calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: Beyond Heuristics and Commercial Navigation: An AI-Augmented Decision-Support for Ambulance Travel Time Estimation

author.name: Muhammad Adil Abid, Johan Holmgren, Fabian Lorig, Jesper Petersson

entry.summary: Using historical ambulance trips from Sweden's Skane region, the paper shows that common heuristics (e.g., ambulances traveling a fixed percentage faster than cars) poorly capture real travel-time variation by hour, day, priority, and origin-destination. It builds an AI-augmented decision-support system replacing static lookup tables with data-driven estimation.

entry.title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation for Interpretable fMRI-based Autism Diagnosis

author.name: Yifan Qiao, Sheng Li

entry.summary: CFBrainAug unifies data augmentation and counterfactual explanation for rs-fMRI autism diagnosis by learning label-altered brain networks: it retrieves a label-opposite, topologically similar candidate and refines it under a module-number constraint. Joint training on factual and counterfactual networks reduces overfitting on limited data and improves clinical interpretability.

entry.title: When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference?

author.name: Oleg Smirnov, Sofiane Ennadir, John Pertoft, Bjartur Hjaltason, Sara Karimi

entry.summary: The paper formalizes 'predictive headroom' — the one-step predictive information a context encoder can add under randomized dynamics — and analyzes when domain-randomization benchmarks actually test context inference in world models. It shows randomization can leave little informative signal, distinguishing query coverage effects from context-weight changes in discrete and continuous environments.

entry.title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning

author.name: C\'ecile Luc, Nathana\"el Lemonnier, Ievgen Redko

entry.summary: The paper models cumulative carbon costs of time series foundation models versus periodically retrained supervised models across a deployment lifecycle, finding Chronos-2 amortizes pretraining within months for large deployments but not small ones. It also shows gradient-free pruning removing a single encoder block can reduce TSFM cost where that matters.

entry.title: Conditional Flow Models for Offline Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hao Cheng, Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Chen Zhong

entry.summary: The paper proposes estimating the optimal soft action-value function in offline maximum entropy RL by separately modeling the unknown reward distribution and transition kernel with conditional diffusion models based on probability flow ODEs, then using the resulting distributional estimators in a Bellman-style update. This decouples environment modeling from value function learning.

entry.title: GeoLEON-CLIP: Graph-Anchored Multimodal Contrastive Learning for Geographic Region Representation

author.name: Radoslaw Malek, Szymon Soltysiak, Aleksandra Kawala-Sterniuk, Piotr Szymanski

entry.summary: GeoLEON-CLIP aligns three views of geographic regions - OpenStreetMap graph embeddings, satellite imagery, and text descriptions - using a tri-modal contrastive objective anchored on frozen pretrained LEON graph embeddings. This underexploited use of structured map data yields richer geographic region representations than prior image-text or image-location contrastive methods. It is relevant for geospatial downstream tasks like urban analysis and retrieval.

entry.title: Score-Preserving Continual Lasso under Task Shift

author.name: Jingyi Guo, Runze Li, Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: The paper proposes score-preserving continual Lasso (SP-CL) for continual learning in high-dimensional sparse regression, separating sparse estimation from state transmission to avoid propagating earlier shrinkage bias. Under squared loss, the cumulative estimator exactly recovers a full-history Lasso minimizer. This is a clean theoretical solution to catastrophic forgetting in a well-defined setting.

entry.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox

author.name: Federico Lucca

entry.summary: The paper presents Foyer, a self-hosted personal email agent in daily use, and a rigorous measurement protocol featuring frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, and human labels to obtain ground truth before training. Comparing nine systems on 739 real Italian/English emails, it evaluates keyword rules, TF-IDF baselines, typed decision models, and an LLM for inbox routing decisions.

entry.title: SUDO: From Scientific Publications to Global Scholarly Discourse

author.name: Nipun D. Pathirage, Henrique Santos, Deborah L. McGuinness

entry.summary: SUDO, the Scholarly Upper Discourse Ontology, defines how papers construct and communicate knowledge, addressing the limitation that existing scholarly knowledge graphs pre-specify extraction targets as either concept-centric entities or statement-centric sentences. The ontology aims to capture discourse-level structure, supporting literature search, scientific discovery, and agent-assisted research.

entry.title: Preference Optimization Improves Definition Generation: Semantic Change in EU Institutional Sustainable Finance Disclosures

author.name: Mariia Fedorova, Andrey Kutuzov, Gustavo Cadenas Delascio

entry.summary: Shows that DPO fine-tuning reduces overly granular sense distributions in dictionary-style definition generators used for lexical semantic change detection, validated on an academic benchmark and a real EU sustainable finance terminology audit. Models, code, and predictions are publicly released.

entry.title: Incremental Predictive Value of LLM Tutoring Interactions for Student Performance

author.name: Zeyu Dong, Mikael Kwame Kuada, Asa Holley Buchakjian-Tweedy, Ibrahem Aljabea

entry.summary: Evaluates whether interaction features from an LLM tutor (16,851 exchanges in an undergraduate AI course) improve assignment-score prediction, finding gradient boosting achieves only a small, statistically marginal improvement over median baselines (MAE 3.023 vs 3.138). The bootstrap interval nearly includes zero.

entry.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition

author.name: Zefang Liu, Chenyang Zhu, Sangwoo Cho, Xujun Peng, Rongqing Huang, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Sambit Sahu

entry.summary: RoleHear extends cache-aware streaming speech recognition transducers to emit speaker-role labels inline via lightweight in-vocabulary role tokens, unifying transcription and role attribution in a single model. An offline teacher provides pseudo-labels for semi-supervised training, addressing the scarcity of role-labeled streaming data. This targets real-time applications like customer-service analytics.

entry.title: HerHealthGPT: An Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI System for Women's Reproductive Health Copy title

author.name: Hassan Saeed Hassan Albattra, Mazen Mohammed Bahgat, Rahatara Ferdousi, Hana Essam Sayed Ahmed Amrya, Mariam Mousa

entry.summary: HerHealthGPT is a conversational AI system for women's reproductive health that combines retrieval-augmented generation, context-aware clarification, and source validation in an interactive web interface. Instead of answering incomplete health queries directly, the system asks targeted follow-up questions, checks for premature conclusions, and grounds its responses in verifiable evidence. This addresses a real safety problem where health chatbots give guidance without gathering essential context.

entry.title: Does the Voynich Manuscript Mean Anything? Calibrated Tests Find Little Trace of Language

author.name: Xin Zhang, Victor S. Sheng

entry.summary: The study formalizes competing hypotheses about the Voynich manuscript (self-copying gibberish versus a ciphered real language) as programs fit under equal budgets, then evaluates them on held-out statistics. Key-switching ciphers and word-class encodings fit as well as the Timm-Schinner copying model, so word statistics alone cannot decide, and calibrated tests find little trace of language.

entry.title: HARP-LoRA: Hierarchy-Conditioned Rank Projection for Low-Rank Adaptation in Scientific Table Understanding

author.name: Hossein Sholehrasa, Mohammadhossein Amini, Doina Caragea, Remya Ampadi Ramachandran, Dan Wu, Zihang Shi, Zelin Li, Lindsey Hulbert, Eder Martinez, Xuan Xu, Majid Jaberi-Douraki

entry.summary: HARP-LoRA extends projected LoRA with hierarchy-conditioned rank projection to explicitly model relationships between table values and surrounding headers for scientific table understanding, targeting complex layouts like multi-level headers and merged cells in pharmacokinetics where value-context association is critical.

entry.title: FATE-5: Faithful Alignment of Trait Expression for Continuous Big Five Personality Control

author.name: Gunhee Cho, Hongyeob Kim, Yun-Gyung Cheong

entry.summary: Proposes FATE-5, a two-stage framework for continuous Big Five personality control in LLMs that first learns continuous soft-prompt representations of personality profiles and then applies preference alignment for dialogue naturalness. It aims to resolve the tradeoff between strong trait expression and natural conversation. Evaluated across three languages for customizable conversational agents.

entry.title: The Geometry of Emotion Representations Across Scale, Depth, and Instruction Tuning

author.name: Adam Hollowell

entry.summary: The study measures emotion representations (emotion geometry) across six Gemma 2 variants (2B, 9B, 27B in base and instruction-tuned forms), showing that a stable core emotion geometry persists across all models and that linear maps between models recover held-out emotions at near-perfect rank. This suggests emotion representations are structurally consistent across scale, depth, and instruction tuning, informing interpretability research.

entry.title: Understanding Jev-Style System One Models: Does Structure Reduce Selection Bias?

author.name: Mingyang Song, Mao Zheng, Zhiyuan Ma, Xinpeng Zhou

entry.summary: Systematically compares selection bias across Jev versions, twelve Jev-style reproductions, and six generative LLMs using an option-shuffling test that holds question and candidate content fixed. Addresses whether direct probabilistic decision structure actually reduces order-based selection bias in multi-option tasks.

entry.title: Whispers from the Neighbors: Rethinking Caption Consensus as Inference-Time Evidence for Vision-Language Retrieval

author.name: Khang Nhat Hoang Vo, Belal Shoer, Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri

entry.summary: This paper shows that consulting an image's neighboring captions at inference time improves text-to-image retrieval, but the magnitude depends critically on annotation provenance: gains of 3.4 to 16.8 R@1 points when captions share annotators with queries, dropping to about a point from a different annotation source. It reframes caption consensus as inference-time evidence with careful attribution of where the gains come from.

entry.title: EKT-Router: Expert-Evidence Alignment for Embodied Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weilin Ruan, Yingjie Xu, Yangkai Wei, Bohan Zhou, Shuaibo Li, Harold Haodong Chen, Kaiwen Zhou, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen, James Cheng

entry.summary: EKT-Router jointly selects a capability expert (General, Spatial Reasoning, or Spatiotemporal), optional knowledge, and perceptual tools for embodied vision-language models answering questions from partial observations. It scores complete expert-evidence routes under a call budget using outcome-derived signatures and verifies acquired evidence with a packet verifier.

entry.title: Evaluating Visual Language Models on Visual Grounding for Visually Impaired People

author.name: Fairooz Azim, Lydia Achour, Claudia Borg, Lina Rojas-Barahona

entry.summary: Evaluates open-source vision-language models on visual grounding in VQA using the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset of real images taken by visually impaired users, framing grounding as a trust and safety requirement in assistive settings. Proposes VG-SHAP, extending SHAP-based explanations to quantify grounding behavior in VLMs.

entry.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch

author.name: Callen MacPhee, Yiming Zhou, Bahram Jalali

entry.summary: MoViD is a physics-inspired motion estimation algorithm that treats video as optical time-stretch signals, drawing on principles from ultrafast photonic time-stretch acquisition to improve real-time motion detection in complex scenes. It aims to avoid the spatial-resolution sacrifices of background subtraction, frame differencing, and optical flow. The cross-disciplinary framing could influence robotics, autonomous driving, and video compression applications.

entry.title: MarineLife-16K: An Attribute-Rich Video-Text Dataset for Motion-Aware Marine Video Understanding

author.name: Quang-Trung Truong, Thanh-Nghia Nguyen, Phu-Phong Vo, Jaeyeon Kim, Cheng Chen, Jie Zhang, Binh-Son Hua, Duc Thanh Nguyen, Ivor Tsang, Sai-Kit Yeung

entry.summary: The authors introduce a marine video-text dataset with 2,000 richly annotated video-text pairs (13 attributes, up to four objects per scene) across diverse lighting, times of day, and 7 countries, from which 16,080 video-question-answer instances are generated. It targets fine-grained, motion-aware understanding of complex in-the-wild marine environments. The resource enables applications in ocean ecology monitoring and marine robotics.

entry.title: Tracking Is Not Sensing: Artifact-Aware Thermal Video Respiration Estimation in Head-Free Marmosets

author.name: Penghao Wang, Sen Yang, Fenghua Xie, He Wang, Xindong Song

entry.summary: This paper presents artifact-aware estimation of respiratory rate from thermal video in head-free marmosets, enabling noncontact physiological monitoring where weak breathing cues are corrupted by head motion and fur. It supports neuroscience research linking behavior, internal state, and neural activity without contact sensor burden. The title highlights the key insight that tracking the animal is not the same as sensing its physiology.

entry.title: Scalable Unrolled Chains for MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Emiljo M\"ehillaj, Ender Konukoglu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a memory-efficient training framework for unrolled variational networks in accelerated MRI reconstruction, updating randomly sampled cascades while propagating supervision via an activation-light backward pass. A time-conditioned shared network keeps parameter count independent of chain length. This decouples training memory from chain depth, enabling deeper unrolled architectures.

entry.title: Explaining Navigation Decisions: Stage-Aware Visual Attribution for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yiyuan Yao, Xinpeng Ding, Minglei Chen, Fei Gao, Lihuo He, Jie Yuan, Aijun Li, Nannan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: The authors identify instruction-stage insensitivity in existing explainability methods for vision-language navigation, where explanations fail to distinguish evidence across navigation stages. They propose a stage-aware attribution framework that constructs action-conditioned temporal instruction-visual attributions across historical and current observations.

entry.title: CropReward: A Human-Preference Benchmark and Reward Model for Aesthetic Image Cropping

author.name: Xiangfei Sheng, Xiaofeng Pan, Leida Li, Qian Zhang, Biao Wang, Johan Wagemans, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: This paper tackles the reliability of evaluation in aesthetic image cropping (AIC), showing that widely used geometry-based metrics like IoU and aesthetic-assessment models poorly reflect human preferences. The authors build a human-preference benchmark (CropBenchmark/CropReward) covering methods from specialized vision models to multimodal LLMs, and train a reward model aligned with human judgments. This provides a better signal both for benchmarking AIC systems and for reward-guided optimization.

entry.title: Learning Discriminative Prototypes via Boundary Repulsion MixUp for Object Re-Identification

author.name: Athena Psalta, Vasileios Tsironis, Konstantinos Karantzalos

entry.summary: PBR-ReID represents each identity with a learnable prototype optimized alongside a DINOv3 backbone, using the prototype similarity matrix to identify confusable identities. Boundary Repulsion MixUp then applies geometry-aware regularization at the hardest inter-class decision boundaries to improve re-identification embeddings.

entry.title: Recursive CLIP: Vision-Language Distillation with Looped Transformer Blocks

author.name: Szymon Mazurek, Alberto Presta, Micha{\l} Byra

entry.summary: This paper studies how far parameter sharing can be pushed in contrastive vision-language models by reusing a small set of N transformer blocks M times per forward pass, with N times M held fixed to match standard ViT-B depth. The authors introduce two families: rCLIP with a recursive vision encoder and r-squared CLIP with recurrence in both vision and text encoders, trained under direct and distillation settings. The work probes whether CLIP's transferable capabilities survive aggressive recurrence-based parameter reduction.

entry.title: Seeing Before Naming: Context-Grounded Learning of Novel Visual Concepts

author.name: Gabriel Adineera, Jinoh Kim

entry.summary: SynerNet learns novel visual concepts in pre-trained vision-language models by anchoring discriminative visual evidence to concept-specific name embeddings exposed to compatible linguistic contexts, with difficulty-aware processing and adaptive objective weighting. It reports 74.35% mean 16-shot accuracy across four VISTA-Beyond domains.

entry.title: CoDeRNet: Selective Cross-Task Routing under Heterogeneous Supervision for Change Detection and Captioning

author.name: Eunki Cho, Hyeon Bae Kim, Seong Tae Kim

entry.summary: CoDeRNet reformulates joint change detection and captioning in remote sensing as selective information routing between heterogeneous task branches, deciding when and what to communicate given differing supervision granularity. It targets uneven reliability across tasks and spatial locations that shared-representation unified models mishandle.

entry.title: DUET4D: Self-Corrective Coupled Guidance for Sparse-View 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Beizhen Zhao, Nanjie Yao, Boyi Fu, Qingsong Yan, Haofan Ren, Kaiyong Zhao, Hao Wang

entry.summary: DUET4D tackles sparse-view 4D Gaussian splatting by using a self-corrective coupled guidance framework where the 4D representation steers generative priors to produce spatio-temporally consistent supervision. It avoids redundant primitives and floating artifacts that arise from naively absorbing uncertain generative outputs into Gaussian optimization.

entry.title: Test-Time Prompt-Agnostic Decomposition

author.name: Junze Wang, Lei Fan, Dezheng Zhang, Donglin Di, Yang Song, Sidong Liu, Cong Cong

entry.summary: The paper identifies two failure modes in test-time prompt tuning (magnitude expansion and directional drift) where noisy unlabeled objectives accumulate across steps and destabilize prompt updates. It proposes Test-Time Prompt-Agnostic Decomposition (TPD), which characterizes and controls these failure modes to make test-time adaptation of large pretrained models more stable under distribution shift.

entry.title: Domain-Adapted Latent Diffusion Models for CT-to-PET Image Translation

author.name: Yann Bourd\'e, Lea Bogensperger, Arnela Hadzic, Michael Krauthammer
